async function loadProducts() {
    // Base query lifted from CustomerPriceList.jrxml (the SQL portion only —
    // it returns base prices; pricing-rule resolution happens in JS below).
    // Images live in the separate `image` table (longtext base64) and are
    // batch-loaded lazily so the main query stays small.
    //
    // De-dup note: `producttotree` is many-to-many — a product can sit in
    // multiple trees, which the LEFT JOIN would otherwise multiply into
    // duplicate rows. GROUP BY product.id + GROUP_CONCAT collapses the
    // tree assignments into a single comma-list per product.
    const rows = await qp(`
        SELECT product.id, product.num AS num, product.description,
               product.price, product.sku, product.upc,
               product.activeflag, product.taxableflag,
               product.partid AS partid,
               product.taxid AS taxratetaxid,
               product.kitflag AS kitflag,
               product.defaultsoitemtype AS defaultsoitemtype,
               taxrate.code AS taxcode, taxrate.name AS taxratename, taxrate.rate AS taxrate,
               GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT producttree.id) AS treeids,
               GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT producttree.name SEPARATOR ', ') AS treenames,
               uom.code AS uomcode, uom.name AS uomname
        FROM product
        LEFT JOIN taxrate ON product.taxid = taxrate.id
        LEFT JOIN producttotree ON product.id = producttotree.productid
        LEFT JOIN producttree ON producttotree.producttreeid = producttree.id
        LEFT JOIN uom ON product.uomid = uom.id
        WHERE product.id > 0 AND product.activeflag = 1
        GROUP BY product.id, product.num, product.description, product.price,
                 product.sku, product.upc, product.activeflag, product.taxableflag,
                 product.partid, product.kitflag, product.defaultsoitemtype,
                 product.taxid, taxrate.code, taxrate.name, taxrate.rate, uom.code, uom.name
        ORDER BY product.num
        LIMIT 10000
    `);
    _allProducts = rows.map(r => {
        const treeIds = (r.treeids ? String(r.treeids).split(',') : [])
            .map(s => parseInt(s, 10)).filter(n => !isNaN(n));
        return {
            id: r.id, num: r.num, description: r.description,
            price: parseFloat(r.price) || 0,
            sku: r.sku, upc: r.upc,
            activeFlag: r.activeflag,
            taxableFlag: r.taxableflag,
            partId: r.partid != null ? parseInt(r.partid, 10) : null,
            // Kits and drop-ship lines are rejected (422) by the REST SO create,
            // so unsupportedRestLines() screens the cart on them before submit.
            kitFlag: bitTrue(r.kitflag),
            defaultSoItemType: intOf(r.defaultsoitemtype),
            taxRate: parseFloat(r.taxrate) || 0,
            taxCode: r.taxcode || '',
            taxRateName: r.taxratename || '',
            treeIds, treeNames: r.treenames || '',
            uomCode: r.uomcode || '', uomName: r.uomname || '',
        };
    });
    // Rebuild the part-grouping index whenever the product list is
    // reloaded — UOM grouping reads from this.
    rebuildPartGroups();
    rebuildFavouriteIdSets();
}

// Pricingrule resolution — see plan §3.2. Loaded once per customer change.
async function loadActiveRulesForCustomer(customer) {
    if (!customer) { _activeRules = []; return; }
    // Pull active rules, optionally filtered by date window. Customer-scope
    // filtering happens JS-side because the enum values for customerInclTypeId
    // aren't easy to reproduce in SQL across Fishbowl versions.
    const rules = await qp(`
        SELECT id, name, isActive, isAutoApply, isTier2,
               customerInclTypeId, customerInclId,
               productInclTypeId, productInclId,
               qtyApplies, qtyMin, qtyMax,
               dateApplies, dateBegin, dateEnd,
               paTypeId, paBaseAmountTypeId, paApplies,
               paAmount, paPercent
        FROM pricingrule
        WHERE isActive = 1
          AND (dateApplies = 0
               OR (CURDATE() BETWEEN COALESCE(dateBegin, '1900-01-01') AND COALESCE(dateEnd, '2999-12-31')))
    `);
    // Resolve the customer's group memberships so group-scoped rules only
    // apply to customers actually IN that group. For type 3,
    // pricingrule.customerInclId is an accountgroup.id; membership lives
    // in accountgrouprelation keyed by the customer's accountId.
    let groupIds = new Set();
    if (customer.accountId != null) {
        try {
            const gRows = await qp(`
                SELECT groupId AS groupid
                FROM accountgrouprelation
                WHERE accountId = ${intOf(customer.accountId)}
            `);
            groupIds = new Set(gRows.map(r => intOf(r.groupid)).filter(n => n != null));
        } catch (e) {
            // On lookup failure fail CLOSED (no group rules) — applying
            // another group's pricing is worse than falling back to
            // product price / customer-specific rules.
            console.warn('Customer group lookup failed — group-scoped rules disabled for this session:', e);
        }
    }
    // Pre-filter to those that apply to this customer. Type IDs
    // (customerincltype lookup table): 1 = All · 2 = Customer · 3 = Customer Group.
    // Compare via intOf() since these columns can come back as either
    // numbers or numeric strings from JxBrowser.
    _activeRules = rules.filter(r => {
        const t = intOf(r.customerincltypeid);
        if (t === 1) return true;
        if (t === 2) return intOf(r.customerinclid) === customer.id;
        if (t === 3) return groupIds.has(intOf(r.customerinclid));
        return false;
    });
    if (DEBUG) {
        qoDebug(`Customer "${customer.name}" group membership: [${[...groupIds].join(', ') || 'none'}]`);
        console.log(`Loaded ${rules.length} active pricing rules total · ${_activeRules.length} apply to customer ${customer.name}`);
        if (_activeRules.length > 0) console.log('Sample rule:', _activeRules[0]);
    }
    // Pre-load part costs if any applicable rule bases its adjustment on
    // a cost (Average / Vendor / Last / Standard). resolvePrice() is
    // synchronous, so the cost maps must exist before the first render.
    if (_activeRules.some(r => ruleUsesCostBase(r))) await loadPartCosts();
}

// Does this rule's paBaseAmountTypeId reference a part cost?
// (1 = Average, 2 = Default Vendor's, 3 = Last, 6 = Standard, 8 = Last Mfg)
function ruleUsesCostBase(r) {
    const b = intOf(r.pabaseamounttypeid);
    return b === 1 || b === 2 || b === 3 || b === 6 || b === 8;
}

// One-shot session cache of the cost columns cost-based rules resolve
// against. partcost has at most one row per part; vendorparts can have
// several (one per vendor × UOM) — we keep the default vendor's cost
// and the most recently dated cost separately.
async function loadPartCosts() {
    if (_partCostsLoaded) return;
    _partCostsLoaded = true;
    try {
        const [costRows, vpRows] = await Promise.all([
            qp(`SELECT part.id AS partid, part.stdCost AS stdcost, partcost.avgCost AS avgcost
                FROM part
                LEFT JOIN partcost ON partcost.partId = part.id`),
            qp(`SELECT partId AS partid, lastCost AS lastcost, defaultFlag AS defaultflag, lastDate AS lastdate
                FROM vendorparts
                WHERE lastCost IS NOT NULL`),
        ]);
        for (const r of costRows) {
            const pid = intOf(r.partid);
            if (pid == null) continue;
            _partCosts.set(pid, {
                avg: r.avgcost != null ? parseFloat(r.avgcost) : null,
                std: r.stdcost != null ? parseFloat(r.stdcost) : null,
                vendor: null, last: null, _lastDate: '',
            });
        }
        for (const r of vpRows) {
            const pid = intOf(r.partid);
            if (pid == null) continue;
            let e = _partCosts.get(pid);
            if (!e) { e = { avg: null, std: null, vendor: null, last: null, _lastDate: '' }; _partCosts.set(pid, e); }
            const cost = parseFloat(r.lastcost);
            if (isNaN(cost)) continue;
            if (bitTrue(r.defaultflag) && e.vendor == null) e.vendor = cost;
            const d = r.lastdate ? String(r.lastdate) : '';
            if (e.last == null || d > e._lastDate) { e.last = cost; e._lastDate = d; }
        }
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`loadPartCosts: cached cost bases for ${_partCosts.size} parts`);
    } catch (e) {
        _partCostsLoaded = false;   // allow a retry on the next customer change
        console.warn('loadPartCosts failed:', e);
    }
}

async function loadCustomerPartsHistory(customer) {
    _customerParts = new Map();
    _customerLastPrice = new Map();
    if (!customer) return;
    // Two sources, two jobs:
    //   1. customerparts (below) — Fishbowl's own denorm of the last price
    //      charged per product. Resolved only by "Customer Last Price"-
    //      based pricing rules (never applied as an implicit fallback).
    //   2. soitem history (this query) — display data (date + qty of the
    //      last purchase) matching the Customer Purchase History report.
    // We pull every sale-type line for this customer (typeId 10 = Sale,
    // 20 = Credit Return, 30 = Misc Sale) across all non-voided SOs, then
    // group JS-side keeping the most-recent row per product.
    const cpPromise = qp(`
        SELECT productId AS productid, lastPrice AS lastprice
        FROM customerparts
        WHERE customerId = ${customer.id}
    `);
    const rows = await qp(`
        SELECT soitem.productid,
               soitem.unitprice AS lastprice,
               soitem.qtyordered AS lastqty,
               COALESCE(soitem.datelastfulfillment, so.datecreated) AS datelastpurchased,
               soitem.id AS soitemid
        FROM soitem
        INNER JOIN so ON so.id = soitem.soid
        WHERE so.customerid = ${customer.id}
          AND soitem.productid IS NOT NULL
          AND soitem.typeid IN (10, 20, 30)
          AND so.statusid NOT IN (90, 95)
        ORDER BY soitem.id DESC
        LIMIT 50000
    `);
    // Rows are id-desc, so the FIRST row encountered per productId is the
    // most recent — skip subsequent rows for the same product.
    for (const r of rows) {
        const pid = r.productid;
        if (_customerParts.has(pid)) continue;
        _customerParts.set(pid, {
            lastPrice: parseFloat(r.lastprice) || 0,
            dateLastPurchased: r.datelastpurchased,
            lastQty: parseFloat(r.lastqty) || 0,
        });
    }
    const cpRows = await cpPromise;
    for (const r of cpRows) {
        const pid = intOf(r.productid);
        const lp = parseFloat(r.lastprice);
        if (pid != null && !isNaN(lp)) _customerLastPrice.set(pid, lp);
    }
    if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`loadCustomerPartsHistory: ${_customerParts.size} soitem history rows · ${_customerLastPrice.size} customerparts last-price rows`);
}

// ── Orders view: data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Queried with SQL rather than GET /api/sales-orders. The REST search exists
// but documents no query parameters at all, so scoping, date-filtering and
// limiting would be guesswork, and every other list in this report is SQL.
// If usable parameters ever surface, only loadOrders() has to change.

// so.statusId ids that count as "open" — an order still being worked.
// Estimate (10), Issued (20), In Progress (25) only.
//
// Fulfilled (60) is NOT open: the goods have shipped and there is nothing
// left to chase, which is the whole question this view answers. It is also
// the bulk of the table — 273 of 444 rows on this database — so including it
// buried the orders that actually need attention. Closed Short (70) is
// likewise finished, just short. Voided (80), Cancelled (85), Expired (90)
// and Historical (95 — present in the data, absent from schema-index.md's
// map) are all terminal too.
//
// The status NAME still comes from the sostatus lookup table rather than a
// hardcoded map, so a customised install shows its own labels.
const SO_STATUS_OPEN = [10, 20, 25];

// The signed-in Fishbowl username, which is what so.salesman stores —
// verified: every distinct so.salesman value matches a sysuser.userName
// exactly. Each MODE keeps that identity somewhere different.
function currentFbUsername() {
    if (typeof getUser === 'function') {
        try {
            const u = JSON.parse(getUser() || '{}');
            if (u && u.userName) return String(u.userName);
        } catch (_) { /* fall through */ }
    }
    if (MODE === 'portal' && _portalActiveConn && _portalActiveConn.fbUsername) {
        return String(_portalActiveConn.fbUsername);
    }
    if (MODE === 'standalone' && _conn.username) return String(_conn.username);
    return '';
}

// CSV import bodies MUST declare UTF-8.
//
// For text/* with no charset parameter, servers fall back to ISO-8859-1 (the
// old HTTP/1.1 default, still Jetty's behaviour). fetch() always encodes the
// body as UTF-8, so every non-ASCII character was written with its UTF-8 bytes
// and read back as Latin-1 -- one character in, several out:
//
//   Pierre’s Pastry        U+2019 = UTF-8 E2 80 99
//   Pierreâ€™s Pastry      the same bytes read as Latin-1
//
// A plain ASCII apostrophe (U+0027, one byte) survives untouched, which is why
// only names carrying the CURLY apostrophe broke -- Word and Outlook
// autocorrect one into the other.
//
// Worse than a display glitch: the importer matches customers BY NAME, so a
// mangled name matched nothing and the import CREATED a customer instead of
// updating one. Every favourites save on such a customer minted a duplicate.
const CSV_CONTENT_TYPE = 'text/plain; charset=utf-8';

// CSV fields must not contain a raw newline.
//
// RFC 4180 allows one inside quotes. Fishbowl's importer does not: it splits
// the body into rows BEFORE it honours quoting, and so does our own legacy
// runApiRequest branch used to (`csvBody.split('\n')`, since removed).
// Either way one row tears into two, the second with the wrong column count,
// and the import dies with an unhandled 500 carrying no message at all.
//
// Cost a real site every favourites save on one customer while every other
// customer worked -- the difference being a two-line main-office address,
// "Australia Fair Shopping Centre\n42 Marine Parade".
//
// Collapsing to a space FLATTENS the value, and on the customer import that
// is a real data change: ImportCustomer demands the address columns on every
// update, so each save rewrites the address. Which is why _postCustomerImport
// sends JSON where it can -- JSON carries the newline intact and never reaches
// this function. Flattening is the price of the CSV fallback only.
function csvSafe(v) {
    return String(v ?? '').replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, ' ');
}

// Should the import-path prober try the NEXT candidate, or stop and report?
//
// Only on an explicit not-found. This used to also infer "wrong path" from a
// 500 whose body carried no message -- on the theory that an unresolvable
// :name answers that way and a genuine rejection always says why. The second
// half is false: an unhandled server-side exception (the newline above) gives
// exactly the same messageless 500, so the rule turned a real failure into
// four pointless retries against paths that do not exist, and reported the
// last one. A 500 means the endpoint took the request and the request failed.
function looksLikeUnresolvedImport(err) {
    // Search the message AND the object: runRestApiAsync rejects with the
    // PARSED response body, so there is no .message and String(err) is
    // "[object Object]" -- reading .message alone never saw that shape.
    if (Number(err && (err.status || err.statusCode)) === 404) return true;
    let hay = String((err && err.message) || '');
    if (err && typeof err === 'object') {
        try { hay += ' ' + JSON.stringify(err); } catch (_) { /* cyclic */ }
    }
    if (!hay.trim()) hay = String(err || '');
    // Deliberately NOT a bare /not found/ -- a row-level rejection naming a
    // missing product or address would match it and send us probing again.
    return /import not found|no such import|unknown import|\bhttp 404\b/i.test(hay);
}

// Readable text out of anything thrown or rejected. Error paths were showing
// "[object Object]" and "[500] undefined" -- a rejection carrying
// {status, detail} has no .message -- which hid the server's actual complaint
// at exactly the moment it was needed.
function errText(err) {
    if (err == null) return 'unknown error';
    if (typeof err === 'string') return err;
    const parts = [];
    if (err.status) parts.push('[' + err.status + ']');
    const body = err.message || err.detail || err.error
              || (err.response && (err.response.message || err.response.detail));
    if (body) {
        parts.push(String(body));
    } else {
        let dump = '';
        try { dump = JSON.stringify(err) || ''; } catch (_) { dump = ''; }
        const onlyStatus = dump === '{"status":' + JSON.stringify(err.status) + '}';
        if (dump && dump !== '{}' && !onlyStatus) parts.push(dump.slice(0, 300));
    }
    return parts.join(' ') || 'unknown error (no message on the response)';
}

// Escape a string for a single-quoted SQL literal. This report otherwise
// never puts free text in a query — the orders search is filtered in JS
// precisely to avoid that — but the salesman filter has to compare against
// a name. Callers ALSO restrict the value to one that came out of the
// database (see ordersSalesmanFilter), so this is the second line of
// defence rather than the only one.
function sqlStr(s) {
    return "'" + String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/'/g, "''") + "'";
}

// Resolve _ordersSalesman to a WHERE fragment, or '' for no filter.
// Returns '' (everyone) when 'me' can't be resolved to a username, rather
// than silently matching nothing.
function ordersSalesmanFilter() {
    const who = _ordersSalesman === 'me' ? currentFbUsername() : _ordersSalesman;
    if (!who) return '';
    // Only ever interpolate a name we have seen in the database, or the
    // signed-in user's own. Anything else is ignored.
    const known = _salesmen.some(s => s.userName === who) || who === currentFbUsername();
    if (!known) return '';
    return `so.salesman = ${sqlStr(who)}`;
}

// Distinct salesmen who actually have orders, most-active first. Loaded once
// per session; a name with no orders would only ever filter to an empty list.
async function loadSalesmen() {
    if (_salesmenLoaded) return;
    _salesmenLoaded = true;
    try {
        const rows = await qp(`
            SELECT so.salesman AS username, COUNT(*) AS n
            FROM so
            WHERE so.salesman IS NOT NULL AND so.salesman <> ''
            GROUP BY so.salesman
            ORDER BY n DESC
        `);
        _salesmen = rows.map(r => ({ userName: String(r.username), count: intOf(r.n) || 0 }));
    } catch (e) {
        _salesmen = [];
        _salesmenLoaded = false;   // allow a retry
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('loadSalesmen failed: ' + (e && e.message || e), 'warn');
    }
}

// Pick status names are user-facing jargon; these read better on an order.
// Ported from Dashboards/Individual Pages/Open_Sales_Orders.htm so the same
// order reads identically in both reports.
function mapPickStatusToDisplay(name) {
    if (name === 'Entered') return 'To Pick';
    if (name === 'Started') return 'Picking';
    return name;
}

// Derive the display status from pick + ship progression, falling back to the
// SO's own status when the order has not been picked yet. Ported verbatim in
// behaviour from Open_Sales_Orders.htm's calculatePickShipStatus().
//
// pickinfo / shipinfo arrive as "num:statusId:statusName|num:statusId:..."
// (verified against live data: "S455:40:Finished").
function calcOrderStatus(row) {
    const parse = s => (!s || s === 'null' ? [] : String(s).split('|').map(p => {
        const bits = p.split(':');
        return { num: bits[0], statusId: parseInt(bits[1], 10), statusName: bits[2] };
    }).filter(p => p.num && p.statusId > 0));

    const picks = parse(row.pickinfo);
    const ships = parse(row.shipinfo);
    const base  = row.statusname || 'Unknown';

    const tip = [];
    if (picks.length) { tip.push('Picks:');     picks.forEach(p => tip.push('  Pick ' + p.num + ': ' + p.statusName)); }
    if (ships.length) { tip.push('Shipments:'); ships.forEach(s => tip.push('  Ship ' + s.num + ': ' + s.statusName)); }
    const tooltip = tip.join('\n') || base;

    if (!picks.length) return { label: base, tooltip, partial: false };

    // Pick status 40 = Finished.
    if (picks.every(p => p.statusId === 40)) {
        if (ships.length) {
            const maxShip = Math.max(...ships.map(s => s.statusId));
            if (maxShip === 30) return { label: 'Shipped', tooltip, partial: false };
            if (maxShip === 20) return { label: 'Packed',  tooltip, partial: false };
            if (maxShip === 10) return { label: 'Picked',  tooltip, partial: false };
        }
        return { label: 'Picked', tooltip, partial: false };
    }

    // Otherwise the least-advanced incomplete pick is what the order is
    // actually waiting on. The asterisk flags that other picks are further
    // along, i.e. the order is only partly through.
    const incomplete = picks.filter(p => p.statusId < 40);
    if (incomplete.length) {
        const min = Math.min(...incomplete.map(p => p.statusId));
        const name = incomplete.find(p => p.statusId === min).statusName;
        const partial = picks.length > 1;
        return { label: mapPickStatusToDisplay(name) + (partial ? ' *' : ''), tooltip, partial };
    }
    return { label: base, tooltip, partial: false };
}

// CSS modifier for the status pill.
function orderStatusClass(label) {
    const k = String(label || '').replace(/\s*\*$/, '').toLowerCase();
    if (k === 'estimate')    return 'st-estimate';
    if (k === 'in progress') return 'st-inprogress';
    if (k === 'issued')      return 'st-issued';
    if (k === 'to pick')     return 'st-topick';
    if (k === 'picking')     return 'st-picking';
    if (k === 'picked')      return 'st-picked';
    if (k === 'packed')      return 'st-packed';
    if (k === 'shipped')     return 'st-shipped';
    if (k === 'fulfilled')   return 'st-fulfilled';
    if (k === 'closed short')return 'st-closed';
    if (k === 'voided' || k === 'cancelled') return 'st-void';
    if (k === 'expired')     return 'st-expired';
    return 'st-unknown';
}

async function loadOrders() {
    _ordersLoading = true;
    _ordersError = null;
    renderOrders();
    try {
        // Every interpolated value here is numeric and passed through
        // Number(), except the salesman name — which is restricted to a
        // value that came out of the database and escaped by sqlStr().
        // The free-text SEARCH is still applied client-side in
        // applyOrdersSearch() so no typed string ever reaches SQL.
        await loadSalesmen();
        const where = ['1 = 1'];
        if (_ordersScope === 'customer' && _selectedCustomer) {
            where.push(`so.customerId = ${Number(_selectedCustomer.id)}`);
        }
        if (_ordersRange > 0) {
            where.push(`so.dateCreated >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL ${Number(_ordersRange)} DAY)`);
        }
        if (_ordersStatusSet === 'open') {
            where.push(`so.statusId IN (${SO_STATUS_OPEN.map(Number).join(',')})`);
        }
        const salesmanWhere = ordersSalesmanFilter();
        if (salesmanWhere) where.push(salesmanWhere);

        const rows = await qp(`
            SELECT so.id, so.num,
                   so.statusId        AS statusid,
                   ss.name            AS statusname,
                   so.dateCreated     AS datecreated,
                   so.dateIssued      AS dateissued,
                   -- The SO's scheduled ship date. There is NO so.dateScheduled
                   -- column; dateFirstShip is the field the SO module labels
                   -- "Date Scheduled", and what the CSV's OrderDateScheduled /
                   -- the REST create's dateScheduled both land in. Same column
                   -- Open_Sales_Orders.htm shows under that name.
                   so.dateFirstShip   AS datefirstship,
                   so.customerId      AS customerid,
                   cu.name            AS customername,
                   cu.number          AS customernum,
                   so.customerPO      AS customerpo,
                   so.salesman        AS salesman,
                   so.subTotal        AS subtotal,
                   so.totalTax        AS totaltax,
                   so.totalPrice      AS totalprice,
                   lg.name            AS lgname,
                   GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN pk.num IS NOT NULL
                        THEN CONCAT(pk.num, ':', COALESCE(ps.id, 0), ':', COALESCE(ps.name, 'None')) END
                        ORDER BY pk.num SEPARATOR '|') AS pickinfo,
                   GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN sh.num IS NOT NULL
                        THEN CONCAT(sh.num, ':', COALESCE(shs.id, 0), ':', COALESCE(shs.name, 'None')) END
                        ORDER BY sh.num SEPARATOR '|') AS shipinfo
            FROM so
            LEFT JOIN customer      cu  ON cu.id  = so.customerId
            LEFT JOIN sostatus      ss  ON ss.id  = so.statusId
            LEFT JOIN locationgroup lg  ON lg.id  = so.locationGroupId
            LEFT JOIN soitem        si  ON si.soId = so.id
            LEFT JOIN pickitem      pi  ON pi.soItemId = si.id
            LEFT JOIN pick          pk  ON pk.id  = pi.pickId
            LEFT JOIN pickstatus    ps  ON ps.id  = pk.statusId
            LEFT JOIN ship          sh  ON sh.soId = so.id
            LEFT JOIN shipstatus    shs ON shs.id = sh.statusId
            WHERE ${where.join(' AND ')}
            GROUP BY so.id
            ORDER BY so.id DESC
            LIMIT ${Number(_ordersLimit)}
        `);

        _orders = rows.map(r => {
            const st = calcOrderStatus(r);
            return {
                id: intOf(r.id),
                num: String(r.num == null ? '' : r.num),
                statusId: intOf(r.statusid),
                statusName: r.statusname || '',
                statusLabel: st.label,
                statusTip: st.tooltip,
                statusClass: orderStatusClass(st.label),
                dateCreated: r.datecreated,
                dateIssued: r.dateissued,
                dateScheduled: r.datefirstship,
                customerId: intOf(r.customerid),
                customerName: r.customername || '',
                customerNum: r.customernum || '',
                customerPO: r.customerpo || '',
                salesman: r.salesman || '',
                subTotal: parseFloat(r.subtotal) || 0,
                totalTax: parseFloat(r.totaltax) || 0,
                totalPrice: parseFloat(r.totalprice) || 0,
                lgName: r.lgname || '',
            };
        });
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`loadOrders: ${_orders.length} rows (scope=${_ordersScope} range=${_ordersRange}d status=${_ordersStatusSet})`);
    } catch (e) {
        _ordersError = (e && e.message) || String(e);
        _orders = [];
        console.error('loadOrders failed:', e);
        showToast('Failed to load orders: ' + _ordersError, 'error', 6000);
    } finally {
        _ordersLoading = false;
        applyOrdersSearch();     // sets _ordersFiltered and re-renders
        renderStatusLine();
    }
}

// Line items for one order. Lazily fetched on first expand and cached — an
// order's lines don't change while the list is open.
async function loadSoLines(soId) {
    const key = Number(soId);
    if (_soLines.has(key)) return _soLines.get(key);
    const rows = await qp(`
        SELECT si.id, si.soLineItem AS solineitem, si.productNum AS productnum,
               si.description, si.qtyOrdered AS qtyordered,
               si.qtyFulfilled AS qtyfulfilled, si.qtyPicked AS qtypicked,
               si.unitPrice AS unitprice, si.totalPrice AS totalprice,
               si.statusId AS statusid, sis.name AS statusname,
               si.typeId AS typeid, sit.name AS typename,
               u.code AS uomcode
        FROM soitem si
        LEFT JOIN soitemstatus sis ON sis.id = si.statusId
        LEFT JOIN soitemtype   sit ON sit.id = si.typeId
        LEFT JOIN uom          u   ON u.id   = si.uomId
        WHERE si.soId = ${Number(soId)}
        ORDER BY si.soLineItem
    `);
    const lines = rows.map(r => ({
        id: intOf(r.id),
        line: intOf(r.solineitem),
        productNum: r.productnum || '',
        description: r.description || '',
        qtyOrdered: parseFloat(r.qtyordered) || 0,
        qtyPicked: parseFloat(r.qtypicked) || 0,
        qtyFulfilled: parseFloat(r.qtyfulfilled) || 0,
        unitPrice: parseFloat(r.unitprice) || 0,
        totalPrice: parseFloat(r.totalprice) || 0,
        statusName: r.statusname || '',
        typeId: intOf(r.typeid),
        typeName: r.typename || '',
        uomCode: r.uomcode || '',
    }));
    _soLines.set(key, lines);
    return lines;
}

// Client-side filter. Deliberately not a SQL LIKE — see loadOrders().
function applyOrdersSearch() {
    const q = (_ordersSearch || '').trim().toLowerCase();
    _ordersFiltered = !q ? _orders.slice() : _orders.filter(o =>
           o.num.toLowerCase().includes(q)
        || o.customerName.toLowerCase().includes(q)
        || o.customerNum.toLowerCase().includes(q)
        || o.customerPO.toLowerCase().includes(q)
        || o.salesman.toLowerCase().includes(q)
        || o.statusLabel.toLowerCase().includes(q));
    sortOrders();
    renderOrders();
    renderStatusLine();
}

function sortOrders() {
    const { key, dir } = _ordersSort;
    const val = o => {
        switch (key) {
            case 'so_num':      return o.num.toLowerCase();
            case 'so_status':   return o.statusLabel.toLowerCase();
            case 'so_customer': return o.customerName.toLowerCase();
            case 'so_po':       return o.customerPO.toLowerCase();
            case 'so_salesman': return o.salesman.toLowerCase();
            case 'so_issued':   return o.dateIssued || '';
            case 'so_total':    return o.totalPrice;
            // Dates sort on the PARSED value, not the raw string — a
            // pre-formatted dd/MM/yyyy string sorts by day-of-month
            // otherwise, which looks almost right and never is.
            case 'so_sched':
            default: {
                const m = parseFbDate(key === 'so_sched' ? o.dateScheduled : o.dateCreated);
                return m ? m.valueOf() : 0;
            }
        }
    };
    // Decorated sort so equal values keep their load order (id DESC).
    _ordersFiltered = _ordersFiltered
        .map((o, i) => ({ o, i, v: val(o) }))
        .sort((a, b) => (a.v < b.v ? -dir : a.v > b.v ? dir : a.i - b.i))
        .map(x => x.o);
}

// ── Pricing resolution — two-stage competition ───────────────────────
// Implementation modelled on SalesOrder/fishbowl-pricing-rules.html, which
// documents the canonical Fishbowl Advanced behaviour:
//
//   Tier 1 — Product Price
//     The base list price on the product. No rules compete here.
//
//   Tier 2 — List Price competition
//     Rules with `isTier2 = 1` compete to set the list price. Only the
//     highest-ranked rule type present competes (Customer > Customer
//     Group > Fixed > Other). Within that group, the T2 module option
//     ('low' or 'high') picks the winning candidate.
//
//   Tier 3 — Sales Price competition
//     Rules with `isTier2 = 0` then compete against the Tier 2 winner.
//     Same ranking + module-option logic. A T3 rule with base value
//     "List Price" discounts off the T2 winner. The T3 result is the
//     final sales order price.
//
// The Tier 2 winner loses its rule TYPE before entering Tier 3 — i.e. a
// Customer rule that won T2 doesn't out-rank a Customer Group rule in
// T3. We model this by running the T2/T3 competitions independently.
//
// Enum mappings below are CALIBRATED against the live lookup tables
// (patype, pabaseamounttype, customerincltype) — not guesses:
//   patype:            1 Markdown · 2 Markup · 3 Margin · 4 Percent ·
//                      5 Amount · 6 Set price
//   pabaseamounttype:  1 Average Cost · 2 Default Vendor's Cost ·
//                      3 Last Cost · 4 List Price · 5 Product Price ·
//                      6 Standard Cost · 7 Customer Last Price ·
//                      8 Last Manufactured Cost
//   customerincltype:  1 All · 2 Customer · 3 Customer Group
// Cost bases resolve through _partCosts (partcost.avgCost, part.stdCost,
// vendorparts.lastCost); "Customer Last Price" resolves through
// _customerLastPrice (the customerparts table).
//
// pricingrule columns referenced: customerInclTypeId, customerInclId,
// productInclTypeId, productInclId, isTier2, paTypeId, paBaseAmountTypeId,
// paApplies, paAmount, paPercent, qtyApplies, qtyMin, qtyMax, dateApplies,
// dateBegin, dateEnd.

function resolvePrice(product, qty) {
    if (!product) return _emptyPriceResult(0);
    const qtyN = qty > 0 ? qty : 1;
    const cacheKey = product.id + '|' + qtyN;
    // In DEBUG mode we always recompute (so the per-rule trace appears in
    // the console each time). Production short-circuits via the cache.
    if (!DEBUG && _resolvedPrices.has(cacheKey)) return _resolvedPrices.get(cacheKey);

    const productPrice = product.price;

    // Filter to rules that apply to this product+qty (customer scope is
    // already applied in _activeRules during loadActiveRulesForCustomer).
    const productMatch = _activeRules.filter(r => productMatchesRule(product, r));
    const applicable = productMatch.filter(r => qtyMatchesRule(qtyN, r));

    const t2rules = applicable.filter(r => ruleIsTier2(r));
    const t3rules = applicable.filter(r => !ruleIsTier2(r));

    if (DEBUG) {
        // Log per-rule outcome with scope IDs + computed type rank so we
        // can verify the precedence ladder (Customer > Customer Group >
        // Fixed > Other) is matching against the right enum values.
        const dump = r => {
            const mn = parseFloat(r.qtymin), mx = parseFloat(r.qtymax);
            const q = qtyMatchesRule(qtyN, r) ? '✓' : '✗';
            const tier = ruleIsTier2(r) ? 'T2' : 'T3';
            const rank = ruleTypeRank(r);
            const spec = productSpecRank(r);
            return `    ${q} ${tier}/typeRank${rank}/prodSpec${spec} "${r.name}" id=${r.id} custType=${r.customerincltypeid} prodType=${r.productincltypeid} qtyMin=${isNaN(mn)?'-':mn} qtyMax=${isNaN(mx)?'-':mx} paType=${r.patypeid} %=${r.papercent} $=${r.paamount}`;
        };
        qoDebug(`resolvePrice  ${product.num}  qty=${qtyN}  productMatches=${productMatch.length}  applicable=${applicable.length}`);
        productMatch.forEach(r => qoDebug(dump(r)));
    }

    // Stage 1: Tier 2 competition → list price
    const t2 = competeAtTier(t2rules, product, productPrice, /*listPrice*/null, _t2ModuleOpt);
    const listPrice = t2.winnerPrice != null ? t2.winnerPrice : productPrice;

    // Stage 2: Tier 3 competition → sales price (operates against the T2 winner)
    const t3 = competeAtTier(t3rules, product, productPrice, listPrice, _t3ModuleOpt);
    const salesPrice = t3.winnerPrice != null ? t3.winnerPrice : listPrice;

    // No fallback beyond the product price. The customer's last price is
    // NOT applied implicitly — it only enters pricing when a rule uses
    // the "Customer Last Price" base (paBaseAmountTypeId 7), matching
    // Fishbowl's own behaviour. No rule fired → product price.
    const rulesFired = !!(t2.winner || t3.winner);
    const finalPrice = salesPrice;
    const source = rulesFired ? 'rule' : 'product.price';

    const result = {
        price: roundCents(finalPrice),
        original: productPrice,
        listPrice: roundCents(listPrice),
        t2winner: t2.winner,
        t3winner: t3.winner,
        // `rule` kept as an array for back-compat with `priceBreakdownTooltip`
        rule: [t2.winner, t3.winner].filter(Boolean),
        source,
    };
    _resolvedPrices.set(cacheKey, result);
    return result;
}

// Run a single tier competition. Returns { winner, winnerPrice } where
// winner is the rule object that won (or null if no rule competed) and
// winnerPrice is the resulting price (or null if no rule fired).
// `product` is needed so cost / customer-last-price bases can resolve.
function competeAtTier(tierRules, product, productPrice, listPrice, moduleOpt) {
    if (!tierRules || tierRules.length === 0) return { winner: null, winnerPrice: null };

    // Within this tier, only the highest-ranked TYPE present competes.
    const ranks = tierRules.map(r => ruleTypeRank(r));
    const minRank = Math.min(...ranks);
    const candidates = tierRules.filter(r => ruleTypeRank(r) === minRank);

    // Score each candidate.
    const scored = [];
    for (const r of candidates) {
        const p = applyRuleAdjustment(r, product, productPrice, listPrice);
        if (p == null || !isFinite(p) || p < 0) continue; // unevaluable rule — skip
        scored.push({ rule: r, price: p });
    }
    if (scored.length === 0) return { winner: null, winnerPrice: null };

    // Module option picks the winner among the scored candidates.
    let winner = scored[0];
    for (const s of scored.slice(1)) {
        if (moduleOpt === 'high' ? s.price > winner.price : s.price < winner.price) winner = s;
    }
    return { winner: winner.rule, winnerPrice: winner.price };
}

function _emptyPriceResult(p) {
    return { price: p, original: p, listPrice: p, t2winner: null, t3winner: null, rule: [], source: 'none' };
}

function roundCents(n) { return Math.round((parseFloat(n) || 0) * 100) / 100; }

// ── pricingrule shape helpers ────────────────────────────────────────

function ruleIsTier2(r) { return bitTrue(r.istier2); }

// Best-effort product-scope mapping (pricingrule.productInclTypeId):
//   1 = All products
//   2 = Specific product   (productInclId = product.id)
//   3 = Product tree       (productInclId = a producttree.id)
function productMatchesRule(product, r) {
    const t = intOf(r.productincltypeid);
    const inclId = intOf(r.productinclid);
    if (t === 1) return true;
    if (t === 2) return inclId === product.id;
    if (t === 3) return inclId != null && (product.treeIds || []).includes(inclId);
    return false;
}

// Qty bracket check. Empirically `qtyApplies` is often false on rules
// that still carry meaningful qtyMin/qtyMax — Fishbowl appears to use
// those values regardless of the flag in some installs. We therefore
// enforce the bracket whenever qtyMin or qtyMax is populated, ignoring
// the qtyApplies flag.
function qtyMatchesRule(qty, r) {
    const mn = parseFloat(r.qtymin), mx = parseFloat(r.qtymax);
    const hasMin = !isNaN(mn) && mn > 0;
    const hasMax = !isNaN(mx) && mx > 0;
    if (!hasMin && !hasMax) return true;
    if (hasMin && qty < mn) return false;
    if (hasMax && qty > mx) return false;
    return true;
}

// Type-rank (per fishbowl-pricing-rules.html §2). Lower rank wins.
//   1 = Customer Rule       (customer-scope = specific customer)
//   2 = Customer Group Rule (customer-scope = group)
//   3 = Fixed Rule          (no customer scope, fixed-price adjustment)
//   4 = Other Rules         (no customer scope, anything else)
function ruleTypeRank(r) {
    const ct = intOf(r.customerincltypeid);
    if (ct === 2) return 1; // specific customer
    if (ct === 3) return 2; // customer group (best-effort enum)
    // No customer scope — distinguish fixed-price ("Fixed") from everything else ("Other").
    if (isFixedPriceAdjustment(r)) return 3;
    return 4;
}

function isFixedPriceAdjustment(r) {
    return adjustmentType(r) === 'fixed_price';
}

// Product-scope specificity (per fishbowl-pricing-rules.html TREE rule).
// Lower rank = more specific = wins ties at the same TYPE rank.
//   1 = Specific product (productInclTypeId = 2)
//   2 = Product tree     (productInclTypeId = 3)
//   3 = All products     (productInclTypeId = 1 or unknown)
function productSpecRank(r) {
    const t = intOf(r.productincltypeid);
    if (t === 2) return 1;
    if (t === 3) return 2;
    return 3;
}

// Map pricingrule.paTypeId → adjustment kind, per the `patype` lookup
// table (verified against a live install):
//   1 = Markdown · 2 = Markup · 3 = Margin · 4 = Percent ·
//   5 = Amount (± flat adjustment) · 6 = Set price (absolute)
function adjustmentType(r) {
    const t = parseInt(r.patypeid, 10);
    switch (t) {
        case 1: return 'markdown';     // base × (1 − pct)
        case 2: return 'markup';       // base × (1 + pct)
        case 3: return 'margin';       // base ÷ (1 − pct) — target margin %
        case 4: return 'percent';      // base × pct
        case 5: return 'amount';       // base + amt (amt may be negative)
        case 6: return 'fixed_price';  // amt, verbatim
        default: return 'markdown';
    }
}

// Human label for a rule's base type — used in debug logs + the price
// breakdown tooltip so mis-scoped rules are diagnosable at a glance.
const PA_BASE_NAMES = {
    1: 'Average Cost', 2: "Default Vendor's Cost", 3: 'Last Cost',
    4: 'List Price', 5: 'Product Price', 6: 'Standard Cost',
    7: 'Customer Last Price', 8: 'Last Manufactured Cost',
};
function baseTypeName(r) { return PA_BASE_NAMES[intOf(r.pabaseamounttypeid)] || 'Product Price'; }

// One-line description of what a rule does, e.g. "Markup 100% on Average
// Cost" or "Customer Last Price + $0.00". Tooltip / debug helper.
function describeRuleAdjustment(r) {
    const kind = adjustmentType(r);
    const pct = parseFloat(r.papercent);
    const amt = parseFloat(r.paamount);
    const pctS = isNaN(pct) ? '?' : ((pct * 100) % 1 ? (pct * 100).toFixed(1) : (pct * 100).toFixed(0)) + '%';
    switch (kind) {
        case 'markdown':    return `Markdown ${pctS} off ${baseTypeName(r)}`;
        case 'markup':      return `Markup ${pctS} on ${baseTypeName(r)}`;
        case 'margin':      return `Margin ${pctS} on ${baseTypeName(r)}`;
        case 'percent':     return `${pctS} of ${baseTypeName(r)}`;
        case 'amount':      return isNaN(amt) ? baseTypeName(r) : `${baseTypeName(r)} ${amt < 0 ? '−' : '+'} ${fmtMoney(Math.abs(amt))}`;
        case 'fixed_price': return isNaN(amt) ? 'Set price' : `Set price ${fmtMoney(amt)}`;
        default:            return '';
    }
}

// Resolve the base value the adjustment operates against, per the
// `pabaseamounttype` lookup table (verified against a live install):
//   1 = Average Cost            → partcost.avgCost
//   2 = Default Vendor's Cost   → vendorparts.lastCost (defaultFlag = 1)
//   3 = Last Cost               → vendorparts.lastCost (newest lastDate)
//   4 = List Price              → the Tier-2 winner (Tier 3 only)
//   5 = Product Price           → product.price (default)
//   6 = Standard Cost           → part.stdCost
//   7 = Customer Last Price     → customerparts.lastPrice
//   8 = Last Manufactured Cost  → no queryable column; unsupported
// Returns `null` when the base can't be resolved (no cost row, customer
// has never bought the product, List Price referenced from Tier 2, …) —
// the rule is then skipped rather than producing a bogus $0 price.
function adjustmentBase(r, product, productPrice, listPrice) {
    const b = intOf(r.pabaseamounttypeid);
    const costs = product && product.partId != null ? _partCosts.get(product.partId) : null;
    switch (b) {
        case 1:  return costs && costs.avg    != null ? costs.avg    : null;
        case 2:  return costs && costs.vendor != null ? costs.vendor : null;
        case 3:  return costs && costs.last   != null ? costs.last   : null;
        case 4:  return listPrice != null ? listPrice : null;
        case 6:  return costs && costs.std    != null ? costs.std    : null;
        case 7: {
            const lp = product ? _customerLastPrice.get(product.id) : null;
            return lp != null && lp > 0 ? lp : null;
        }
        case 8:  return null;
        case 5:
        default: return productPrice;
    }
}

// Apply one rule's adjustment to its base. Returns the resulting price,
// or `null` if the adjustment can't be evaluated (missing amount, or an
// unresolvable base — see adjustmentBase).
//
// IMPORTANT — `paPercent` is stored as a DECIMAL FRACTION in Fishbowl
// (0.2 means 20%, 1.0 means 100%). The reference doc's calculator uses
// `v/100` because it assumes the UI value (20) is fed in directly, but
// the underlying database value is already divided. So our formulas do
// NOT divide by 100 — `pct` is used as-is.
//
// Note: we deliberately do NOT gate on `paApplies`. Empirically that flag
// may be false on rules that still carry a usable paTypeId/paAmount —
// requiring it caused valid rules to silently no-op.
function applyRuleAdjustment(r, product, productPrice, listPrice) {
    const base = adjustmentBase(r, product, productPrice, listPrice);
    if (base == null) {
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`Rule "${r.name}" (id ${r.id}) skipped for ${product ? product.num : '?'} — base "${baseTypeName(r)}" unavailable`, 'warn');
        return null;
    }
    const kind = adjustmentType(r);
    const pct = parseFloat(r.papercent);
    const amt = parseFloat(r.paamount);

    let result;
    switch (kind) {
        case 'markdown':    result = isNaN(pct) ? null : base * (1 - pct);          break;
        case 'markup':      result = isNaN(pct) ? null : base * (1 + pct);          break;
        case 'margin':      result = isNaN(pct) ? null : (pct >= 1 ? base : base / (1 - pct)); break;
        case 'percent':     result = isNaN(pct) ? null : base * pct;                break;
        case 'amount':      result = isNaN(amt) ? null : Math.max(0, base + amt);   break;
        case 'fixed_price': result = isNaN(amt) ? null : amt;                       break;
        default:            result = null;
    }
    if (DEBUG && result == null) {
        console.warn(`Rule "${r.name}" (id ${r.id}) couldn't be evaluated:`,
                     'kind=', kind, 'paTypeId=', r.patypeid, 'paPercent=', r.papercent, 'paAmount=', r.paamount);
    }
    return result;
}

function invalidatePriceCache() { _resolvedPrices = new Map(); }

// bit(1) columns reach JS as 0/1, true/false, '1'/'0', or sometimes a
// base64-encoded single byte ("AQ=="/"AA==") depending on driver path.
// This helper accepts the union and returns a plain boolean.
function bitTrue(v) {
    if (v === 1 || v === true || v === '1') return true;
    if (typeof v === 'object' && v && v[0] === 1) return true;
    if (typeof v === 'string' && (v === 'AQ==' || v === 'true')) return true;
    return false;
}

// Tolerant integer cast — accepts numbers, numeric strings, null/undefined.
function intOf(v) {
    if (v == null) return null;
    const n = typeof v === 'number' ? v : parseInt(v, 10);
    return isNaN(n) ? null : n;
}

// ── Next-break suggestion ────────────────────────────────────────────
// Scan rules that would apply to (product, customer) at a higher qty
// than the current one. If any has a `qtyMin` greater than the current
// qty, return the lowest such break + the price that would result.
//
// Only T3 rules are considered (the final-sales-price tier). T2 breaks
// could matter too, but the savings reflected to the user come from
// the sales price, so T3 is the right surface.
function findNextBreak(product, currentQty) {
    if (!product || !_activeRules.length) return null;
    const breaks = [];
    for (const r of _activeRules) {
        if (ruleIsTier2(r)) continue;                       // T3 only
        if (!productMatchesRule(product, r)) continue;
        const mn = parseFloat(r.qtymin);
        if (isNaN(mn) || mn <= currentQty) continue;
        breaks.push(mn);
    }
    if (breaks.length === 0) return null;
    const nextQty = Math.min(...breaks);
    const projected = resolvePrice(product, nextQty);
    // Only return the suggestion if hitting the new qty actually changes
    // the price. Otherwise the tooltip / tile hint just confuses the user
    // by pointing at a "break" that isn't really a break.
    const current = resolvePrice(product, currentQty);
    if (projected.price >= current.price) return null;
    return { atQty: nextQty, price: projected.price };
}

// Open-PO summary for a product. Returns null if no opens are cached
// yet (i.e. lazy load hasn't completed for this product) so the caller
// can render a neutral placeholder. Returns an empty array when load
// completed and found no open POs.
function openPoSummary(productId) {
    const arr = _openPOs.get(productId);
    if (arr === undefined) return null;  // not yet loaded
    return arr;
}

// Render the per-product favourite-star pair. Two independent toggles:
//   - .fav-cust (green) — customer favourite, shared across all staff
//     working with the selected customer. Disabled when no customer is
//     selected (nothing to persist to).
//   - .fav-user (orange) — this rep's personal favourite.
// A product can be in NEITHER, EITHER, or BOTH sets at once — they're
// no longer mutually exclusive. toggleFavourite(pid, kind) handles each
// independently.
const _favStarSvg = `<svg stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
    <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M11.049 2.927c.3-.921 1.603-.921 1.902 0l1.519 4.674a1 1 0 00.95.69h4.915c.969 0 1.371 1.24.588 1.81l-3.976 2.888a1 1 0 00-.363 1.118l1.518 4.674c.3.922-.755 1.688-1.538 1.118l-3.976-2.888a1 1 0 00-1.176 0l-3.976 2.888c-.783.57-1.838-.196-1.538-1.118l1.518-4.674a1 1 0 00-.363-1.118l-3.976-2.888c-.783-.57-.38-1.81.588-1.81h4.914a1 1 0 00.951-.69l1.519-4.674z"></path>
</svg>`;

function _favTitle(kind, isOn, customerSelected) {
    if (kind === 'customer') {
        if (!customerSelected) return 'Select a customer first to set a customer favourite';
        return isOn ? 'Customer favourite (shared) — click to remove'
                    : 'Add to customer favourites (shared with all staff)';
    }
    return isOn ? 'Your favourite — click to remove'
                : 'Add to your favourites';
}

function favBtnHtml(productId) {
    const isCust    = _customerFavIds.has(productId);
    const isUser    = _userFavIds.has(productId);
    const canCust   = !!_selectedCustomer;
    const custCls   = 'fav-btn fav-cust' + (isCust ? ' active' : '') + (canCust ? '' : ' disabled');
    const userCls   = 'fav-btn fav-user' + (isUser ? ' active' : '');
    // The favourites display setting hides the implementation(s) the
    // org doesn't use — only render the enabled star(s).
    const custBtn = _favDisplayMode === 'user' ? '' :
        `<button class="${custCls}" data-fav-pid="${productId}" data-fav-kind="customer"
            aria-pressed="${isCust}" aria-label="Customer favourite"
            title="${_favTitle('customer', isCust, canCust)}"
            onclick="event.stopPropagation();toggleFavourite(${productId}, 'customer')">${_favStarSvg}</button>`;
    const userBtn = _favDisplayMode === 'customer' ? '' :
        `<button class="${userCls}" data-fav-pid="${productId}" data-fav-kind="user"
            aria-pressed="${isUser}" aria-label="Personal favourite"
            title="${_favTitle('user', isUser, canCust)}"
            onclick="event.stopPropagation();toggleFavourite(${productId}, 'user')">${_favStarSvg}</button>`;
    return `<span class="fav-group">${custBtn}${userBtn}</span>`;
}

// Refresh the ID-set caches from the num-set sources. Called whenever
// products reload or favourites change. Cheap — usually < 1k entries.
function rebuildFavouriteIdSets() {
    _userFavIds = new Set();
    _customerFavIds = new Set();
    if (!_allProducts.length) return;
    const byNum = new Map();
    const loadedIds = new Set();
    for (const p of _allProducts) { byNum.set(String(p.num), p.id); loadedIds.add(p.id); }
    // User favourites are stored as product NUMs → map to ids.
    for (const num of _userFavourites) {
        const id = byNum.get(String(num));
        if (id != null) _userFavIds.add(id);
    }
    // Customer favourites are stored as product IDs directly.
    for (const raw of _customerFavourites) {
        const id = intOf(raw);
        if (id != null && loadedIds.has(id)) _customerFavIds.add(id);
    }
}

// Build the part-group indexes. Called whenever the product list loads
// or _groupPreferredUOM changes — the primary picker honours the UOM.
function rebuildPartGroups() {
    _partGroups = new Map();
    _groupPrimary = new Map();
    _groupedHidden = new Set();
    if (!_allProducts.length) return;
    // Group every product by its partId. Products with no partId (rare —
    // unconfigured product) stand on their own and aren't grouped.
    for (const p of _allProducts) {
        if (p.partId == null) continue;
        if (!_partGroups.has(p.partId)) _partGroups.set(p.partId, []);
        _partGroups.get(p.partId).push(p.id);
    }
    // For groups with ≥ 2 products, pick a primary. Preference order:
    //   1. UOM matches _groupPreferredUOM (e.g. 'ea')
    //   2. lowest product.id (deterministic, stable across reloads)
    // Every member maps to the primary; non-primaries go in _groupedHidden.
    const pref = String(_groupPreferredUOM || 'ea').toLowerCase();
    for (const [partId, ids] of _partGroups) {
        if (ids.length < 2) {
            _groupPrimary.set(ids[0], ids[0]);
            continue;
        }
        const members = ids.map(id => _allProducts.find(p => p.id === id)).filter(Boolean);
        let primary = members.find(p => String(p.uomCode || '').toLowerCase() === pref);
        if (!primary) primary = members.slice().sort((a, b) => a.id - b.id)[0];
        for (const m of members) {
            _groupPrimary.set(m.id, primary.id);
            if (m.id !== primary.id) _groupedHidden.add(m.id);
        }
    }
}

// Helpers for the tile UOM dropdown — return the list of sibling products
// in the same group (including the focal product), or null if the product
// stands alone. Used both for rendering the dropdown and for the search
// haystack so a hidden sibling's num/desc still hits.
function productGroupMembers(product) {
    if (!product || product.partId == null) return null;
    const ids = _partGroups.get(product.partId);
    if (!ids || ids.length < 2) return null;
    return ids.map(id => _allProducts.find(p => p.id === id)).filter(Boolean);
}

// Inventory helper — sum across selected LGs (or all LGs if no filter).
function qtyForLG(productId) {
    const lgMap = _inventory.get(productId);
    if (!lgMap) return 0;
    if (_filters.locationGroupIds.size === 0) {
        let total = 0;
        for (const v of lgMap.values()) total += v;
        return total;
    }
    let total = 0;
    for (const [lg, qty] of lgMap) {
        if (_filters.locationGroupIds.has(String(lg))) total += qty;
    }
    return total;
}

// ── Loaders for part-level data (vendorparts + inventory) ────────────
async function loadLocationGroups() {
    const rows = await qp(`SELECT id, name FROM locationgroup WHERE activeFlag = 1 ORDER BY name`);
    _locationGroups = rows;
    updateMSTrigger('lg');
}

// Active UOMs for the "Preferred UOM" dropdown in Settings. Compared
// against product.uomCode (case-insensitive) in rebuildPartGroups, so
// the option `value` is the code. Label shows "code · name" so reps
// can pick between obscure codes (e.g. `pcs` vs `pc`) confidently.
async function loadUoms() {
    const rows = await qp(`SELECT code, name FROM uom WHERE activeFlag = 1 ORDER BY code`);
    _uoms = rows.map(r => ({ code: String(r.code || '').trim(), name: r.name || '' }))
                .filter(u => u.code);
    populateUomSelect();
}

function populateUomSelect() {
    const sel = document.getElementById('groupPreferredUomInput');
    if (!sel || !_uoms.length) return;
    const cur = String(_groupPreferredUOM || 'ea').toLowerCase();
    // Preserve the saved choice even if the install has since
    // deactivated that UOM — prepend it as a "(saved)" option so the
    // dropdown shows what's stored rather than silently swapping.
    const known = _uoms.some(u => u.code.toLowerCase() === cur);
    const opts = [];
    // Track whether any option has been marked `selected` yet. Earlier
    // versions used `!opts.length` as the proxy here, which is only true
    // on the first loop iteration — so when the matching UOM wasn't
    // alphabetically first (e.g. cur='ea' but list starts with '$'),
    // NOTHING was marked selected and the browser fell back to the
    // first option.
    let selectedDone = false;
    if (!known && cur) {
        opts.push(`<option value="${escapeHtml(cur)}" selected>${escapeHtml(cur)} · (saved)</option>`);
        selectedDone = true;
    }
    for (const u of _uoms) {
        const isSel = !selectedDone && u.code.toLowerCase() === cur;
        if (isSel) selectedDone = true;
        opts.push(`<option value="${escapeHtml(u.code)}"${isSel ? ' selected' : ''}>${escapeHtml(u.code)}${u.name && u.name.toLowerCase() !== u.code.toLowerCase() ? ' · ' + escapeHtml(u.name) : ''}</option>`);
    }
    sel.innerHTML = opts.join('');
}

// ── Lazy side-data loaders ──────────────────────────────────────────
// `loadSideDataForVisible(productIds)` fires three batched queries
// (part data, inventory, open POs) for the productIds that aren't
// already cached. Called from renderProducts() with the visible page's
// IDs only — large catalogues don't pay the cost of loading data for
// products the user never sees.
async function loadSideDataForVisible(productIds) {
    if (!productIds || !productIds.length) return;
    const needPart = productIds.filter(id => !_partData.has(id));
    const needInv  = productIds.filter(id => !_inventory.has(id));
    const needPO   = productIds.filter(id => !_openPOs.has(id));

    const tasks = [];
    if (needPart.length) tasks.push(_loadPartDataBatch(needPart));
    if (needInv.length)  tasks.push(_loadInventoryBatch(needInv));
    if (needPO.length)   tasks.push(_loadOpenPOsBatch(needPO));
    if (!tasks.length) return;

    await Promise.all(tasks);
    // After data arrives, re-render the visible host so the new info
    // (stock, lead, PO badges, next-break) shows up. Cheap because
    // renderProducts only paints the current page.
    if (typeof renderProducts === 'function') renderProducts(/*skipSideDataReload*/true);
}

// Chunked batch helper — Fishbowl's MySQL has no hard cap on IN-list
// length, but huge IN lists tank performance.
function chunked(arr, size) {
    const out = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += size) out.push(arr.slice(i, i + size));
    return out;
}

async function _loadPartDataBatch(ids) {
    for (const slice of chunked(ids, 200)) {
        // Mark all as resolved-to-null first so failed lookups don't re-query.
        for (const id of slice) _partData.set(id, null);
        const rows = await qp(`
            SELECT p.id AS productid, v.name AS vendorname, vp.leadtime
            FROM product p
            LEFT JOIN vendorparts vp ON vp.partid = p.partid AND vp.defaultflag = 1
            LEFT JOIN vendor v ON v.id = vp.vendorid
            WHERE p.id IN (${slice.join(',')})
        `);
        for (const r of rows) {
            if (r.productid == null) continue;
            _partData.set(r.productid, {
                leadTime: r.leadtime != null ? parseInt(r.leadtime, 10) : null,
                vendorName: r.vendorname || '',
            });
        }
    }
}

async function _loadInventoryBatch(ids) {
    for (const slice of chunked(ids, 200)) {
        for (const id of slice) if (!_inventory.has(id)) _inventory.set(id, new Map());
        const rows = await qp(`
            SELECT p.id AS productid, l.locationgroupid, COALESCE(SUM(t.qty), 0) AS qty
            FROM product p
            INNER JOIN tag t ON t.partid = p.partid
            INNER JOIN location l ON l.id = t.locationid
            WHERE p.id IN (${slice.join(',')}) AND t.typeid IN (30, 40)
            GROUP BY p.id, l.locationgroupid
        `);
        for (const r of rows) {
            if (r.productid == null || r.locationgroupid == null) continue;
            if (!_inventory.has(r.productid)) _inventory.set(r.productid, new Map());
            _inventory.get(r.productid).set(parseInt(r.locationgroupid, 10), parseFloat(r.qty) || 0);
        }
    }
}

// Open PO lines for the underlying parts. Open = not Fulfilled/Closed/Voided.
// poitem.statusid: 60=Fulfilled, 70=Closed, 80=Voided (mirrors so/po conventions).
// We compute qtyRemaining = qtyToFulfill - qtyFulfilled to surface useful
// short qty figures rather than "ordered" qty alone.
async function _loadOpenPOsBatch(ids) {
    for (const slice of chunked(ids, 200)) {
        for (const id of slice) _openPOs.set(id, []); // default empty
        const rows = await qp(`
            SELECT p.id AS productid, po.num AS ponum, po.statusid AS postatus,
                   pi.qtytofulfill, pi.qtyfulfilled, pi.datescheduledfulfillment,
                   v.name AS vendorname,
                   lg.id AS lgid, lg.name AS lgname
                  FROM product p
            INNER JOIN poitem pi ON pi.partid = p.partid
            INNER JOIN po ON po.id = pi.poid
            LEFT JOIN vendor v ON v.id = po.vendorid
            LEFT JOIN locationgroup lg ON lg.id = po.locationgroupid
            WHERE p.id IN (${slice.join(',')})
              AND po.statusid NOT IN (60, 70, 80)
              AND pi.statusid NOT IN (60, 70, 80)
              AND COALESCE(pi.qtytofulfill, 0) > COALESCE(pi.qtyfulfilled, 0)
            ORDER BY pi.datescheduledfulfillment ASC
        `);
        for (const r of rows) {
            if (r.productid == null) continue;
            const remaining = (parseFloat(r.qtytofulfill) || 0) - (parseFloat(r.qtyfulfilled) || 0);
            if (remaining <= 0) continue;
            if (!_openPOs.has(r.productid)) _openPOs.set(r.productid, []);
            _openPOs.get(r.productid).push({
                poNum: r.ponum,
                qtyToFulfill: parseFloat(r.qtytofulfill) || 0,
                qtyFulfilled: parseFloat(r.qtyfulfilled) || 0,
                qtyRemaining: remaining,
                dateScheduled: r.datescheduledfulfillment,
                vendorName: r.vendorname || '',
                lgId: intOf(r.lgid),
                lgName: r.lgname || '',
                statusId: intOf(r.postatus),
            });
        }
    }
}

function priceBreakdownTooltip(product, qty) {
    const r = resolvePrice(product, qty);
    let html = `<div><span class="lbl">Product:</span><span class="val">${escapeHtml(product.num)} × ${qty}</span></div>`;
    html += `<div><span class="lbl">Product price (T1):</span><span class="val">${fmtMoney(r.original)}</span></div>`;
    if (r.t2winner) {
        html += `<div class="rule-line">▸ T2 winner: ${escapeHtml(r.t2winner.name)} — ${escapeHtml(describeRuleAdjustment(r.t2winner))}</div>`;
        html += `<div><span class="lbl">List price (T2):</span><span class="val">${fmtMoney(r.listPrice)}</span></div>`;
    }
    if (r.t3winner) {
        html += `<div class="rule-line">▸ T3 winner: ${escapeHtml(r.t3winner.name)} — ${escapeHtml(describeRuleAdjustment(r.t3winner))}</div>`;
        html += `<div><span class="lbl">Sales price (T3):</span><span class="val" style="color:#86efac;">${fmtMoney(r.price)}</span></div>`;
    } else if (r.t2winner) {
        // T2 set the list price; no T3 rule fired so the list price is also the final.
        html += `<div><span class="lbl">Customer price:</span><span class="val" style="color:#86efac;">${fmtMoney(r.price)}</span></div>`;
    } else {
        html += `<div style="color:#94a3b8;font-style:italic;margin-top:4px;">No customer-specific pricing — list price applies.</div>`;
    }
    // Next break suggestion
    const nb = findNextBreak(product, qty);
    if (nb) {
        const deltaQty = nb.atQty - qty;
        html += `<div style="margin-top:6px;padding-top:6px;border-top:1px solid #334155;">`;
        html += `<div class="rule-line">▸ Next break at qty ${nb.atQty} (${deltaQty > 0 ? '+' + deltaQty : '0'}): ${fmtMoney(nb.price)} ea</div>`;
        if (nb.price < r.price) {
            const savePerUnit = r.price - nb.price;
            html += `<div style="color:#94a3b8;font-size:10px;">Saves ${fmtMoney(savePerUnit)} / unit at the new break</div>`;
        }
        html += `</div>`;
    }
    return html;
}

// ── Customer change orchestration ────────────────────────────────────
// Sync the mobile-only header customer trigger label with the
// current selection. Cheap no-op on desktop (the element exists but
// is `display:none`).
function updateMobileCustomerLabel() {
    const labelEl = document.getElementById('mobileCustomerLabel');
    if (!labelEl) return;
    if (_selectedCustomer) {
        labelEl.textContent = customerLabel(_selectedCustomer);
        labelEl.classList.remove('placeholder');
    } else {
        labelEl.textContent = 'Select customer';
        labelEl.classList.add('placeholder');
    }
}

async function selectCustomer(c, skipSave) {
    // If a customer-favourites write is mid-debounce, flush it before
    // swapping customers — otherwise the queued edits would silently
    // attribute to the new customer at fire time.
    if (_customerFavouritesSaveTimer) {
        clearTimeout(_customerFavouritesSaveTimer);
        _customerFavouritesSaveTimer = null;
        const prev = _selectedCustomer;
        if (prev) {
            writeCustomerFavourites(prev, [..._customerFavourites]).catch(err =>
                console.warn('Flushing pending customer-favourites write failed:', err));
        }
    }
    _selectedCustomer = c || null;
    // True-duplicate warning: another ACTIVE customer produces the SAME
    // "Parent > Name" label (sub-customers of different parents are fine
    // — the path already distinguishes them). Which record is picked
    // changes group membership → pricing, so make ambiguity loud.
    if (c && _duplicateCustomerNames.has(customerBaseLabel(c))) {
        showToast(`⚠ Multiple customer records labelled "${customerBaseLabel(c)}" exist — you selected #${c.num}. Pricing follows THIS record's groups; consider merging the duplicates in Fishbowl.`, 'info', 8000);
    }
    // Refresh _customerFavourites from the newly-selected customer (or
    // clear if they deselected). Must happen before applyAllFilters so
    // the "customer favourites" filter mode renders against the right
    // set on the first paint.
    applyCustomerFavourites(c);
    invalidatePriceCache();
    // Refresh the SO-detail fields against the new customer (carrier
    // defaults to customer → company; PO + scheduled date reset).
    initOrderDetailsForCustomer(c);
    if (c) {
        await Promise.all([
            loadActiveRulesForCustomer(c),
            loadCustomerPartsHistory(c),
            loadCustomerAddresses(c),
        ]);
    } else {
        _activeRules = [];
        _customerParts = new Map();
        _customerLastPrice = new Map();
        _customerAddresses = [];
        _selectedShipToId = _selectedBillToId = null;
        // A 'customer'-mode favourites filter only makes sense with a
        // selected customer — collapse to off when they deselect.
        if (_filters.favouritesMode === 'customer') _filters.favouritesMode = null;
        // Same for previously-purchased: _customerParts is now empty, so
        // leaving the filter on would match nothing and the catalogue
        // would look broken rather than reset. (Matters most after a
        // successful SO create, which deselects the customer.)
        if (_filters.previouslyPurchasedOnly) {
            _filters.previouslyPurchasedOnly = false;
            updatePrevPurchasedBtn();
        }
    }
    // Cart may need to refresh resolved prices
    for (const [pid, line] of _cart) {
        const product = _allProducts.find(p => p.id === pid);
        if (product) line.resolved = resolvePrice(product, line.qty);
    }
    if (!skipSave) saveState();
    updateMSTrigger('cust');
    updateMobileCustomerLabel();
    closeMS();
    renderStatusLine();
    renderFilterChipStrip();
    renderAddressPickers();
    updateFavouritesBtn();
    refreshCustomerFavButtonAvailability();
    applyAllFilters();
    renderCart();
    // The Orders view follows the selected customer. Only re-query when it is
    // actually on screen — otherwise setAppView() loads it on first open.
    if (_appView === 'orders') {
        _ordersExpanded = null;
        if (!c) _ordersScope = 'all';
        loadOrders();
    } else {
        _orders = [];      // stale for the new customer; refetched on open
    }
}

// ── Filtering / sorting / pagination ─────────────────────────────────
function applyAllFilters() {
    // NB: does NOT close the filter dropdowns. Multi-select filters
    // (Category / Stock LG) call this on every checkbox tick so the
    // catalogue updates live while the dropdown stays open for more
    // selections. Single-select pickers close themselves explicitly.
    // Pull values from inputs
    _filters.search = (document.getElementById('searchInput').value || '').trim().toLowerCase();

    _filteredProducts = _allProducts.filter(p => {
        // UOM grouping hides every non-primary group member from the main
        // list — they're still selectable via the primary tile's UOM
        // dropdown. List views deliberately bypass grouping (the
        // dropdown wouldn't fit cleanly in a row), so the filter only
        // applies in tile mode.
        if (_groupByPart && _viewMode === 'tile' && _groupedHidden.has(p.id)) return false;
        if (_filters.activeOnly && !p.activeFlag) return false;
        if (_filters.productTreeIds.size > 0) {
            const treeIds = p.treeIds || [];
            // Product passes if it belongs to ANY of the selected trees.
            if (!treeIds.some(id => _filters.productTreeIds.has(String(id)))) return false;
        }
        if (_filters.search) {
            // When grouping is on, the search should also match hidden
            // siblings (otherwise typing "BOX" wouldn't find a tile whose
            // primary is the EA variant). Build the haystack from the
            // group when applicable, the product alone otherwise.
            const members = _groupByPart ? productGroupMembers(p) : null;
            const pool = members && members.length ? members : [p];
            const hay = pool
                .flatMap(m => [m.num, m.sku, m.upc, m.description])
                .map(x => String(x ?? '').toLowerCase()).join(' ');
            if (!hay.includes(_filters.search)) return false;
        }
        if (_filters.previouslyPurchasedOnly) {
            if (!_customerParts.has(p.id)) return false;
        }
        if (_filters.inStockOnly) {
            if (qtyForLG(p.id) <= 0) return false;
        }
        if (_filters.favouritesMode) {
            // Customer / user / both favourites filter. Match either the
            // primary product or — when grouping is on — any sibling, so
            // a user-favourited "WIDGET-BOX" still surfaces the primary
            // "WIDGET-EA" tile. 'both' = union of the two sets.
            let favIds;
            if (_filters.favouritesMode === 'customer')   favIds = _customerFavIds;
            else if (_filters.favouritesMode === 'user')  favIds = _userFavIds;
            else /* 'both' */                             favIds = new Set([..._customerFavIds, ..._userFavIds]);
            const members = _groupByPart ? productGroupMembers(p) : null;
            const pool = members && members.length ? members : [p];
            if (!pool.some(m => favIds.has(m.id))) return false;
        }
        return true;
    });

    sortFiltered();
    _pageIndex = 0;
    renderFilterChipStrip();
    renderStatusLine();
    renderProducts();
    saveState();
}

// Parse `_sortBy` into its field + direction halves. Built so the rest
// of the code can ask cleanly without splitting the string everywhere.
function parseSort() {
    const m = String(_sortBy || '').match(/^(.*)-(asc|desc)$/);
    if (m) return { field: m[1], dir: m[2] };
    return { field: _sortBy || 'name', dir: 'asc' };
}

function sortFiltered() {
    const { field, dir } = parseSort();
    const mult = dir === 'desc' ? -1 : 1;
    _filteredProducts.sort((a, b) => {
        let r = 0;
        if (field === 'num') {
            r = String(a.num).localeCompare(String(b.num), undefined, { numeric: true });
        } else if (field === 'price') {
            r = (a.price || 0) - (b.price || 0);
        } else if (field === 'stock') {
            r = qtyForLG(a.id) - qtyForLG(b.id);
        } else if (field === 'last-purchased') {
            const da = _customerParts.get(a.id)?.dateLastPurchased || '';
            const db = _customerParts.get(b.id)?.dateLastPurchased || '';
            // Compare ascending here — `mult` flips to desc for newest-first.
            r = String(da).localeCompare(String(db));
        } else if (field === 'desc') {
            r = String(a.description || '').localeCompare(String(b.description || ''));
        } else if (field === 'catpath') {
            r = productCatSortKey(a).localeCompare(productCatSortKey(b), undefined, { sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true });
        } else if (field === 'upc') {
            r = String(a.upc || '').localeCompare(String(b.upc || ''), undefined, { numeric: true });
        } else {
            // 'name' (fallback): use description-or-num so blank descriptions don't all cluster.
            r = String(a.description || a.num).localeCompare(String(b.description || b.num));
        }
        return r * mult;
    });
}

// ── Favourites ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Each product has TWO independent favourite slots:
//   - customer (green star) — saved against the selected customer's
//     `Favourites` custom field; visible to every rep when that
//     customer is loaded.
//   - user (orange star) — saved against this rep's per-user settings
//     blob; private.
// They were briefly a tri-state cycle (mutually exclusive) but reps
// want to flag both simultaneously — e.g. mark a product as a customer
// favourite and ALSO keep it on their own personal pinned list.
// Toggle is now a simple on/off per kind; favBtnHtml renders two
// separate buttons.
//
// "Favourite whole part" setting still applies: when ON, toggling
// one product's customer star (say) also flips every sibling sharing
// that part's customer star to the same state. Only the kind being
// toggled fans out — the OTHER kind's siblings stay untouched.
function toggleFavourite(productId, kind) {
    if (kind !== 'customer' && kind !== 'user') return;
    // Kinds hidden by the favourites display setting can't be toggled —
    // the star isn't rendered, but defend against stale DOM anyway.
    if (kind === 'customer' && _favDisplayMode === 'user') return;
    if (kind === 'user' && _favDisplayMode === 'customer') return;
    const product = _allProducts.find(p => p.id === productId);
    if (!product) return;

    // Customer favourites need a target to write back to; no-op with a
    // toast when nothing is selected. The UI also disables the green
    // button visually but defends here in case the click slips through.
    if (kind === 'customer' && !_selectedCustomer) {
        showToast('Select a customer first to set a customer favourite', 'info', 4000);
        return;
    }

    // Customer favourites store product IDs (persist to the customer
    // record by id); user favourites store product NUMs (private blob).
    const idSet = kind === 'customer' ? _customerFavIds : _userFavIds;
    // Clicked product's CURRENT state determines the action — turn this
    // kind on if currently off, off if currently on. With whole-part
    // mode, siblings get forced to the SAME state regardless of their
    // own prior state ("this part is now my favourite, period").
    const turnOn = !idSet.has(productId);

    let targetIds = [productId];
    if (_favouriteWholePart) {
        const members = productGroupMembers(product);
        if (members && members.length > 1) targetIds = members.map(m => m.id);
    }

    for (const pid of targetIds) {
        const p = _allProducts.find(x => x.id === pid);
        if (!p) continue;
        if (kind === 'customer') {
            if (turnOn) { _customerFavourites.add(pid); _customerFavIds.add(pid); }
            else        { _customerFavourites.delete(pid); _customerFavIds.delete(pid); }
        } else {
            const n = String(p.num);
            if (turnOn) { _userFavourites.add(n); _userFavIds.add(pid); }
            else        { _userFavourites.delete(n); _userFavIds.delete(pid); }
        }
    }

    saveState();
    // Customer changes go through the debounced backend write; user
    // changes only need to persist locally (saveState covered that).
    if (kind === 'customer') queueCustomerFavouritesSave();

    // Flip the relevant button on every affected product. Only buttons
    // matching THIS kind get touched — the other star stays as-is.
    const canCust = !!_selectedCustomer;
    const sel = '.fav-btn[data-fav-pid="$"][data-fav-kind="' + kind + '"]';
    for (const pid of targetIds) {
        const isOn = idSet.has(pid);
        document.querySelectorAll(sel.replace('$', pid)).forEach(btn => {
            btn.classList.toggle('active', isOn);
            btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(isOn));
            btn.title = _favTitle(kind, isOn, canCust);
        });
    }
    // When the favourites filter is on, removing/changing may flip visibility.
    if (_filters.favouritesMode) applyAllFilters();
}

// Settings change handler — saves the new policy. We don't retroactively

    saveState();
}

        btn.classList.toggle('disabled', !canCust);
