// Detect the favourites custom fields installed on the customer entity.
// Queries the `customfield` table once at startup and populates:
//   - _installFavouritesFieldName — base spelling ('Favourites' or
//     'Favorites'; numbered fields outrank the legacy unnumbered one)
//   - _favCfExisting — exact names of every favourites CF that exists,
//     so writes only reference real columns and auto-creation knows
//     which numbered fields are still missing.
async function detectInstallFavouritesFieldName() {
    try {
        const rows = await qp(`
            SELECT name FROM customfield
            WHERE activeFlag = 1
              AND name IN ('Favourites', 'Favorites',
                           'Favourites_1', 'Favourites_2', 'Favourites_3', 'Favourites_4', 'Favourites_5',
                           'Favorites_1',  'Favorites_2',  'Favorites_3',  'Favorites_4',  'Favorites_5')
        `);
        _favCfExisting = new Set((rows || []).map(r => String(r.name)).filter(Boolean));
        const hasNum = base => [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].some(i => _favCfExisting.has(base + '_' + i));
        if (hasNum('Favourites'))                    _installFavouritesFieldName = 'Favourites';
        else if (hasNum('Favorites'))                _installFavouritesFieldName = 'Favorites';
        else if (_favCfExisting.has('Favourites'))   _installFavouritesFieldName = 'Favourites';
        else if (_favCfExisting.has('Favorites'))    _installFavouritesFieldName = 'Favorites';
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('detectInstallFavouritesFieldName → base=' + _installFavouritesFieldName
            + ' existing=[' + [..._favCfExisting].join(', ') + ']');
    } catch (e) {
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('detectInstallFavouritesFieldName failed: ' + (e && e.message || e), 'warn');
    }
}

// Create missing Favourites<n> customer custom fields via the Custom
// Fields import. Row format matches Fishbowl's own Custom Fields
// export: FieldName, Description, Type, ModuleName, Required,
// SortOrder, Active, ListName. Type "Long Text", never Required (a
// Required customer CF would break every other customer import).
// Throws on failure; on success the new names join _favCfExisting so
// the caller can write to them immediately.
async function createFavCustomFields(names) {
    if (!names || !names.length) return;
    // Next free sort order — cosmetic; keeps the new fields at the end
    // of the module's custom-field list rather than colliding at 0.
    let sortBase = 0;
    try {
        const rows = await qp(`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sortOrder), 0) AS maxsort FROM customfield`);
        sortBase = (rows && rows.length ? intOf(rows[0].maxsort) : 0) || 0;
    } catch (_) { /* cosmetic only */ }

    const cols = ['FieldName', 'Description', 'Type', 'ModuleName', 'Required', 'SortOrder', 'Active', 'ListName'];
    const importRows = [cols];
    names.forEach((nm, i) => {
        importRows.push([nm, 'Quick Order tool favourites', 'Long Text', 'Customer',
                         'FALSE', String(sortBase + 1 + i), 'TRUE', '']);
    });
    if (DEBUG) { qoDebug('createFavCustomFields ↓'); importRows.forEach(r => qoDebug('  ' + JSON.stringify(r))); }

    const pathsToTry = _resolvedCustomFieldImportPath
        ? [_resolvedCustomFieldImportPath]
        : _customFieldImportPathCandidates.slice();
    let lastErr = null;
    for (const path of pathsToTry) {
        try {
            await _postCustomerImport(path, importRows);   // generic row poster
            if (_resolvedCustomFieldImportPath !== path) {
                _resolvedCustomFieldImportPath = path;
                if (DEBUG) qoDebug('Custom Fields import path resolved → ' + path);
            }
            for (const nm of names) _favCfExisting.add(nm);
            showToast(`Created customer custom field${names.length > 1 ? 's' : ''}: ${names.join(', ')}`, 'info', 5000);
            return;
        } catch (e) {
            lastErr = e;
            const pathWrong = looksLikeUnresolvedImport(e);
            if (DEBUG) qoDebug('createFavCustomFields ' + path
                + (pathWrong ? ' returned not-found' : ' failed: ' + (e && e.message || e)), 'warn');
            if (!pathWrong) break;
        }
    }
    if (_resolvedCustomFieldImportPath && pathsToTry.length === 1) {
        _resolvedCustomFieldImportPath = null;   // re-probe next time
    }
    throw lastErr || new Error('Could not create the favourites custom fields — no Custom Fields import endpoint accepted the request.');
}

// Parse ONE favourites custom-field cell into an array of product nums.
// Each cell holds either the JSON array we wrote, or (legacy / manual
// edits) a plain comma-delimited string. Try JSON first, fall back to
// comma-split.
function _parseFavCell(v) {
    if (v == null) return [];
    const s = String(v).trim();
    if (!s) return [];
    try {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(s);
        if (Array.isArray(parsed)) return parsed;
        if (parsed != null) return [String(parsed)];
    } catch (_) { /* not JSON — fall through */ }
    return s.split(',').map(x => x.trim()).filter(Boolean);
}

// Apply customer favourites to the live state. Called from selectCustomer.
//
// Canonical storage is the NUMBERED custom fields Favourites_1.._5 (or
// Favorites_1.._5) — Fishbowl custom fields cap at 512 characters, so one
// field can't hold a long list. Each numbered field is an independently-
// parseable JSON array; reading concatenates them in order. A customer
// still carrying data only in the legacy unnumbered field is read from
// there and migrated to the numbered fields on the next write.
//
// Values come from `cust.favFieldsUK/US` + `favouritesValueUK/US`,
// extracted server-side via CustomFieldByName() in loadCustomers() —
// client-side parsing of the structured customFields JSON wrapper is
// unreliable (it's not a flat key-value object).
function applyCustomerFavourites(cust) {
    _customerFavourites = new Set();
    _customerFavouritesFieldName = _installFavouritesFieldName || 'Favourites';
    if (!cust) { rebuildFavouriteIdSets(); return; }

    // Pick whichever spelling actually has data for this customer so
    // writes go back under the same keys. Numbered fields win over the
    // legacy single field; install-wide default applies only when the
    // customer has nothing saved yet.
    const hasUKNum = (cust.favFieldsUK || []).some(v => v && String(v).trim());
    const hasUSNum = (cust.favFieldsUS || []).some(v => v && String(v).trim());
    let tokens = [];
    let src = 'none';
    if (hasUKNum || hasUSNum) {
        _customerFavouritesFieldName = hasUKNum ? 'Favourites' : 'Favorites';
        const fields = hasUKNum ? cust.favFieldsUK : cust.favFieldsUS;
        for (const cell of fields) tokens.push(..._parseFavCell(cell));
        src = 'numbered';
    } else if (cust.favouritesValueUK != null && String(cust.favouritesValueUK).trim()) {
        _customerFavouritesFieldName = 'Favourites';
        tokens = _parseFavCell(cust.favouritesValueUK);
        src = 'legacy';
    } else if (cust.favouritesValueUS != null && String(cust.favouritesValueUS).trim()) {
        _customerFavouritesFieldName = 'Favorites';
        tokens = _parseFavCell(cust.favouritesValueUS);
        src = 'legacy';
    }
    // Customer favourites are stored as product IDs. Resolve each token:
    //   - a numeric token matching a loaded product id → used verbatim.
    //   - a token matching a product NUMBER instead → a legacy num-keyed
    //     entry (written before the id switch); migrate to that product's
    //     id. The migrated set persists on the next write.
    //   - a numeric token with no loaded product → kept as-is (inactive
    //     product). A non-numeric unresolved token is dropped.
    const byNumMig = new Map();
    const loadedIdSet = new Set();
    for (const p of _allProducts) { byNumMig.set(String(p.num), p.id); loadedIdSet.add(p.id); }
    for (const raw of tokens) {
        const s = raw == null ? '' : String(raw).trim();
        if (!s) continue;
        const asId = intOf(s);
        if (asId != null && loadedIdSet.has(asId)) { _customerFavourites.add(asId); continue; }
        const mapped = byNumMig.get(s);
        if (mapped != null) { _customerFavourites.add(mapped); continue; }
        if (asId != null) _customerFavourites.add(asId);
    }
    // Whole-part expansion. With "Favourite all UOMs of the same part
    // together" on, the stored list may carry only ONE product per part
    // (e.g. the initial CSV upload stored a single UOM variant). Expand
    // the in-memory set to every sibling product sharing a part with a
    // loaded favourite so all UOM variants show the green star. The
    // fuller set persists on the next write (writeCustomerFavourites
    // serialises the whole _customerFavourites set), migrating the
    // upload's one-per-part data to the full family.
    if (_favouriteWholePart && _allProducts.length && _customerFavourites.size) {
        const byId = new Map();
        for (const p of _allProducts) byId.set(p.id, p);
        const toAdd = [];
        for (const idRaw of _customerFavourites) {
            const p = byId.get(intOf(idRaw));
            if (!p) continue;
            const members = productGroupMembers(p);   // null unless part has ≥2 UOM variants
            if (members && members.length > 1) {
                for (const m of members) if (m.id != null) toAdd.push(m.id);
            }
        }
        let added = 0;
        for (const id of toAdd) { if (!_customerFavourites.has(id)) added++; _customerFavourites.add(id); }
        if (DEBUG && added) qoDebug('applyCustomerFavourites: whole-part expansion added ' + added + ' sibling UOM(s)');
    }
    if (DEBUG) qoDebug('applyCustomerFavourites ' + cust.name
        + ' base=' + _customerFavouritesFieldName + ' src=' + src
        + ' loaded=' + _customerFavourites.size + ' [' + [..._customerFavourites].slice(0, 5).join(',')
        + (_customerFavourites.size > 5 ? ',…' : '') + ']');
    rebuildFavouriteIdSets();
}

// Debounced backend write for customer favourites. ~600ms after the
// last star flip the current set is serialised + posted. Persisting on
// every click would hammer the import endpoint when a rep is star-
// mashing through their pinned-products list.
function queueCustomerFavouritesSave() {
    if (!_selectedCustomer) return;
    clearTimeout(_customerFavouritesSaveTimer);
    _customerFavouritesSaveTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        _customerFavouritesSaveTimer = null;
        // Capture the customer at fire time — if the rep switched
        // customers between debounce and fire, the queued write belongs
        // to the previous customer (still correct, the data we built up
        // was theirs).
        const cust = _selectedCustomer;
        if (!cust) return;
        writeCustomerFavourites(cust, [..._customerFavourites]).catch(err => {
            console.warn('writeCustomerFavourites failed:', err);
            showToast('Could not save customer favourites: ' + errText(err), 'error', 6000);
        });
    }, 600);
}

// Push the customer's favourites set to Fishbowl via the Customer
// import endpoint.
//
// Fishbowl's ImportCustomer requires every row to provide a complete
// default main office address, even when only updating a custom field
// (otherwise it rejects with "Customer must have a default main office
// address"). We pull the main office address out of the already-loaded
// _customerAddresses cache and include it alongside Name + CF-<field>.
// Every OTHER customer field (other custom fields, ship/bill addresses,
// defaults, contacts) is omitted from the CSV and therefore left
// untouched on the customer record — the import only updates the
// columns it sees.
//
// The exact REST path varies by Fishbowl version — we probe a list of
// candidates and cache the first one that works. The error
// "Import not found." (from FB itself, not the proxy) means the path
// is wrong; any other 4xx means the row was rejected.
async function writeCustomerFavourites(cust, productIds) {
    if (!cust) return;

    // Find the main office address. ImportCustomer requires this even
    // on update — we can't substitute the ship or bill address since
    // they're a different type. Prefer the literal "Main Office" type,
    // fall back to whichever address is marked default, then the first
    // address on file.
    const mainAddr = _customerAddresses.find(a =>
            a.typeName && /main\s*office|^main$/i.test(a.typeName))
        || _customerAddresses.find(a => a.defaultFlag)
        || _customerAddresses[0];
    if (!mainAddr) {
        throw new Error('Customer has no addresses on file — '
            + 'can\'t save favourites until a main office address is configured.');
    }

    const baseName = _customerFavouritesFieldName || 'Favourites';
    // Favourites persist across up to FIVE numbered custom fields
    // (Favourites_1..Favourites_5) — Fishbowl custom fields cap at 512
    // characters, so long lists don't fit in one. Pack product ids
    // greedily into JSON-array chunks whose serialised form stays
    // within the cap; each field is independently parseable and the
    // reader concatenates them in order.
    const FAV_FIELD_COUNT = 5;
    const FAV_FIELD_MAX   = 512;
    const chunks = [[]];
    const dropped = [];
    for (const n of (productIds || []).map(String)) {
        const arr = chunks[chunks.length - 1];
        if (JSON.stringify([...arr, n]).length <= FAV_FIELD_MAX) { arr.push(n); continue; }
        if (chunks.length < FAV_FIELD_COUNT) { chunks.push([n]); continue; }
        dropped.push(n);
    }
    if (dropped.length) {
        showToast(`Favourites list is full — ${dropped.length} product(s) not saved (5 × 512-character field capacity reached).`, 'error', 8000);
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('writeCustomerFavourites: capacity exceeded, dropped ' + dropped.join(', '), 'warn');
    }
    // Lazily create ONLY the numbered fields this write actually needs
    // (one per non-empty chunk). Nothing is created up front — a list
    // only spills into Favourites_2 once its JSON exceeds Favourites_1's
    // 512 chars, and only then does that field get created.
    const usedCount = chunks.filter(c => c.length).length;
    const missing = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < usedCount; i++) {
        const nm = baseName + '_' + (i + 1);
        if (!_favCfExisting.has(nm)) missing.push(nm);
    }
    if (missing.length) {
        if (_autoCreateFavCf) {
            await createFavCustomFields(missing);
            // The Custom Fields import touches every customer record
            // server-side (the new field is merged into each customer's
            // customFields payload), so a customer import fired straight
            // after collides with Hibernate's optimistic lock ("Row was
            // updated or deleted by another transaction"). Give the
            // server a beat to settle; the retry loop below covers any
            // residual collision.
            await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 750));
        } else {
            throw new Error('Customer custom field(s) missing: ' + missing.join(', ')
                + '. Create them in Fishbowl (module Customer, type Long Text) or enable '
                + '"Create favourites custom fields automatically" in Settings.');
        }
    }
    // One CSV value per EXISTING numbered field — write every existing
    // one (blank when unused) so a shrinking list clears its tail
    // fields, but never reference a column whose CF doesn't exist:
    // that fails the whole import row. ImportCustomer expects
    // custom-field columns prefixed `CF-` (CSV header `CF-<name>`).
    const numberedVals = [null, null, null, null, null];   // per-slot cache, index = field − 1
    const cfCols = [];
    const cfVals = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < FAV_FIELD_COUNT; i++) {
        const nm = baseName + '_' + (i + 1);
        if (!_favCfExisting.has(nm)) continue;
        const v = i < chunks.length && chunks[i].length ? JSON.stringify(chunks[i]) : '';
        cfCols.push('CF-' + nm);
        cfVals.push(v);
        numberedVals[i] = v || null;
    }
    // One-shot migration: blank the legacy unnumbered field once the
    // numbered fields own the data. Only included when it actually held
    // a value — referencing a CF column that doesn't exist on the
    // install fails the whole import row.
    const legacyVal = baseName === 'Favourites' ? cust.favouritesValueUK : cust.favouritesValueUS;
    if (legacyVal != null && String(legacyVal).trim()) {
        cfCols.push('CF-' + baseName);
        cfVals.push('');
    }
    // Nothing writable at all — no numbered fields exist yet (e.g.
    // clearing an already-empty list with auto-create off) and no
    // legacy value to blank. Skip rather than send an empty update.
    if (!cfCols.length) {
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('writeCustomerFavourites: no favourites CF columns to write — skipped', 'warn');
        return { ok: true };
    }

    // Columns:
    //   Name              — identity key (matches the existing customer)
    //   Address* / Main*  — the main office address Fishbowl insists on
    //   CF-<base>_1.._5   — the favourites chunks (+ legacy blank-out)
    // Everything else on the customer (other addresses, contacts,
    // defaults, other custom fields) stays as-is because we don't
    // include those columns.
    const cols = [
        'Name',
        'AddressName', 'AddressContact', 'AddressType', 'IsDefault',
        'Address', 'City', 'State', 'Zip', 'Country', 'Residential',
        ...cfCols,
    ];
    // AddressType MUST be the numeric addresstype.id — Fishbowl tries to
    // parse the column as an int and throws "For input string: 'Main
    // Office'" if you send the name. The id comes from addresstype.id
    // (typically 10 = Main Office, 20 = Bill To, 40 = Ship To). If we
    // don't have a typeId on the cached address, default to 10 which is
    // the conventional Main Office id across Fishbowl installs.
    const addrTypeId = mainAddr.typeId != null ? mainAddr.typeId : 10;
    const vals = [
        cust.name,
        mainAddr.label    || mainAddr.recipient || 'Main Office',
        mainAddr.recipient || cust.name,
        addrTypeId,
        'true',
        mainAddr.street, mainAddr.city, mainAddr.state, mainAddr.zip, mainAddr.country,
        mainAddr.residential ? 'true' : 'false',
        ...cfVals,
    ];

    const importRows = [cols, vals];

    // Surface the rows in the debug console so column-mismatch / formatting
    // issues are visible without devtools. JSON.stringify rather than raw
    // text so an embedded newline shows as \n instead of silently wrapping
    // the log line — which is exactly what made the two-line-address bug
    // look like a torn CSV in the first place.
    if (DEBUG) {
        qoDebug('writeCustomerFavourites rows ↓');
        importRows.forEach(r => qoDebug('  ' + JSON.stringify(r)));
    }

    // Build the ordered list of paths to attempt. If we've already
    // resolved one this session, try it first (and ONLY it — if the
    // cached path stops working we'll re-probe on next call).
    const pathsToTry = _resolvedCustomerImportPath
        ? [_resolvedCustomerImportPath]
        : _customerImportPathCandidates.slice();

    // Post with retry on optimistic-lock collisions. "Row was updated
    // or deleted by another transaction" is Hibernate's stale-version
    // error on the customer row — transient (another write, e.g. the
    // just-run Custom Fields import or a concurrent user, bumped the
    // row's version). The import re-reads the row on retry, so backing
    // off briefly and resending the identical CSV is safe.
    const postWithRetry = async (path) => {
        for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
            try { return await _postCustomerImport(path, importRows); }
            catch (e) {
                const stale = /updated or deleted by another transaction/i.test(String(e && e.message || e));
                if (!stale || attempt >= 2) throw e;
                if (DEBUG) qoDebug('writeCustomerFavourites: stale-row collision — retry ' + (attempt + 1) + '/2', 'warn');
                await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 800 * (attempt + 1)));
            }
        }
    };

    let lastErr = null;
    for (const path of pathsToTry) {
        try {
            await postWithRetry(path);
            // Cache the working path so subsequent saves go straight
            // to it without probing.
            if (_resolvedCustomerImportPath !== path) {
                _resolvedCustomerImportPath = path;
                if (DEBUG) qoDebug('Customer import path resolved → ' + path);
            }
            // Keep the cached values on the customer in sync with what
            // we just wrote so switching customers during the session
            // and switching back doesn't re-load the pre-edit list.
            // The written spelling's numbered slots take the new chunks;
            // the other spelling and the legacy single field are cleared
            // so applyCustomerFavourites keeps picking the right source.
            const cachedFields = numberedVals.map(v => v || null);
            if (baseName === 'Favourites') {
                cust.favFieldsUK = cachedFields;
                cust.favFieldsUS = [null, null, null, null, null];
                cust.favouritesValueUK = null;
            } else {
                cust.favFieldsUS = cachedFields;
                cust.favFieldsUK = [null, null, null, null, null];
                cust.favouritesValueUS = null;
            }
            return { ok: true };
        } catch (e) {
            lastErr = e;
            const msg = String(e && e.message || e);
            const pathWrong = looksLikeUnresolvedImport(e);
            if (DEBUG) {
                qoDebug('writeCustomerFavourites ' + path
                    + (pathWrong ? ' returned not-found' : ' failed: ' + msg), 'warn');
            }
            // If the error looks like "wrong path" keep probing.
            // Anything else (e.g. "bad update type", auth error) is a
            // real failure of THIS path — stop probing so the user sees
            // the actual reason instead of a generic "no path worked".
            if (!pathWrong) break;
        }
    }
    // If our cached path stopped working, clear it so the next call re-
    // probes the full list. (We didn't fall through to the candidate
    // list above because pathsToTry had only the cached entry.)
    if (_resolvedCustomerImportPath && pathsToTry.length === 1) {
        _resolvedCustomerImportPath = null;
    }
    throw lastErr || new Error('No customer import endpoint accepted the request. Tried: '
        + pathsToTry.join(', '));
}

// Single attempt at posting import ROWS to a specific path. `rows` is an
// array of row arrays, header row first:
//   [['Name','City'], ['Pierres Pastry','Southport']]
//
// JSON FIRST, deliberately. POST /api/import/:name accepts exactly that shape
// under Content-Type: application/json (apidocs "Import data via JSON", server
// 26.6), and sending it that way removes an entire class of text-escaping
// bugs at once: no row splitting, no quote doubling, no charset guessing.
//
// It is also the ONLY way to send a value that CONTAINS a newline. In JSON a
// two-line street address is just "a\nb"; in CSV the importer tears the row in
// half and throws (see csvSafe). So on a server that takes JSON, the address
// goes back exactly as it was stored — nothing is flattened.
//
// CSV remains the fallback for older servers, and the working encoding is
// cached, so discovering which one this server speaks costs one extra request
// once per session and only if the first attempt fails.
//
// Returns on success, throws on any failure. The caller distinguishes
// "wrong path" vs "real error" via looksLikeUnresolvedImport.
async function _postCustomerImport(path, rows) {
    const asCsv = () => rows.map(r => r.map(csvField).join(',')).join('\n');

    // Legacy bridge (fishbowl host without runRestApiAsync). ImportRq is
    // line-oriented, so it is CSV-only — but the rows arrive already split,
    // so nothing can tear on a value's newline the way `csvBody.split('\n')`
    // used to. The values are still flattened by csvField.
    if (MODE === 'fishbowl' && typeof runRestApiAsync !== 'function'
        && typeof runApiRequest === 'function') {
        // Type derived from the URL path (strip the /api/import/ prefix and
        // re-add 'Import', so 'Customers' becomes 'ImportCustomers').
        const typeName = 'Import' + path.replace(/^.*\/api\/import\//, '').replace(/-/g, '');
        const payload = {
            ImportRq: { Type: typeName, Rows: { Row: rows.map(r => r.map(csvField).join(',')) } },
        };
        const raw = runApiRequest('ImportRq', JSON.stringify(payload));
        const resp = typeof raw === 'string' ? safeParse(raw) : raw;
        const flat = JSON.stringify(resp || {}).toLowerCase();
        const ok = /statuscode"\s*:\s*"?1000/.test(flat) || /"success"\s*:\s*true/.test(flat);
        if (!ok) throw new Error(extractImportError(resp) || 'ImportRq did not return success status');
        return resp;
    }

    const send = async (encoding) => {
        const body = encoding === 'json' ? JSON.stringify(rows) : asCsv();
        const type = encoding === 'json' ? 'application/json' : CSV_CONTENT_TYPE;
        if (typeof runRestApiAsync === 'function') {
            return await runRestApiAsync({ method: 'POST', path, body, contentType: type });
        }
        // Direct fetch — portal/standalone.
        if (MODE === 'standalone' && !_conn.token) {
            throw new Error('Not connected — log in via the header Connect button.');
        }
        const url = _conn.baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, '') + path;
        const headers = { 'Content-Type': type, 'Accept': 'application/json, text/plain' };
        if (_conn.token) headers.Authorization = 'Bearer ' + _conn.token;
        const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
        if (!res.ok) {
            const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
            const err = new Error('HTTP ' + res.status + (text ? ' — ' + text.slice(0, 400) : ''));
            err.status = res.status;
            throw err;
        }
        return await res.text().catch(() => '');
    };

    const order = _importEncoding ? [_importEncoding] : ['json', 'csv'];
    let lastErr = null;
    for (const encoding of order) {
        try {
            const resp = await send(encoding);
            if (_importEncoding !== encoding) {
                _importEncoding = encoding;
                if (DEBUG) qoDebug('Import encoding resolved → ' + encoding
                    + (encoding === 'csv' ? ' (this server does not take the JSON form; '
                        + 'values containing newlines will be flattened)' : ''));
            }
            return resp;
        } catch (e) {
            lastErr = e;
            if (DEBUG) qoDebug('import via ' + encoding + ' failed: ' + errText(e), 'warn');
        }
    }
    // A cached encoding that stopped working gets re-probed on the next call.
    if (_importEncoding && order.length === 1) _importEncoding = null;
    throw lastErr;
}

function onModuleOptChange() {
    _t2ModuleOpt = document.getElementById('t2ModuleOptSelect').value === 'high' ? 'high' : 'low';
    _t3ModuleOpt = document.getElementById('t3ModuleOptSelect').value === 'high' ? 'high' : 'low';

    renderStatusLine();
}

function toggleInStockOnlyBtn() {

// Header favourites toggle. With the display setting on 'both' this is
// the 4-state cycle:
//   null       → 'customer'  (filter to customer's shared favourites)
//   'customer' → 'user'      (filter to this user's personal favourites)
//   'user'     → 'both'      (union — show either kind)
//   'both'     → null        (no filter)
// When no customer is selected, the customer-bearing states drop out of
// the cycle (they'd resolve to an empty set), so it compresses to
// null ↔ 'user'.
// With the display setting on 'customer' or 'user' the cycle collapses
// to a plain on/off toggle for that single kind — no extra clicks.
function toggleFavouritesOnly() {
    const cur = _filters.favouritesMode;
    const have = !!_selectedCustomer;
    let nxt;
    if (_favDisplayMode === 'customer') {
        if (!have) { showToast('Select a customer first to filter by customer favourites', 'info', 4000); return; }
        nxt = cur ? null : 'customer';
    } else if (_favDisplayMode === 'user') {
        nxt = cur ? null : 'user';
    } else {
        if (cur === null)            nxt = have ? 'customer' : 'user';
        else if (cur === 'customer') nxt = 'user';
        else if (cur === 'user')     nxt = have ? 'both' : null;
        else                         nxt = null;   // cur === 'both'
    }
    _filters.favouritesMode = nxt;
    updateFavouritesBtn();
    applyAllFilters();
}
function updateFavouritesBtn() {
    const btn = document.getElementById('favouritesToggleBtn');
    if (!btn) return;
    btn.classList.remove('fav-mode-customer', 'fav-mode-user', 'fav-mode-both');
    if (_filters.favouritesMode === 'customer') btn.classList.add('fav-mode-customer');
    else if (_filters.favouritesMode === 'user') btn.classList.add('fav-mode-user');
    else if (_filters.favouritesMode === 'both') btn.classList.add('fav-mode-both');
    let titleByMode;
    if (_favDisplayMode === 'customer') {
        titleByMode = {
            off:      'Favourites filter: off · click to show customer favourites',
            customer: 'Showing customer favourites (shared) · click to turn off',
        };
    } else if (_favDisplayMode === 'user') {
        titleByMode = {
            off:  'Favourites filter: off · click to show your favourites',
            user: 'Showing your personal favourites · click to turn off',
        };
    } else {
        titleByMode = {
            off:       'Favourites filter: off · click to cycle customer → user → both → off',
            customer:  'Showing customer favourites (shared) · click to cycle to user',
            user:      _selectedCustomer
                         ? 'Showing your personal favourites · click to cycle to both'
                         : 'Showing your personal favourites · click to turn off',
            both:      'Showing customer + your favourites (union) · click to turn off',
        };
    }
    btn.title = titleByMode[_filters.favouritesMode || 'off'] || titleByMode.off;
    btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(_filters.favouritesMode !== null));
}

// ── View mode ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Switch the live view. This is session-only — the view the report OPENS
// in comes from the Default view setting (_defaultViewMode), so clicking
// a header toggle no longer silently rewrites that default.
function setViewMode(mode) {
    if (!VIEW_MODES.includes(mode)) return;
    // Phones only. A multi-column table cannot fit at 390px, so coerce to
    // tile and let the matching CSS hide the toggle — saved state from a
    // desktop must not leave a phone user with a clipped table.
    // Tablets are explicitly NOT coerced: an iPad has more width than many
    // laptops, and gating this on isMobileViewport() took the tile/list
    // choice away from them along with the toggle.
    if (mode !== 'tile' && isPhoneViewport()) {
        mode = 'tile';
    }
    _viewMode = mode;
    VIEW_MODES.forEach(m => {
        const b = document.getElementById('view-btn-' + m);
        if (b) b.classList.toggle('active', m === mode);
    });
    // The Columns selector only applies to the two list views.
    const colWrap = document.getElementById('colWrap');
    if (colWrap) colWrap.style.display = (mode === 'tile') ? 'none' : '';
    const colPanel = document.getElementById('colPanel');
    if (colPanel && mode === 'tile') colPanel.classList.add('hidden');
    // applyAllFilters (not renderProducts) so the UOM-grouping filter
    // is recomputed when switching between tile (groups collapsed) and
    // list (every product shown).
    applyAllFilters();
    saveState();
}

// ── App view (Catalog | Orders) ──────────────────────────────────────
// The outer screen switch. Follows the page's body-class idiom
// (mobile-enabled / mode-<MODE> / cart-drawer-open) rather than inventing a
// second mechanism. Session-only: the report always opens on the catalogue.
function setAppView(v) {
    if (!APP_VIEWS.includes(v) || v === _appView) return;
    _appView = v;
    document.body.classList.toggle('qo-view-orders', v === 'orders');
    APP_VIEWS.forEach(x => {
        const b = document.getElementById('app-view-' + x);
        if (b) {
            b.classList.toggle('active', x === v);
            b.setAttribute('aria-current', String(x === v));
        }
    });
    // Catalogue-owned popovers must not float over the other screen.
    const settings = document.getElementById('settingsPanel');
    const help     = document.getElementById('helpPanel');
    const colPanel = document.getElementById('colPanel');
    if (settings) settings.classList.remove('open');
    if (help)     help.classList.remove('open');
    if (colPanel) colPanel.classList.add('hidden');
    closeMS();
    closeOrdersMenu();
    // Carry the one real customer picker across to whichever view is showing.
    relocateCustomerPicker(v === 'orders');
    updateMSTrigger('cust');

    if (v === 'orders') {
        // Follow whatever customer the rep is already working on.
        if (!_selectedCustomer) _ordersScope = 'all';
        renderOrders();                       // paint immediately, even if empty
        if (!_orders.length && !_ordersLoading) loadOrders();
    } else {
        // observeListTableResize() keeps ONE module-level observer and
        // disconnects the previous one, so the product table lost its observer
        // when an orders table was rendered. Re-rendering re-establishes it.
        // `true` skips the side-data reload — stock/lead/PO caches are already
        // warm, and switching views is not a refresh.
        renderProducts(true);
    }
    renderStatusLine();
}

// ── Product rendering ────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Paginate any array against the current page size / index.
function pagedList(arr) {
    if (_pageSize >= 9999) return arr;
    const start = _pageIndex * _pageSize;
    return arr.slice(start, start + _pageSize);
}

// Row descriptors for the list views. Ungrouped → one row per product.
// Grouped (_groupByTree) → one row per (product × distinct MAIN
// category); rows are ordered so each main category is contiguous
// (alphabetical, "Uncategorised" last) while preserving the current
// sort within each group. renderListTable emits a header when the main
// changes.
function buildListDescriptors() {
    if (!_groupByTree) return _filteredProducts.map(p => ({ product: p, main: null }));
    const rows = [];
    _filteredProducts.forEach((p, idx) => {
        productMainCats(p).forEach(m => rows.push({ product: p, main: m, _idx: idx }));
    });
    rows.sort((a, b) => {
        const an = a.main ? a.main.name : '', bn = b.main ? b.main.name : '';
        const au = an === 'Uncategorised' ? 1 : 0, bu = bn === 'Uncategorised' ? 1 : 0;
        if (au !== bu) return au - bu;
        const c = an.localeCompare(bn, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true });
        return c !== 0 ? c : a._idx - b._idx;   // keep current sort within a group
    });
    return rows;
}

function renderProducts(skipSideDataReload) {
    const host = document.getElementById('productHost');
    if (!host) return;
    if (_filteredProducts.length === 0) {
        host.innerHTML = `<div class="text-center text-sm text-slate-400 italic py-12">No products match the current filters.</div>`;
        renderPagination();
        return;
    }
    let visibleIds;
    if (_viewMode === 'tile') {
        _pageItemCount = _filteredProducts.length;
        const products = pagedList(_filteredProducts);
        host.innerHTML = '<div class="tile-grid"></div>';
        const grid = host.querySelector('.tile-grid');
        products.forEach(p => grid.appendChild(renderTile(p)));
        visibleIds = products.map(p => p.id);
    } else {
        // List / List+Img: page over row descriptors (which may expand a
        // product across several main-category groups when grouping is on).
        const descriptors = buildListDescriptors();
        _pageItemCount = descriptors.length;
        const pageRows = pagedList(descriptors);
        host.innerHTML = '';
        host.appendChild(renderListTable(pageRows, _viewMode === 'list-image'));
        visibleIds = [...new Set(pageRows.map(d => d.product.id))];
    }
    renderPagination();
    armLazyImages(host);
    // Kick off lazy side-data load for the visible products. `skipSideDataReload`
    // suppresses the second render that fires when the load finishes (used when
    // we're already re-rendering because new data just arrived).
    if (!skipSideDataReload) {
        loadSideDataForVisible(visibleIds).catch(e => console.warn('Side-data load failed:', e));
    }
}

function renderTile(product) {
    const card = document.createElement('div');
    card.className = 'product-tile';
    card.dataset.pid = product.id;
    const inCart = _cart.get(product.id);
    // Initial qty shown in the tile's stepper input. Desktop defaults
    // to 1 (the "to-add" amount the user can change before clicking
    // Add). Mobile defaults to 0 — the stepper IS the cart row and
    // not-in-cart products read as 0.
    const qty = inCart ? inCart.qty : (isMobileViewport() ? 0 : 1);
    const resolved = resolvePrice(product, qty);
    const hasRule = resolved.source === 'rule' && resolved.price !== resolved.original;
    const cp = _customerParts.get(product.id);

    const lastPurchaseHtml = cp
        ? `<span class="last-purchase">Last: ${moment(cp.dateLastPurchased).fromNow(true)} ago · ${cp.lastQty} ${product.uomCode || ''}</span>`
        : '';

    // Stock + lead-time + open-PO row. Stock honours selected LG filter;
    // if none selected it shows the all-LGs total. Lead time is for the
    // default vendor on the underlying part. PO badge shows aggregate
    // remaining qty + the earliest scheduled date.
    const partInfo = _partData.get(product.id);
    const stock = qtyForLG(product.id);
    const leadTime = partInfo?.leadTime;
    const lgSelected = _filters.locationGroupIds.size > 0;
    const stockClass = stock > 0 ? 'text-emerald-600' : 'text-slate-400';
    const pos = openPoSummary(product.id) || [];
    let poBadge = '';
    if (pos.length > 0) {
        const totalRemaining = pos.reduce((s, p) => s + p.qtyRemaining, 0);
        const earliest = pos[0].dateScheduled ? formatDateShort(pos[0].dateScheduled) : '—';
        poBadge = `<span class="po-badge" data-po-pid="${product.id}">
            <svg fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M9 17v-2m3 2v-4m3 4v-6m2 10H7a2 2 0 01-2-2V5a2 2 0 012-2h5.586a1 1 0 01.707.293l5.414 5.414a1 1 0 01.293.707V19a2 2 0 01-2 2z"></path></svg>
            ${totalRemaining.toLocaleString()} · ${earliest}${pos.length > 1 ? ` +${pos.length - 1}` : ''}
        </span>`;
    }
    const stockLine = `<div style="font-size:11px;color:var(--muted-2);display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;">
        <span class="stock-badge" data-stock-pid="${product.id}" style="cursor:help;"><span class="${stockClass}" style="font-weight:600;">${stock.toLocaleString()}</span> in stock</span>
        ${leadTime != null ? `<span title="Lead time from ${escapeHtml(partInfo.vendorName || 'default vendor')}">· ${leadTime}d lead</span>` : ''}
        ${poBadge}
    </div>`;

    // Next-break suggestion — only render if it actually saves money.
    // `.next-break` class lets refreshPrice() find + replace/remove this
    // node when the qty stepper crosses a rule boundary.
    const nb = findNextBreak(product, qty);
    let nextBreakHtml = '';
    if (nb && nb.price < resolved.price) {
        const need = nb.atQty - qty;
        nextBreakHtml = `<div class="next-break" style="font-size:11px;color:#b45309;font-weight:600;cursor:help;" title="Buy ${need} more to reach the ${nb.atQty}-unit price tier">↑ +${need} for ${fmtMoney(nb.price)} ea</div>`;
    }

    // UOM dropdown vs plain span. When grouping is on AND this product
    // belongs to a multi-member part-group, render a <select> showing
    // each sibling's UOM — change handler swaps the tile to that sibling.
    const groupMembers = (_groupByPart && _viewMode === 'tile') ? productGroupMembers(product) : null;
    const hasUomGroup  = !!(groupMembers && groupMembers.length > 1);
    const uomCell = hasUomGroup
        ? `<select class="uom-select" data-uom-group-pid="${product.id}" title="Switch UOM — siblings share the same part">
                ${groupMembers.map(m => `<option value="${m.id}"${m.id === product.id ? ' selected' : ''}>/ ${escapeHtml(m.uomCode || '?')}</option>`).join('')}
           </select>`
        : `<span class="uom">${product.uomCode ? '/ ' + escapeHtml(product.uomCode) : ''}</span>`;

    card.innerHTML = `
        <div class="img-wrap">
            ${favBtnHtml(product.id)}
            <img class="product-img" data-product-id="${product.id}" src="${PLACEHOLDER_SVG}" alt="">
        </div>
        <div class="body">
            <div class="num-row">
                <a class="num-pill" href="#" data-open-product title="Open ${escapeHtml(product.num)} in the Product module">${escapeHtml(product.num)}</a>
                ${(_showUpcTile && product.upc) ? `<span class="tile-upc" title="UPC: ${escapeHtml(product.upc)}">${escapeHtml(product.upc)}</span>` : ''}
            </div>
            <div class="name">${escapeHtml(product.description || product.num)}</div>
            ${lastPurchaseHtml}
            ${stockLine}
            ${nextBreakHtml}
            <div class="price-row">
                ${hasRule && _showOrigPrice ? `<span class="price-orig">${fmtMoney(resolved.original)}</span>` : ''}
                <span class="price ${hasRule ? 'has-rule' : ''}">${fmtMoney(resolved.price)}</span>
                ${uomCell}
            </div>
        </div>
        <div class="actions">
            <div class="qty-stepper">
                <button data-step="-1">−</button>
                <input type="number" min="1" value="${qty}">
                <button data-step="1">+</button>
            </div>
            <button class="hdr-btn primary" style="margin-left:auto;" data-add ${inCart ? `data-in-cart="${inCart.qty}"` : ''}>Add</button>
        </div>
    `;
    wireProductCard(card, product);
    return card;
}

// Swap a tile in place to show a different product (same part-group sibling).
// Triggered by the UOM dropdown change. Renders a fresh tile against the
// new product and replaces the existing card — cheap because it's only
// the one tile, not the whole grid.
function swapTileToProduct(card, newProductId) {
    const np = _allProducts.find(p => p.id === newProductId);
    if (!np) return;
    const fresh = renderTile(np);
    card.replaceWith(fresh);
    // Re-arm lazy image loading for the swapped-in product so its
    // thumbnail loads if it has one in cache or comes into view.
    armLazyImages(fresh.parentElement || fresh);
}

// Resize handle on a list-view <th>. The width the rep drags to is the
// column's "desired width" (stored on the col's data-desired-width).
// Actual rendered width is computed by fitListColumns() — if the sum of
// desired widths exceeds the table's available width, every column gets
// scaled down proportionally. Min DESIRED width 30px so a column can't
// be dragged into oblivion.
function attachColumnResizer(th) {
    if (!th || th.querySelector('.col-resizer')) return;
    const colKey = th.dataset.col;
    if (!colKey) return;
    const table = th.closest('table');
    const colEl = table?.querySelector(`colgroup col[data-col="${colKey}"]`);
    if (!colEl) return;
    const r = document.createElement('div');
    r.className = 'col-resizer';
    th.appendChild(r);
    r.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {
        e.preventDefault();
        e.stopPropagation();
        const startX = e.pageX;
        // Drag baseline = the current DESIRED width, not the rendered
        // one. Otherwise dragging a scaled-down column would snap it to
        // its rendered (compressed) size on every move.
        const startDesired = parseFloat(colEl.dataset.desiredWidth) || colEl.offsetWidth;
        r.classList.add('dragging');
        document.body.style.cursor = 'col-resize';
        function move(ev) {
            const w = Math.max(30, startDesired + (ev.pageX - startX));
            colEl.dataset.desiredWidth = w;
            fitListColumns(table);
        }
        function up() {
            document.removeEventListener('mousemove', move);
            document.removeEventListener('mouseup', up);
            r.classList.remove('dragging');
            document.body.style.cursor = '';
            // Persist every col's desired width — that's the rep's
            // intent, scaling is recomputed per render.
            table.querySelectorAll('colgroup col').forEach(c => {
                const k = c.dataset.col;
                const d = parseFloat(c.dataset.desiredWidth);
                if (k && d > 0) _colWidths[k] = Math.round(d);
            });
            saveState();
        }
        document.addEventListener('mousemove', move);
        document.addEventListener('mouseup', up);
    });
}

// Scale every <col>'s rendered width so the sum equals the table's
// available content width. Desired widths (data-desired-width) are the
// authoritative source; rendered widths (style.width) are derived.
//   - If sum(desired) ≤ available, render at desired (no scale).
//   - If sum(desired) > available, scale every col by (available/sum).
// Min 20px on each rendered width so qty/action stay grabbable even at
// extreme contractions.
function fitListColumns(table) {
    if (!table) return;
    const parent = table.parentElement;
    if (!parent) return;
    // productHost is a plain block child of productArea — its
    // clientWidth is already net of productArea's 12px padding, so we
    // can use it directly. Subtract 2px for the table's border so the
    // rendered cells don't ever push past the visible edge.
    const avail = Math.max(0, parent.clientWidth - 2);
    if (!avail) return;
    const cols = [...table.querySelectorAll('colgroup col')];
    if (!cols.length) return;
    const desired = cols.map(c => parseFloat(c.dataset.desiredWidth) || 0);
    const sum = desired.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
    if (!sum) return;
    const scale = sum > avail ? avail / sum : 1;
    cols.forEach((c, i) => {
        const w = Math.max(20, Math.floor(desired[i] * scale));
        c.style.width = w + 'px';
    });
}

// One ResizeObserver per table — refits on productArea width changes
// (window resize, cart-panel show/hide, debug-console toggle).
let _listResizeObserver = null;
function observeListTableResize(table) {
    const parent = table?.parentElement;
    if (!parent || typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined') return;
    if (_listResizeObserver) _listResizeObserver.disconnect();
    _listResizeObserver = new ResizeObserver(() => fitListColumns(table));
    _listResizeObserver.observe(parent);
}

// The registry columns currently active for a list render: visible,
// in user order, minus 'thumb' outside list-image mode. qty + action
// are appended by the caller — they're pinned, not registry-driven.
function activeListCols(withImage) {
    return _listCols.filter(c => c.vis && (withImage || c.key !== 'thumb'));
}

function renderListTable(rows, withImage) {
    const table = document.createElement('table');
    table.className = 'list-table';
    // Default widths in px. Resizable columns get a data-col key so we
    // can persist user-adjusted widths in _colWidths under saveState().
    const dw = {
        fav: 52, thumb: 48,
        num: 110, upc: 130, desc: 220, catpath: 180, last: 140, stock: 70, lead: 60,
        onorder: 170, price: 130, qty: 110, action: 70,
    };
    // Authoritative column widths via <colgroup>. With `table-layout: fixed`,
    // the browser uses these widths verbatim — bypasses any ambiguity in
    // <th style="width:…"> + padding + text-overflow. Order MUST match the
    // header / body cell sequence below — both derive from dataCols.
    const dataCols = activeListCols(withImage);
    const colSpecs = [
        ...dataCols.map(c => ({ key: c.key })),
        { key: 'qty' },
        { key: 'action' },
    ];
    // Two widths per col:
    //   data-desired-width — the rep's intended width (saved/default).
    //                         Authoritative; scaled at fit time.
    //   style.width         — the actual rendered width after fit-to-pane.
    // `width: 100%` on the table + `table-layout: fixed` ought to scale
    // col widths proportionally, but Chromium honours px widths verbatim
    // when the sum exceeds the table width, causing horizontal overflow.
    // We side-step that by computing actual widths in JS via
    // fitListColumns() and re-running on ResizeObserver. Cart-panel
    // resize automatically narrows productArea (flex:1, cart fixed at
    // 360px) so the observer fires whenever the cart changes width too.
    const colgroup = document.createElement('colgroup');
    colgroup.innerHTML = colSpecs.map(c => {
        const w = _colWidths[c.key] ?? dw[c.key];
        return `<col data-col="${c.key}" data-desired-width="${w}" style="width:${w}px;">`;
    }).join('');
    table.appendChild(colgroup);

    const thead = document.createElement('thead');
    // Map of th data-col → sort field. Columns without an entry can't be
    // sort-clicked (image, qty input, action). The `lead` column has no
    // matching sortField yet; keep it pure-resize.
    const sortByCol = {
        num: 'num', upc: 'upc', desc: 'desc', catpath: 'catpath', last: 'last-purchased',
        stock: 'stock', price: 'price',
    };
    const { field: activeField, dir: activeDir } = parseSort();
    const cellHtml = (key, label, align) => {
        const sortField = sortByCol[key];
        const sortable = !!sortField;
        const active = sortable && sortField === activeField;
        const arrow = !sortable ? '' :
            `<span class="arrow">${active ? (activeDir === 'desc' ? '↓' : '↑') : '↕'}</span>`;
        const cls = sortable ? `sortable${active ? ' sort-active' : ''}` : '';
        return `<th data-col="${key}"${sortField ? ` data-sort-field="${sortField}"` : ''}
                    class="${cls}"
                    ${align ? `style="text-align:${align};"` : ''}>${label}${arrow}</th>`;
    };
    // Per-key header builders — emitted in dataCols order so the header
    // always matches the colgroup + body cell sequence.
    const headByKey = {
        fav:     () => '<th data-col="fav"></th>',
        thumb:   () => '<th data-col="thumb" class="thumb-cell"></th>',
        num:     () => cellHtml('num', 'Product #'),
        upc:     () => cellHtml('upc', 'UPC'),
        desc:    () => cellHtml('desc', 'Description'),
        catpath: () => cellHtml('catpath', 'Category'),
        last:    () => cellHtml('last', 'Last purchased'),
        stock:   () => cellHtml('stock', 'Stock', 'right'),
        lead:    () => '<th data-col="lead" style="text-align:right;">Lead</th>',
        onorder: () => '<th data-col="onorder">On order</th>',
        price:   () => cellHtml('price', 'Price', 'right'),
    };
    thead.innerHTML = `<tr>
        ${dataCols.map(c => headByKey[c.key] ? headByKey[c.key]() : '').join('\n        ')}
        <th data-col="qty" class="qty-cell">Qty</th>
        <th data-col="action" class="action-cell"></th>
    </tr>`;
    // Wire resizers + click-to-sort after the thead is in the table.
    setTimeout(() => {
        thead.querySelectorAll('th[data-col]').forEach(th => attachColumnResizer(th));
        thead.querySelectorAll('th.sortable').forEach(th => {
            th.addEventListener('click', e => {
                // Don't trigger sort when the user is grabbing the resize
                // strip — `.col-resizer` swallows mousedown but click can
                // still bubble through, so check the original target.
                if (e.target.classList && e.target.classList.contains('col-resizer')) return;
                const f = th.dataset.sortField;
                if (!f) return;
                // Toggle direction if already sorting on this field, else default asc.
                // Exception: clicking 'last-purchased' fresh defaults to DESC (newest first).
                const cur = parseSort();
                let dir = 'asc';
                if (cur.field === f) dir = cur.dir === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc';
                else if (f === 'last-purchased' || f === 'stock') dir = 'desc';
                _sortBy = `${f}-${dir}`;
                document.getElementById('sortBySelect').value = _sortBy;
                sortFiltered(); _pageIndex = 0; renderProducts(); saveState();
            });
        });
    }, 0);
    table.appendChild(thead);
    const tbody = document.createElement('tbody');
    const totalCols = dataCols.length + 2;   // + qty + action (pinned)
    let lastMain;                            // undefined until first row
    rows.forEach(d => {
        if (_groupByTree) {
            const mainName = d.main ? d.main.name : 'Uncategorised';
            if (lastMain === undefined || mainName !== lastMain) {
                lastMain = mainName;
                const hr = document.createElement('tr');
                hr.className = 'group-row';
                hr.innerHTML = `<td colspan="${totalCols}">${escapeHtml(mainName)}</td>`;
                tbody.appendChild(hr);
            }
        }
        tbody.appendChild(renderListRow(d.product, withImage, dataCols, d.main));
    });
    table.appendChild(tbody);
    // Initial fit + observe parent for resize so the table always
    // matches productArea's current width (e.g. when the cart panel
    // shifts or the window is dragged onto a smaller monitor).
    setTimeout(() => fitListColumns(table), 0);
    observeListTableResize(table);
    return table;
}

function renderListRow(product, withImage, dataCols, groupMain) {
    if (!dataCols) dataCols = activeListCols(withImage);
    const tr = document.createElement('tr');
    const inCart = _cart.get(product.id);
    const qty = inCart ? inCart.qty : 1;
    const resolved = resolvePrice(product, qty);
    const hasRule = resolved.source === 'rule' && resolved.price !== resolved.original;
    const cp = _customerParts.get(product.id);
    const lastPurchase = cp ? `${moment(cp.dateLastPurchased).fromNow(true)} ago · ${cp.lastQty} ${product.uomCode || ''}` : '<span class="text-slate-400">—</span>';

    const partInfo = _partData.get(product.id);
    const stock = qtyForLG(product.id);
    const leadTime = partInfo?.leadTime;
    const stockColor = stock > 0 ? '#059669' : '#94a3b8';
    const nb = findNextBreak(product, qty);
    const nbCell = (nb && nb.price < resolved.price)
        ? `<div style="font-size:10px;color:#b45309;font-weight:600;">↑ +${nb.atQty - qty} @ ${fmtMoney(nb.price)}</div>`
        : '';
    const pos = openPoSummary(product.id) || [];
    let poCellHtml = '<span class="text-slate-400">—</span>';
    if (pos.length > 0) {
        const totalRemaining = pos.reduce((s, p) => s + p.qtyRemaining, 0);
        const earliest = pos[0].dateScheduled ? formatDateShort(pos[0].dateScheduled) : '—';
        poCellHtml = `<span class="po-badge" data-po-pid="${product.id}"><strong>${totalRemaining.toLocaleString()}</strong> · ${earliest}${pos.length > 1 ? ` <span style="color:#64748b;">+${pos.length - 1}</span>` : ''}</span>`;
    }

    // Per-key cell builders — emitted in dataCols order so body cells
    // always line up with the header + colgroup built in renderListTable.
    const tdByKey = {
        fav:     () => `<td style="text-align:center;">${favBtnHtml(product.id)}</td>`,
        thumb:   () => `<td class="thumb-cell"><div class="thumb"><img class="product-img" data-product-id="${product.id}" src="${PLACEHOLDER_SVG}" alt=""></div></td>`,
        num:     () => `<td class="num-cell"><a class="row-link" href="#" data-open-product title="Open ${escapeHtml(product.num)} in the Product module">${escapeHtml(product.num)}</a></td>`,
        upc:     () => `<td title="${escapeHtml(product.upc || '')}">${escapeHtml(product.upc || '')}</td>`,
        desc:    () => `<td>${escapeHtml(product.description || '')}</td>`,
        catpath: () => {
            // Full category path(s). In a grouped row, show only the
            // path(s) under the current group's main category; otherwise
            // show every tagged path. Joined with " · " when several.
            const paths = productCatPaths(product);
            const shown = groupMain
                ? paths.filter(x => (x.mainId == null ? '~' : String(x.mainId)) === (groupMain.id == null ? '~' : String(groupMain.id)))
                : paths;
            const txt = (shown.length ? shown : paths).map(x => x.pathStr).join(' · ') || '—';
            return `<td class="catpath-cell" title="${escapeHtml(txt)}">${escapeHtml(txt)}</td>`;
        },
        last:    () => `<td>${lastPurchase}</td>`,
        stock:   () => `<td class="stock-badge" data-stock-pid="${product.id}" style="text-align:right;color:${stockColor};font-weight:600;cursor:help;">${stock.toLocaleString()}</td>`,
        lead:    () => `<td style="text-align:right;" title="${escapeHtml(partInfo?.vendorName || '')}">${leadTime != null ? leadTime + 'd' : '<span class="text-slate-400">—</span>'}</td>`,
        onorder: () => `<td>${poCellHtml}</td>`,
        price:   () => `<td class="price-cell ${hasRule ? 'has-rule' : ''}">${nbCell}${hasRule && _showOrigPrice ? `<span class="text-slate-400" style="text-decoration:line-through;font-weight:400;margin-right:6px;">${fmtMoney(resolved.original)}</span>` : ''}${fmtMoney(resolved.price)}</td>`,
    };
    tr.innerHTML = `
        ${dataCols.map(c => tdByKey[c.key] ? tdByKey[c.key]() : '').join('\n        ')}
        <td class="qty-cell">
            <div class="qty-stepper">
                <button data-step="-1">−</button>
                <input type="number" min="1" value="${qty}">
                <button data-step="1">+</button>
            </div>
        </td>
        <td class="action-cell"><button class="hdr-btn primary" data-add>Add</button></td>
    `;
    wireProductCard(tr, product);
    return tr;
}

// ── Orders view: rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Two DOM shapes, chosen at render time. A 9-column table cannot work on a
// phone: with table-layout:fixed every cell degrades to an ellipsis, so the
// mobile tier gets cards instead. CSS-only reflow is not an option either —
// the column widths come from a <colgroup> that fitListColumns() writes to
// in JS, and the header is position:sticky.
function ordersUseCards() {
    // Cards on ANY touch layout, tablets included — not phone-gated.
    //
    // The catalogue and this view answer different questions. There, list vs
    // tile is an explicit user choice, so a tablet needs the toggle and has
    // the width to honour it. Here there is no toggle, so the default is the
    // whole behaviour, and on a touch device that default should be cards:
    // a desktop table with 32px rows under a touch toolbar reads as a page
    // that only half-adapted.
    //
    // Cards are safe at tablet width because every .order-card rule lives in
    // the base stylesheet rather than inside a media block — width does not
    // gate them. The class check still matters: in MODE==='fishbowl' the body
    // has no `mobile-enabled` class, so the responsive CSS never applies and
    // cards would render unstyled in a narrow JxBrowser pane.
    //
    // Routed through isMobileViewport() so the tablet Desktop override also
    // switches this back to the table, which is the point of that button.
    return document.body.classList.contains('mobile-enabled') && isMobileViewport();
}

const ORDER_COLS = [
    // `key` doubles as the _colWidths key. The so_ prefix is NOT cosmetic:
    // _colWidths is a flat, persisted map SHARED with the product list, so an
    // unprefixed 'num' here would silently resize the catalogue's Part # too.
    { key: 'so_num',      label: 'SO #',        w: 110 },
    { key: 'so_status',   label: 'Status',      w: 120 },
    // Scheduled, not Created. When an order is due out is the operational
    // question; when it was keyed in is bookkeeping. Created is still in
    // the expanded detail for anyone who needs it.
    { key: 'so_sched',    label: 'Scheduled',   w: 110 },
    { key: 'so_customer', label: 'Customer',    w: 200 },
    { key: 'so_po',       label: 'Customer PO', w: 130 },
    { key: 'so_salesman', label: 'Salesman',    w: 110 },
    { key: 'so_issued',   label: 'Issued',      w: 100 },
    { key: 'so_total',    label: 'Total',       w: 110 },
    { key: 'so_chev',     label: '',            w: 40  },
];

function activeOrderCols() {
    // Customer is redundant when the list is already scoped to one.
    return ORDER_COLS.filter(c =>
        !(c.key === 'so_customer' && _ordersScope === 'customer' && _selectedCustomer));
}

function orderStatusPill(o) {
    return `<span class="so-status ${o.statusClass}">${escapeHtml(o.statusLabel)}</span>`;
}

function renderOrdersTable(rows) {
    const cols = activeOrderCols();
    const table = document.createElement('table');
    table.className = 'list-table';
    table.id = 'ordersTable';

    const cg = document.createElement('colgroup');
    cols.forEach(c => {
        const col = document.createElement('col');
        col.setAttribute('data-col', c.key);
        // Honour a width the user dragged to previously. _colWidths is the
        // same persisted map the product list uses, which is exactly why
        // these keys are so_-prefixed.
        col.setAttribute('data-desired-width', String(_colWidths[c.key] ?? c.w));
        cg.appendChild(col);
    });
    table.appendChild(cg);

    const thead = document.createElement('thead');
    const htr = document.createElement('tr');
    cols.forEach(c => {
        const th = document.createElement('th');
        th.setAttribute('data-col', c.key);
        if (c.key === 'so_total') th.style.textAlign = 'right';
        if (c.key === 'so_chev') { htr.appendChild(th); return; }
        th.className = 'sortable';
        const arrow = _ordersSort.key === c.key
            ? `<span class="arrow">${_ordersSort.dir === 1 ? '▲' : '▼'}</span>` : '';
        th.innerHTML = escapeHtml(c.label) + ' ' + arrow;
        th.addEventListener('click', e => {
            // The resize strip swallows mousedown but the click still
            // bubbles — don't sort when the user was dragging an edge.
            if (e.target.classList && e.target.classList.contains('col-resizer')) return;
            toggleOrdersSort(c.key);
        });
        htr.appendChild(th);
    });
    thead.appendChild(htr);
    table.appendChild(thead);
    // Drag-to-resize, same primitive the product list uses. It writes the
    // dragged width to _colWidths[data-col] and calls saveState(), so the
    // so_ prefix on these keys is what stops an orders column resize from
    // silently resizing a catalogue column.
    setTimeout(() => {
        thead.querySelectorAll('th[data-col]').forEach(th => attachColumnResizer(th));
    }, 0);

    const tbody = document.createElement('tbody');
    rows.forEach(o => {
        const tr = document.createElement('tr');
        tr.className = 'order-row' + (_ordersExpanded === o.id ? ' expanded' : '');
        tr.setAttribute('data-soid', String(o.id));
        const cell = {
            so_num:      () => `<td class="num-cell"><strong>${escapeHtml(o.num)}</strong></td>`,
            so_status:   () => `<td data-status-tip="1">${orderStatusPill(o)}</td>`,
            so_sched:    () => `<td title="Scheduled ship date">${escapeHtml(o.dateScheduled ? formatDateShort(o.dateScheduled) : '—')}</td>`,
            so_customer: () => `<td>${escapeHtml(o.customerName)}</td>`,
            so_po:       () => `<td>${escapeHtml(o.customerPO)}</td>`,
            so_salesman: () => `<td>${escapeHtml(o.salesman)}</td>`,
            so_issued:   () => `<td>${escapeHtml(o.dateIssued ? formatDateShort(o.dateIssued) : '—')}</td>`,
            so_total:    () => `<td class="total-cell">${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(o.totalPrice))}</td>`,
            so_chev:     () => `<td><svg class="so-chev" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M9 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg></td>`,
        };
        tr.innerHTML = cols.map(c => (cell[c.key] || (() => '<td></td>'))()).join('');
        // The per-pick / per-ship breakdown behind the derived status.
        const stCell = tr.querySelector('[data-status-tip]');
        if (stCell && o.statusTip && o.statusTip !== o.statusLabel) {
            stCell.addEventListener('mouseenter', e => showTooltip(e, escapeHtml(o.statusTip).replace(/\n/g, '<br>')));
            stCell.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTooltip);
        }
        tr.addEventListener('click', () => toggleOrderDetail(o.id));
        tbody.appendChild(tr);

        if (_ordersExpanded === o.id) tbody.appendChild(buildDetailRow(o, cols.length));
    });
    table.appendChild(tbody);
    return table;
}

// The expanded detail, as a full-width row. The cell spans EVERY column so
// the <colgroup> does not constrain it — which is why the contents below are
// divs and not a nested <table> sharing that geometry.
function buildDetailRow(o, colCount) {
    const tr = document.createElement('tr');
    tr.className = 'so-detail-row';
    const td = document.createElement('td');
    td.className = 'so-detail-cell';
    td.colSpan = colCount;
    td.appendChild(buildDetailBlock(o));
    tr.appendChild(td);
    return tr;
}

function renderOrderCards(rows) {
    const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
    const scoped = _ordersScope === 'customer' && _selectedCustomer;
    rows.forEach(o => {
        const card = document.createElement('div');
        card.className = 'order-card' + (_ordersExpanded === o.id ? ' expanded' : '');
        card.setAttribute('data-soid', String(o.id));
        // Scheduled date leads, matching the desktop column. Prefixed so a
        // bare date on a card can't be mistaken for the created date.
        const meta = [o.dateScheduled ? 'Sched ' + formatDateShort(o.dateScheduled) : '',
                      o.customerPO ? 'PO ' + o.customerPO : '',
                      o.salesman].filter(Boolean).join(' · ');
        card.innerHTML = `
            <div class="oc-body">
                <div class="oc-top"><span class="oc-num">${escapeHtml(o.num)}</span>${orderStatusPill(o)}</div>
                ${scoped ? '' : `<div class="oc-cust">${escapeHtml(o.customerName)}</div>`}
                <div class="oc-meta">${escapeHtml(meta)}</div>
            </div>
            <div class="oc-right">
                <span class="oc-total">${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(o.totalPrice))}</span>
                <svg class="so-chev" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M9 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
            </div>`;
        card.addEventListener('click', () => toggleOrderDetail(o.id));
        frag.appendChild(card);
        if (_ordersExpanded === o.id) {
            const wrap = document.createElement('div');
            wrap.className = 'order-card-detail';
            wrap.appendChild(buildDetailBlock(o));
            frag.appendChild(wrap);
        }
    });
    return frag;
}

// Shared detail body for both tiers. Renders synchronously with a spinner,
// then fills the line list once loadSoLines() resolves — so expanding is
// instant even when the query is not.
function buildDetailBlock(o) {
    const box = document.createElement('div');
    box.className = 'so-detail';
    box.addEventListener('click', e => e.stopPropagation());   // don't collapse on inner clicks

    const kv = [
        ['Customer', o.customerName + (o.customerNum ? ' (' + o.customerNum + ')' : '')],
        ['Customer PO', o.customerPO || '—'],
        ['Scheduled', o.dateScheduled ? formatDateShort(o.dateScheduled) : '—'],
        ['Created', formatDateShort(o.dateCreated)],
        ['Issued', o.dateIssued ? formatDateShort(o.dateIssued) : '—'],
        ['Salesman', o.salesman || '—'],
        ['Location group', o.lgName || '—'],
        ['SO status', o.statusName || '—'],
    ].map(([k, v]) => `<div>${escapeHtml(k)}: <b>${escapeHtml(String(v))}</b></div>`).join('');

    box.innerHTML =
        `<div class="sd-kv">${kv}</div>` +
        `<div class="sd-head">Line items</div>` +
        `<div class="sd-lines" data-lines><div class="spinner"></div></div>` +
        `<div class="sd-totals">
            <span>Subtotal ${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(o.subTotal))}</span>
            <span>Tax ${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(o.totalTax))}</span>
            <span>Total <b>${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(o.totalPrice))}</b></span>
         </div>` +
        // openModule is fishbowl-host only — omit the button entirely in
        // portal/standalone rather than render one that only errors.
        (typeof openModule === 'function'
            ? `<div class="sd-actions"><button class="hdr-btn" data-open-so>Open in Fishbowl</button></div>`
            : '');

    const openBtn = box.querySelector('[data-open-so]');
    if (openBtn) {
        openBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
            try { openModule('Sales Order', o.num); }
            catch (e) { showToast('Could not open the Sales Order module: ' + e, 'error', 5000); }
        });
    }

    const host = box.querySelector('[data-lines]');
    loadSoLines(o.id)
        .then(lines => { host.innerHTML = renderSoLinesHtml(lines); })
        .catch(err => {
            // Fails inside the block — never collapse the row out from under
            // the user, and never blank the list behind it.
            host.innerHTML = `<div class="sd-err">Could not load line items: ${escapeHtml((err && err.message) || String(err))}</div>`
                           + `<button class="hdr-btn" data-retry>Retry</button>`;
            const rb = host.querySelector('[data-retry]');
            if (rb) rb.addEventListener('click', () => {
                _soLines.delete(Number(o.id));
                host.innerHTML = '<div class="spinner"></div>';
                loadSoLines(o.id)
                    .then(ls => { host.innerHTML = renderSoLinesHtml(ls); })
                    .catch(e2 => { host.innerHTML = `<div class="sd-err">${escapeHtml((e2 && e2.message) || String(e2))}</div>`; });
            });
        });
    return box;
}

function renderSoLinesHtml(lines) {
    if (!lines.length) return '<div class="oc-meta">This order has no line items.</div>';
    const head =
        `<div class="sd-line sd-line-head">
            <div class="sd-c-n">#</div><div class="sd-c-prod">Product</div>
            <div class="sd-c-desc">Description</div>
            <div class="sd-c-qty sd-r">Ord / Pick / Ful</div>
            <div class="sd-c-price sd-r">Unit</div>
            <div class="sd-c-total sd-r">Total</div>
            <div class="sd-c-status">Status</div>
         </div>`;
    const body = lines.map(l => {
        // Non-sale rows (discount, subtotal, note, shipping…) are supporting
        // detail, not things ordered — de-emphasise rather than hide, so the
        // order still adds up on screen.
        const nonSale = l.typeId !== SOITEM_TYPE_SALE;
        // Each figure carries its own label, hidden on desktop (the column
        // header says it) and revealed on a phone where the header is not
        // rendered — otherwise "5 / 2 / 0" means nothing on its own.
        const qty = `<span class="qty-lbl">Ord </span>${escapeHtml(formatQtyShort(l.qtyOrdered))}`
                  + ` / <span class="qty-lbl">Pick </span>${escapeHtml(formatQtyShort(l.qtyPicked))}`
                  + ` / <span class="qty-lbl">Ful </span>${escapeHtml(formatQtyShort(l.qtyFulfilled))}`;
        return `<div class="sd-line${nonSale ? ' sd-nonsale' : ''}">
            <div class="sd-c-n">${l.line || ''}</div>
            <div class="sd-c-prod"><strong>${escapeHtml(l.productNum)}</strong>${nonSale ? ' <span class="oc-meta">(' + escapeHtml(l.typeName) + ')</span>' : ''}</div>
            <div class="sd-c-desc">${escapeHtml(l.description)}</div>
            <div class="sd-c-qty sd-r" title="Ordered / Picked / Fulfilled">${qty}${l.uomCode ? ' ' + escapeHtml(l.uomCode) : ''}</div>
            <div class="sd-c-price sd-r">${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(l.unitPrice))}</div>
            <div class="sd-c-total sd-r">${escapeHtml(fmtMoney(l.totalPrice))}</div>
            <div class="sd-c-status">${escapeHtml(l.statusName)}</div>
        </div>`;
    }).join('');
    return head + body;
}

// Trim trailing zeros — soitem quantities are decimal(28,9), so a raw value
// reads as "1.000000000" on every line.
function formatQtyShort(n) {
    const v = Number(n) || 0;
    return Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : String(parseFloat(v.toFixed(4)));
}

function toggleOrderDetail(soId) {
    _ordersExpanded = (_ordersExpanded === soId) ? null : soId;
    renderOrders();
}

function toggleOrdersSort(key) {
    if (_ordersSort.key === key) _ordersSort.dir = -_ordersSort.dir;
    else _ordersSort = { key, dir: key === 'so_sched' || key === 'so_issued' || key === 'so_total' ? -1 : 1 };
    sortOrders();
    renderOrders();
}

function renderOrders() {
    const host = document.getElementById('ordersHost');
    if (!host) return;
    renderOrdersToolbarState();

    if (_ordersLoading) { host.innerHTML = '<div class="spinner"></div>'; return; }
    if (_ordersError) {
        host.innerHTML =
            '<div style="text-align:center; padding:32px 16px;">'
          + '<div style="font-size:13px; color:#b91c1c; margin-bottom:10px;">Could not load sales orders.</div>'
          + '<div style="font-size:11px; color:#94a3b8; margin-bottom:14px;">' + escapeHtml(_ordersError) + '</div>'
          + '<button class="hdr-btn" onclick="loadOrders()">Retry</button></div>';
        return;
    }
    if (!_ordersFiltered.length) {
        host.innerHTML = '<div style="text-align:center; padding:48px 16px; font-size:13px; color:#94a3b8; font-style:italic;">'
                       + (_orders.length ? 'No orders match the search.' : 'No sales orders match the current filters.')
                       + '</div>';
        renderOrdersFooter();
        return;
    }

    host.innerHTML = '';
    if (ordersUseCards()) {
        host.appendChild(renderOrderCards(_ordersFiltered));
    } else {
        const table = renderOrdersTable(_ordersFiltered);
        host.appendChild(table);
        fitListColumns(table);
        // NOTE: observeListTableResize() is deliberately NOT called here — it
        // keeps a single module-level observer and disconnecting the product
        // list's would break the catalogue. setAppView() re-renders instead.
    }
    renderOrdersFooter();
}

function renderOrdersFooter() {
    const foot = document.getElementById('ordersFooter');
    if (!foot) return;
    // Only offer "load more" when the query actually hit the cap.
    if (!_ordersLoading && _orders.length >= _ordersLimit) {
        foot.innerHTML = `<div style="text-align:center; padding:12px;">
            <button class="hdr-btn" onclick="loadMoreOrders()">Load more (showing ${_orders.length})</button></div>`;
    } else {
        foot.innerHTML = '';
    }
}

function loadMoreOrders() { _ordersLimit += 300; loadOrders(); }

function renderOrdersToolbarState() {
    // The customer control is the relocated #cust-ms itself, so its label is
    // maintained by updateMSTrigger('cust') — nothing to do here for it.
    // Whether the list is scoped TO that customer, or showing everyone.
    const scopeBtn = document.getElementById('ordersScopeBtn');
    const scopeLbl = document.getElementById('ordersScopeBtnLabel');
    if (scopeBtn) {
        const scoped = _ordersScope === 'customer' && _selectedCustomer;
        if (scopeLbl) scopeLbl.textContent = scoped ? 'This customer' : 'All customers';
        scopeBtn.classList.toggle('active', !!scoped);
        scopeBtn.disabled = !_selectedCustomer;
        scopeBtn.title = _selectedCustomer
            ? (scoped ? 'Showing only ' + _selectedCustomer.name + ' — click for all customers'
                      : 'Showing all customers — click to scope to ' + _selectedCustomer.name)
            : 'Choose a customer first to scope this list';
    }
    // Filter button labels — each shows its own current value, so the row
    // still reads at a glance on desktop even though the controls are
    // popovers rather than selects.
    const me = currentFbUsername();
    if (_ordersSalesman === 'me' && !me) _ordersSalesman = '';   // identity never resolved
    setBtnLabel('ordersSalesmanBtnLabel',
        _ordersSalesman === 'me' ? 'My sales'
        : _ordersSalesman ? _ordersSalesman : 'All salesmen');
    setBtnLabel('ordersRangeBtnLabel',
        _ordersRange === 0 ? 'All time'
        : _ordersRange === 365 ? 'Last 12 months'
        : 'Last ' + _ordersRange + ' days');
    setBtnLabel('ordersStatusBtnLabel',
        _ordersStatusSet === 'open' ? 'Open orders' : 'All statuses');
    const salesBtn = document.getElementById('ordersSalesmanBtn');
    if (salesBtn) salesBtn.classList.toggle('active', _ordersSalesman !== '');
    const statusBtn = document.getElementById('ordersStatusBtn');
    if (statusBtn) statusBtn.classList.toggle('active', _ordersStatusSet === 'open');

    const line = document.getElementById('ordersStatusLine');
    if (line) line.innerHTML = ordersStatusText();
}

function setBtnLabel(id, text) {
    const el = document.getElementById(id);
