    if (el) el.textContent = text;
}

function onOrdersSalesmanChange(v) {
    _ordersSalesman = v == null ? '' : String(v);
    _ordersExpanded = null;
    loadOrders();
}

function customerLabelShort(c) {
    const n = (c && c.name) || '';
    return n.length > 22 ? n.slice(0, 21) + '…' : n;
}

// ── Orders filter popover ────────────────────────────────────────────
// Replaces three native <select>s. On a phone a select shrunk to fit reads
// as a squashed desktop control and opens the OS picker; this gives a
// proper tap target per option and collapses to a single icon.
const _ordersMenuDefs = {
    salesman: {
        get: () => _ordersSalesman,
        set: v => onOrdersSalesmanChange(v),
        items: () => {
            const me = currentFbUsername();
            const out = [];
            // Only offer "My sales" when the identity actually resolves —
            // otherwise it silently means everyone.
            if (me) out.push({ value: 'me', label: 'My sales', sub: me });
            out.push({ value: '', label: 'All salesmen' });
            for (const s of _salesmen) {
                if (me && s.userName === me) continue;
                out.push({ value: s.userName, label: s.userName, sub: s.count + ' orders' });
            }
            return out;
        },
    },
    range: {
        get: () => String(_ordersRange),
        set: v => onOrdersRangeChange(v),
        items: () => ([
            { value: '30',  label: 'Last 30 days' },
            { value: '90',  label: 'Last 90 days' },
            { value: '365', label: 'Last 12 months' },
            { value: '0',   label: 'All time' },
        ]),
    },
    status: {
        get: () => _ordersStatusSet,
        set: v => onOrdersStatusChange(v),
        items: () => ([
            { value: 'open', label: 'Open orders', sub: 'Estimate, Issued, In Progress' },
            { value: 'all',  label: 'All statuses', sub: 'Includes fulfilled and cancelled' },
        ]),
    },
};
let _ordersMenuOpen = null;

function closeOrdersMenu() {
    const m = document.getElementById('ordersMenu');
    if (m) m.classList.remove('open');
    _ordersMenuOpen = null;
}

function openOrdersMenu(kind, anchor) {
    const m = document.getElementById('ordersMenu');
    const def = _ordersMenuDefs[kind];
    if (!m || !def) return;
    if (_ordersMenuOpen === kind) { closeOrdersMenu(); return; }
    closeMS();
    const cur = def.get();
    m.innerHTML = def.items().map(it =>
        `<button type="button" class="om-item${String(it.value) === String(cur) ? ' active' : ''}"
                 data-val="${escapeHtml(String(it.value))}">
            <span class="om-check">${String(it.value) === String(cur) ? '✓' : ''}</span>
            <span class="om-body"><span class="om-lbl">${escapeHtml(it.label)}</span>${
                it.sub ? `<span class="om-sub">${escapeHtml(it.sub)}</span>` : ''}</span>
         </button>`).join('');
    m.querySelectorAll('.om-item').forEach(b => {
        b.addEventListener('click', () => {
            const v = b.getAttribute('data-val');
            closeOrdersMenu();
            def.set(v);
        });
    });

    // Anchor under the button, then pull back inside the viewport. On a
    // phone the button can sit near the right edge, so a naive left-align
    // would push the menu off screen.
    m.classList.add('open');
    const r = anchor.getBoundingClientRect();
    const mw = m.offsetWidth || 220;
    let left = r.left;
    if (left + mw > window.innerWidth - 8) left = window.innerWidth - mw - 8;
    if (left < 8) left = 8;
    m.style.left = left + 'px';
    m.style.top  = (r.bottom + 4) + 'px';
    _ordersMenuOpen = kind;
}

// The customer picker is a single shared control (#cust-ms). Move it into
// whichever view is on screen rather than duplicating it — moving a node
// preserves its listeners, so the picker keeps working untouched.
let _custMsHome = null;
function relocateCustomerPicker(toOrders) {
    const ms = document.getElementById('cust-ms');
    if (!ms) return;
    if (!_custMsHome) _custMsHome = { parent: ms.parentNode, next: ms.nextSibling };
    if (toOrders) {
        const host = document.getElementById('ordersCustHost');
        if (host && ms.parentNode !== host) host.appendChild(ms);
    } else if (_custMsHome.parent && ms.parentNode !== _custMsHome.parent) {
        _custMsHome.parent.insertBefore(ms, _custMsHome.next);
    }
}

function ordersStatusText() {
    if (_ordersLoading) return 'Loading orders…';
    if (_ordersError)   return '<span style="color:#b91c1c;">Load failed</span>';
    const scoped = _ordersScope === 'customer' && _selectedCustomer;
    const me = currentFbUsername();
    const who = _ordersSalesman === 'me' ? (me ? me + ' (me)' : 'all salesmen')
              : _ordersSalesman ? _ordersSalesman
              : 'all salesmen';
    const bits = [
        `<strong class="text-slate-700">${_ordersFiltered.length}</strong> order${_ordersFiltered.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`,
        escapeHtml(who),
        scoped ? escapeHtml(_selectedCustomer.name) : 'all customers',
        _ordersRange ? 'last ' + _ordersRange + ' days' : 'all time',
        _ordersStatusSet === 'open' ? 'open only' : 'all statuses',
    ];
    return '<span>' + bits.join(' <span class="sep">·</span> ') + '</span>';
}

function toggleOrdersScope() {
    if (!_selectedCustomer) return;
    _ordersScope = _ordersScope === 'customer' ? 'all' : 'customer';
    _ordersExpanded = null;
    loadOrders();
}

function onOrdersRangeChange(v) { _ordersRange = Number(v) || 0; _ordersExpanded = null; loadOrders(); }
function onOrdersStatusChange(v) { _ordersStatusSet = v === 'all' ? 'all' : 'open'; _ordersExpanded = null; loadOrders(); }

// ── List-column selector panel (mirrors PurchaseOrderSummary) ────────
// Checkbox toggles visibility; drag the handle to reorder. Both re-render
// the active list view immediately and persist via saveState().
function buildColPanel() {
    const list = document.getElementById('colList');
    if (!list) return;
    list.innerHTML = '';
    const labelByKey = {};
    LIST_COL_DEFS.forEach(d => { labelByKey[d.key] = d.label; });
    _listCols.forEach((col, i) => {
        const div = document.createElement('div');
        div.className = 'col-row'; div.draggable = true; div.dataset.idx = i;
        const handle = document.createElement('span'); handle.className = 'col-drag-handle';
        handle.innerHTML = '<svg width="12" height="10" viewBox="0 0 12 10" fill="currentColor"><rect y="0" width="12" height="2" rx="1"/><rect y="4" width="12" height="2" rx="1"/><rect y="8" width="12" height="2" rx="1"/></svg>';
        const cb = document.createElement('input'); cb.type = 'checkbox'; cb.checked = col.vis; cb.id = 'qo_cv_' + col.key;
        cb.addEventListener('change', () => { col.vis = cb.checked; renderProducts(); saveState(); });
        const lbl = document.createElement('label'); lbl.htmlFor = cb.id; lbl.textContent = labelByKey[col.key] || col.key;
        div.appendChild(handle); div.appendChild(cb); div.appendChild(lbl);
        div.addEventListener('dragstart', e => { _colDragIdx = i; setTimeout(() => div.classList.add('dragging'), 0); e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move'; });
        div.addEventListener('dragend',   () => { _colDragIdx = null; div.classList.remove('dragging'); list.querySelectorAll('.col-row').forEach(r => r.classList.remove('drag-over')); });
        div.addEventListener('dragover',  e => { e.preventDefault(); e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'move'; list.querySelectorAll('.col-row').forEach(r => r.classList.remove('drag-over')); if (_colDragIdx !== null && _colDragIdx !== i) div.classList.add('drag-over'); });
        div.addEventListener('dragleave', () => div.classList.remove('drag-over'));
        div.addEventListener('drop', e => {
            e.preventDefault(); div.classList.remove('drag-over');
            const from = _colDragIdx;
            if (from === null || from === i) return;
            const [moved] = _listCols.splice(from, 1); _listCols.splice(i, 0, moved);
            buildColPanel(); renderProducts(); saveState();
        });
        list.appendChild(div);
    });
}

function toggleColPanel() {
    const panel = document.getElementById('colPanel');
    if (!panel) return;
    if (panel.classList.contains('hidden')) buildColPanel();
    panel.classList.toggle('hidden');
}

function wireProductCard(root, product) {
    const stepperInput = root.querySelector('.qty-stepper input');
    const minus = root.querySelector('[data-step="-1"]');
    const plus  = root.querySelector('[data-step="1"]');
    const addBtn = root.querySelector('[data-add]');
    const priceEl = root.querySelector('.price, .price-cell');

    function getQty() { return Math.max(1, parseInt(stepperInput.value, 10) || 1); }
    function refreshPrice() {
        const q = getQty();
        const r = resolvePrice(product, q);
        const hasRule = r.source === 'rule' && r.price !== r.original;
        // Next-break reflects the COMMITTED cart quantity, not the tile's
        // transient to-add field — "buy N more" only makes sense against
        // what's already in the order. Falls back to the field qty when the
        // product isn't in the cart yet. findNextBreak returns null when
        // the base qty is at/above every remaining break, so a cart qty of
        // 20 correctly hides a "+19 to reach 20" hint.
        const nbBaseQty = _cart.has(product.id) ? _cart.get(product.id).qty : q;
        const nb = findNextBreak(product, nbBaseQty);
        const nbActive = !!nb;

        if (DEBUG) {
            qoDebug(`refreshPrice  ${product.num}  qty=${q}  price=${r.price}  source=${r.source}  t2=${r.t2winner?.name || '—'}  t3=${r.t3winner?.name || '—'}`);
        }

        if (!priceEl) {
            if (DEBUG) console.warn('refreshPrice: priceEl missing on', root);
            return;
        }

        if (root.classList.contains('product-tile')) {
            // ── Tile view ────────────────────────────────────────────────
            priceEl.classList.toggle('has-rule', hasRule);
            priceEl.textContent = fmtMoney(r.price);

            // Strike-through "list" price — sits BEFORE the .price span so
            // the visual reads "$10.00  $8.00" (list on left, customer on
            // right). May not exist in the DOM yet if the initial render
            // had no rule applied.
            let orig = priceEl.parentElement.querySelector('.price-orig');
            if (hasRule && _showOrigPrice) {
                if (!orig) {
                    orig = document.createElement('span');
                    orig.className = 'price-orig';
                    priceEl.insertAdjacentElement('beforebegin', orig);
                }
                orig.textContent = fmtMoney(r.original);
            } else if (orig) {
                orig.remove();
            }

            // Next-break suggestion — inserted directly ABOVE the .price-row
            // so the price stays pinned to the bottom (via price-row's
            // margin-top:auto). When the next-break appears/disappears, the
            // price itself doesn't move; the flex slack above absorbs the
            // height change instead.
            const body = root.querySelector('.body');
            const priceRow = body?.querySelector('.price-row');
            let nbEl = body?.querySelector('.next-break');
            if (nbActive) {
                const need = nb.atQty - nbBaseQty;
                const title = `Buy ${need} more to reach the ${nb.atQty}-unit price tier`;
                const text  = `↑ +${need} for ${fmtMoney(nb.price)} ea`;
                if (!nbEl) {
                    nbEl = document.createElement('div');
                    nbEl.className = 'next-break';
                    nbEl.style.cssText = 'font-size:11px;color:#b45309;font-weight:600;cursor:help;';
                    if (priceRow) priceRow.insertAdjacentElement('beforebegin', nbEl);
                    else body.appendChild(nbEl);
                }
                nbEl.title = title;
                nbEl.textContent = text;
            } else if (nbEl) {
                nbEl.remove();
            }
        } else {
            // ── List views (priceEl is the <td class="price-cell">) ─────
            priceEl.classList.toggle('has-rule', hasRule);
            const strike = (hasRule && _showOrigPrice)
                ? `<span class="text-slate-400" style="text-decoration:line-through;font-weight:400;margin-right:6px;">${fmtMoney(r.original)}</span>`
                : '';
            const nbCell = nbActive
                ? `<div style="font-size:10px;color:#b45309;font-weight:600;">↑ +${nb.atQty - nbBaseQty} @ ${fmtMoney(nb.price)}</div>`
                : '';
            priceEl.innerHTML = nbCell + strike + fmtMoney(r.price);
        }
    }

    // Stepper +/- update instantly; typed input debounces so we don't
    // re-resolve every keystroke (which on a wide cart can fire several
    // expensive rule walks per second).
    //
    // Two interaction modes:
    //   - Desktop: +/- modifies the LOCAL qty input (the "to-add"
    //     amount). User clicks the Add button to commit that qty
    //     into the cart. Stepper does NOT touch the cart directly.
    //   - Mobile (mobile-enabled body + narrow viewport): the stepper
    //     IS the cart row. +/- modifies the cart immediately, the
    //     input shows the current cart qty (0 if not added).
    const debouncedRefresh = debounce(refreshPrice, 300);
    const cartQty = () => _cart.has(product.id) ? _cart.get(product.id).qty : 0;
    const isMobileStepper = () => isMobileViewport();
    minus && minus.addEventListener('click', () => {
        if (isMobileStepper()) {
            const cur = cartQty();
            if (cur > 0) setCartQty(product.id, cur - 1);
            return;
        }
        stepperInput.value = Math.max(1, getQty() - 1);
        refreshPrice();
    });
    plus && plus.addEventListener('click', () => {
        if (isMobileStepper()) {
            const cur = cartQty();
            if (cur > 0) setCartQty(product.id, cur + 1);
            else addToCart(product, 1);
            return;
        }
        stepperInput.value = getQty() + 1;
        refreshPrice();
    });
    if (stepperInput) {
        stepperInput.addEventListener('input',  () => {
            if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`tile input  ${product.num}  raw="${stepperInput.value}"`);
            debouncedRefresh();
        });
        stepperInput.addEventListener('change', () => {
            if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`tile change ${product.num}  raw="${stepperInput.value}"`);
            if (isMobileStepper()) {
                // Mobile: commit input value as cart qty. Empty/0 →
                // remove from cart; positive → add or set.
                const v = parseInt(stepperInput.value, 10);
                if (!v || v < 1) {
                    if (_cart.has(product.id)) removeFromCart(product.id);
                    else stepperInput.value = '0';
                } else if (_cart.has(product.id)) {
                    setCartQty(product.id, v);
                } else {
                    addToCart(product, v);
                }
                return;
            }
            refreshPrice();
        });
        stepperInput.addEventListener('blur', () => {
            if (DEBUG) qoDebug(`tile blur   ${product.num}  raw="${stepperInput.value}"`);
            refreshPrice();
        });
        stepperInput.addEventListener('focus', e => e.target.select());
        stepperInput.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
            if (e.key === 'Enter') {
                e.preventDefault();
                if (isMobileStepper()) {
                    stepperInput.blur();   // triggers change → commit
                    return;
                }
                refreshPrice();              // commit any debounced value first
                if (addBtn) addBtn.click();
            }
        });
    }

    if (priceEl) {
        priceEl.addEventListener('mouseover', e => showTooltip(e, priceBreakdownTooltip(product, getQty())));
        priceEl.addEventListener('mousemove', e => showTooltip(e, priceBreakdownTooltip(product, getQty())));
        priceEl.addEventListener('mouseout',  () => hideTooltip());
    }

    // Product-number link → opens the Product module in Fishbowl. Wired
    // via addEventListener (mirrors Part/PartActivity.htm L1081) rather
    // than inline onclick, which appeared to silently no-op in some
    // JxBrowser contexts.
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-open-product]').forEach(a => {
        a.addEventListener('click', e => {
            e.preventDefault();
            openProduct(product.num);
        });
    });

    // PO badge — rich tooltip with vendor + LG + per-PO breakdown,
    // matching the .qo-tooltip style of the price breakdown.
    const poEl = root.querySelector('.po-badge[data-po-pid]');
    if (poEl) {
        const pos = openPoSummary(product.id) || [];
        poEl.addEventListener('mouseover', e => showTooltip(e, poTooltipHtml(pos)));
        poEl.addEventListener('mousemove', e => showTooltip(e, poTooltipHtml(pos)));
        poEl.addEventListener('mouseout',  () => hideTooltip());
    }

    // Stock badge — per-LG qty breakdown. Built lazily on hover so it
    // reflects the latest cached inventory (which loads after first paint).
    root.querySelectorAll('.stock-badge[data-stock-pid]').forEach(el => {
        el.addEventListener('mouseover', e => showTooltip(e, stockTooltipHtml(product.id)));
        el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => showTooltip(e, stockTooltipHtml(product.id)));
        el.addEventListener('mouseout',  () => hideTooltip());
    });

    addBtn && addBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        addToCart(product, getQty());
    });

    // UOM-group dropdown — only present on tiles whose product is in a
    // multi-member part-group AND grouping is on. Changing the value
    // re-renders this tile against the alternative product (price,
    // stock, last-purchase, favourite state, cart badge all rebind).
    // Stop propagation so the dropdown click doesn't bubble up to any
    // outer tile handlers.
    const uomSelect = root.querySelector('.uom-select[data-uom-group-pid]');
    if (uomSelect) {
        uomSelect.addEventListener('click', e => e.stopPropagation());
        uomSelect.addEventListener('change', e => {
            e.stopPropagation();
            const newPid = parseInt(uomSelect.value, 10);
            if (!isNaN(newPid) && newPid !== product.id) {
                swapTileToProduct(root, newPid);
            }
        });
    }
}

// ── Lazy image loading (IntersectionObserver + batch query) ──────────
// Strategy: every product img renders with PLACEHOLDER_SVG as its default
// src plus a data-product-id attribute. On scroll-into-view, the
// IntersectionObserver collects product IDs, debounces them into a single
// batch SQL query against `image` (tableName='product', recordId IN …),
// caches the results in _thumbCache, and swaps the img src to the
// returned base64. Products with no row in the image table keep the
// placeholder (cache stores `null` so we don't re-query).
let _imgObserver = null;
let _pendingThumbIds = new Set();
let _pendingThumbImgs = new Map(); // productId -> [img elements waiting for this product]
let _thumbBatchTimer = null;

function armLazyImages(root) {
    const imgs = root.querySelectorAll('img.product-img[data-product-id]');
    if (!imgs.length) return;

    // First, apply anything already cached so we don't wait on the IO.
    imgs.forEach(img => {
        const pid = parseInt(img.dataset.productId, 10);
        if (_thumbCache.has(pid)) applyThumb(img, _thumbCache.get(pid));
    });

    if (!_lazyImages) {
        imgs.forEach(img => {
            const pid = parseInt(img.dataset.productId, 10);
            if (!_thumbCache.has(pid)) queueThumbFetch(pid, img);
        });
        flushThumbBatch();
        return;
    }

    if (!_imgObserver) {
        _imgObserver = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
            for (const e of entries) {
                if (!e.isIntersecting) continue;
                const img = e.target;
                const pid = parseInt(img.dataset.productId, 10);
                _imgObserver.unobserve(img);
                if (_thumbCache.has(pid)) {
                    applyThumb(img, _thumbCache.get(pid));
                } else {
                    queueThumbFetch(pid, img);
                }
            }
            if (_pendingThumbIds.size > 0) scheduleThumbFlush();
        }, { rootMargin: '120px' });
    }

    imgs.forEach(img => {
        const pid = parseInt(img.dataset.productId, 10);
        if (!_thumbCache.has(pid)) _imgObserver.observe(img);
    });
}

function queueThumbFetch(pid, img) {
    _pendingThumbIds.add(pid);
    if (!_pendingThumbImgs.has(pid)) _pendingThumbImgs.set(pid, []);
    _pendingThumbImgs.get(pid).push(img);
}

function scheduleThumbFlush() {
    if (_thumbBatchTimer) return;
    _thumbBatchTimer = setTimeout(() => { _thumbBatchTimer = null; flushThumbBatch(); }, 80);
}

async function flushThumbBatch() {
    if (_pendingThumbIds.size === 0) return;
    const ids = [..._pendingThumbIds];
    const imgsByPid = _pendingThumbImgs;
    _pendingThumbIds = new Set();
    _pendingThumbImgs = new Map();
    // Chunk to avoid blowing past SQL parameter limits on huge selections
    const CHUNK = 80;
    for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i += CHUNK) {
        const slice = ids.slice(i, i + CHUNK);
        try {
            const rows = await qp(`
                SELECT recordid, imagethumbnail
                FROM image
                WHERE tablename = 'product' AND recordid IN (${slice.join(',')})
            `);
            const found = new Map();
            for (const r of rows) found.set(r.recordid, r.imagethumbnail);
            for (const pid of slice) {
                const data = found.has(pid) ? found.get(pid) : null;
                _thumbCache.set(pid, data);
                const waiting = imgsByPid.get(pid) || [];
                for (const img of waiting) applyThumb(img, data);
            }
        } catch (e) {
            console.warn('Thumbnail batch fetch failed:', e);
        }
    }
}

function applyThumb(img, data) {
    if (!data) return; // no image — leave placeholder visible
    const s = String(data);
    // imageThumbnail content is usually raw base64; some installs prefix
    // with "data:image/...;base64,". Honour either shape.
    img.src = s.startsWith('data:') ? s : 'data:image/png;base64,' + s;
}

// ── Pagination ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function renderPagination() {
    const el = document.getElementById('pagination');
    if (!el) return;
    // Count of paginated items: products (tile / ungrouped list) or
    // expanded rows (grouped list). Set by renderProducts each paint.
    const n = _pageItemCount || _filteredProducts.length;
    if (_pageSize >= 9999 || n <= _pageSize) {
        el.innerHTML = '';
        return;
    }
    const total = Math.ceil(n / _pageSize);
    const noun = (_viewMode !== 'tile' && _groupByTree) ? 'rows' : 'products';
    el.innerHTML = `
        <button class="hdr-btn" ${_pageIndex === 0 ? 'disabled' : ''} onclick="goToPage(${_pageIndex - 1})">◂ Prev</button>
        <span>Page <strong>${_pageIndex + 1}</strong> of ${total} · ${n} ${noun}</span>
        <button class="hdr-btn" ${_pageIndex + 1 >= total ? 'disabled' : ''} onclick="goToPage(${_pageIndex + 1})">Next ▸</button>
    `;
}
function goToPage(p) {
    const n = _pageItemCount || _filteredProducts.length;
    const total = Math.ceil(n / _pageSize);
    _pageIndex = Math.max(0, Math.min(p, total - 1));
    renderProducts();
    document.getElementById('productArea').scrollTop = 0;
}

// ── Cart ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Sync a product tile's UI state to the current cart. Called whenever
// the cart changes for that product (addToCart, setCartQty,
// removeFromCart). Updates two things:
//   - `data-in-cart` on the Add button (used by the old morph-badge
//     CSS; harmless on the new vertical stepper layout)
//   - the qty stepper input value (the new mobile pattern — input
//     reflects cart qty live)
// Skips the input if it's currently focused so we don't fight the
// user mid-edit.
function updateProductInCartBadge(productId) {
    const inCart = _cart.get(productId);
    const tileSel = '.product-tile[data-pid="' + productId + '"]';
    document.querySelectorAll(tileSel + ' [data-add]').forEach(btn => {
        if (inCart && inCart.qty > 0) btn.setAttribute('data-in-cart', String(inCart.qty));
        else btn.removeAttribute('data-in-cart');
    });
    document.querySelectorAll(tileSel + ' .qty-stepper input').forEach(input => {
        if (document.activeElement === input) return;
        const cartQty = inCart ? inCart.qty : 0;
        // Desktop default: show 1 (the "to-add" amount). Mobile
        // default: show cart qty (0 if not added). isMobileViewport()
        // distinguishes; if undefined just fall back to cart qty.
        const isMobile = (typeof isMobileViewport === 'function') && isMobileViewport();
        input.value = cartQty || (isMobile ? 0 : 1);
    });
}

function addToCart(product, qty) {
    // No customer gate — building a quick quote at base/list prices is
    // a valid workflow ("client on the phone, what would X cost?").
    // Submission still requires a customer (enforced in createSalesOrder);
    // when one is picked later, selectCustomer() re-resolves every cart
    // line's price against that customer's rules.
    const existing = _cart.get(product.id);
    const newQty = existing ? existing.qty + qty : qty;
    // Preserve a manual price override when topping up an existing line —
    // only recompute from rules when there's no override. setCartQty does
    // the same check; this path was clobbering it before.
    let resolved;
    let priceOverride = false;
    if (existing && existing.priceOverride) {
        resolved = existing.resolved;
        priceOverride = true;
    } else {
        resolved = resolvePrice(product, newQty);
    }
    _cart.set(product.id, { qty: newQty, product, resolved, priceOverride });
    showToast(`✓ Added ${qty} × ${product.num}`, 'success', 1800);
    renderCart();
    updateProductInCartBadge(product.id);
    renderStatusLine();
}

function setCartQty(productId, qty) {
    const line = _cart.get(productId);
    if (!line) return;
    if (qty <= 0) {
        _cart.delete(productId);
    } else {
        line.qty = qty;
        // Honour a manual price override — don't re-run the pricing-rule
        // resolver when the rep has typed a custom unit price. Only the
        // qty (and therefore the line total) updates.
        if (!line.priceOverride) {
            line.resolved = resolvePrice(line.product, qty);
        }
    }
    renderCart();
    updateProductInCartBadge(productId);
    renderStatusLine();
}

// Stamp a manual price onto a cart line. Marks the line as overridden so
// future qty changes don't blow the price away. Pass `null` to clear the
// override and snap back to the calculated price.
function setCartPrice(productId, price) {
    const line = _cart.get(productId);
    if (!line) return;
    if (price == null || isNaN(price)) {
        line.priceOverride = false;
        line.resolved = resolvePrice(line.product, line.qty);
    } else {
        line.priceOverride = true;
        if (!line.resolved) line.resolved = resolvePrice(line.product, line.qty);
        line.resolved = { ...line.resolved, price: roundCents(price) };
    }
    renderCart();
    renderStatusLine();
}

function removeFromCart(productId) {
    _cart.delete(productId);
    renderCart();
    updateProductInCartBadge(productId);
    renderStatusLine();
}

// Reorder a cart line. `fromPid` moves to the slot before `beforePid`
// (or to the end if `beforePid` is null). Map preserves insertion order,
// so we rebuild the Map with entries in the new sequence — the order
// flows through to buildImportPayload's itemValueRows verbatim.
function moveCartLine(fromPid, beforePid) {
    if (fromPid === beforePid) return;
    const entries = [..._cart.entries()];
    const idx = entries.findIndex(([k]) => k === fromPid);
    if (idx < 0) return;
    const [moved] = entries.splice(idx, 1);
    if (beforePid == null) {
        entries.push(moved);
    } else {
        const target = entries.findIndex(([k]) => k === beforePid);
        if (target < 0) entries.push(moved);
        else entries.splice(target, 0, moved);
    }
    _cart = new Map(entries);
    renderCart();
}

async function clearCart() {
    if (_cart.size === 0) return;
    const lines = _cart.size;
    const ok = await showConfirm({
        title: 'Empty the cart?',
        body: `<p>This will remove <strong>${lines}</strong> line${lines === 1 ? '' : 's'} from the cart. This can't be undone.</p>`,
        okLabel: 'Empty cart',
        danger: true,
    });
    if (!ok) return;
    _cart.clear();
    renderCart();
    renderStatusLine();
}

function cartSubtotal() {
    let total = 0;
    for (const line of _cart.values()) {
        total += (line.resolved?.price ?? line.product.price) * line.qty;
    }
    return roundCents(total);
}

// Sum of (line extended × tax rate) for taxable lines only. The
// per-product tax rate (decimal fraction, e.g. 0.08 = 8%) is loaded
// in loadProducts via JOIN taxrate. Non-taxable products or products
// with no tax row contribute zero. Fishbowl recomputes server-side on
// import, so small rounding differences are expected.
// Tax code label shown on a cart line's blue pill. Customer's default
// tax rate wins when configured — every taxable line then shares that
// code. Otherwise falls back to the product's own taxrate.code. Empty
// string when the product isn't taxable (caller should suppress the pill).
function taxCodeForLine(product) {
    if (!product) return '';
    // Treat the line as taxable if EITHER taxableFlag is set OR a tax
    // rate is configured at all (some product records have taxid set
    // without the bit flag — Fishbowl will still apply tax in that
    // case, so the rep needs to see the pill).
    const looksTaxable = bitTrue(product.taxableFlag)
                      || !!product.taxCode || !!product.taxRateName;
    if (!looksTaxable) return '';
    // Customer-default tax wins when populated. Empty code+name on the
    // customer falls through to the product's own (avoids "I see no
    // pill because the customer's rate row has only an id, no code").
    if (_selectedCustomer && _selectedCustomer.taxRateId) {
        const c = _selectedCustomer.taxRateCode || _selectedCustomer.taxRateName;
        if (c) return c;
    }
    // Product's own code, then name.
    const own = product.taxCode || product.taxRateName;
    if (own) return own;
    // UOM-group fallback. When a part has multiple UOM variants
    // (ea / box / case), Fishbowl sometimes has the tax rate set on
    // one variant and not the others — picking a variant whose taxid
    // isn't set otherwise drops the pill. Borrow from a sibling that
    // does have it configured so the rep still sees the correct code.
    if (product.partId != null) {
        const sibIds = _partGroups.get(product.partId) || [];
        for (const sid of sibIds) {
            if (sid === product.id) continue;
            const s = _allProducts.find(x => x.id === sid);
            if (!s) continue;
            const sc = s.taxCode || s.taxRateName;
            if (sc) return sc;
        }
    }
    return '';
}

function cartTax() {
    let tax = 0;
    // If the customer has a default tax rate, it applies to EVERY taxable
    // line — overrides the per-product rate. Mirrors how Fishbowl uses
    // the SO header tax rate when no per-line TaxCode is supplied.
    const custRate = _selectedCustomer && _selectedCustomer.taxRateId
        ? (parseFloat(_selectedCustomer.taxRateRate) || 0)
        : null;
    for (const line of _cart.values()) {
        const p = line.product;
        // "Looks taxable" — same criteria as taxCodeForLine() so the
        // pill and the total stay in sync. Lines have been seen in the
        // wild where the product carries a taxid (and shows a code) but
        // the bit flag is unset; strict `bitTrue(p.taxableFlag)` was
        // skipping those lines and the total ran 10× short.
        const looksTaxable = bitTrue(p.taxableFlag)
                          || !!p.taxCode || !!p.taxRateName;
        if (!looksTaxable) continue;
        // Resolve the effective rate against the same fallback chain as
        // taxCodeForLine: customer default → product's own → sibling UOM
        // variant in the part group. taxrate.rate is stored as a decimal
        // fraction by Fishbowl (0.10 = 10%), so no /100 conversion.
        let rate = custRate;
        if (rate == null) {
            rate = parseFloat(p.taxRate) || 0;
            if (rate <= 0 && p.partId != null) {
                const sibIds = _partGroups.get(p.partId) || [];
                for (const sid of sibIds) {
                    if (sid === p.id) continue;
                    const s = _allProducts.find(x => x.id === sid);
                    if (s && parseFloat(s.taxRate) > 0) { rate = parseFloat(s.taxRate); break; }
                }
            }
        }
        if (rate <= 0) continue;
        const ext = (line.resolved?.price ?? p.price ?? 0) * line.qty;
        tax += ext * rate;
    }
    return roundCents(tax);
}

// ── Barcode scan (placeholder) ────────────────────────────────────
// Phone-only: tap the scan icon in the search bar. Future work could
// wire this up to the BarcodeDetector API (Chrome on Android) or a
// JS scanner library like quagga2 for iOS support. For now, focus
// the search input + nudge the user to type.
function openBarcodeScan() {
    showToast('Barcode scanning is coming soon — type the SKU or UPC for now', 'info', 4000);
    const input = document.getElementById('searchInput');
    if (input) { input.focus(); input.select(); }
}

// ── Swipe-to-delete (phone-only) ───────────────────────────────────
// Attached to each cart line on mobile. Horizontal drag past the
// threshold deletes the line; shorter drag springs back. Vertical
// drag is allowed to scroll the cart list (touch-action: pan-y in
// CSS handles that). One handler per line; cheap enough.
function attachSwipeToDelete(lineEl, productId) {
    if (!isMobileViewport()) return;
    const THRESHOLD = 100;       // px — release past this to delete
    let startX = 0, startY = 0, currentX = 0;
    let active = false, decided = false;

    lineEl.addEventListener('touchstart', e => {
        if (e.touches.length !== 1) return;
        startX = e.touches[0].clientX;
        startY = e.touches[0].clientY;
        currentX = 0;
        active = true; decided = false;
        lineEl.style.transition = 'none';
    }, { passive: true });

    lineEl.addEventListener('touchmove', e => {
        if (!active) return;
        const dx = e.touches[0].clientX - startX;
        const dy = e.touches[0].clientY - startY;
        if (!decided) {
            // Wait until the user's intent is clear — > 10px in either
            // axis. If vertical wins, bail and let the list scroll.
            if (Math.abs(dx) < 8 && Math.abs(dy) < 8) return;
            decided = true;
            if (Math.abs(dy) > Math.abs(dx)) { active = false; return; }
        }
        // Horizontal drag — only allow leftward. e.preventDefault is
        // needed once we know we're handling this gesture so the page
        // doesn't try to scroll horizontally too.
        if (e.cancelable) e.preventDefault();
        currentX = Math.min(0, dx);
        lineEl.style.transform = 'translateX(' + currentX + 'px)';
        lineEl.classList.toggle('swiping', Math.abs(currentX) > 24);
    }, { passive: false });

    function release() {
        if (!active) return;
        active = false;
        lineEl.style.transition = 'transform 0.18s ease-out';
        if (Math.abs(currentX) > THRESHOLD) {
            // Past threshold — animate off-screen then delete.
            lineEl.style.transform = 'translateX(-110%)';
            setTimeout(() => removeFromCart(productId), 180);
        } else {
            // Spring back.
            lineEl.style.transform = 'translateX(0)';
            lineEl.classList.remove('swiping');
        }
    }
    lineEl.addEventListener('touchend',    release, { passive: true });
    lineEl.addEventListener('touchcancel', release, { passive: true });
}

// ── Mobile cart drawer (tier 1 responsive) ────────────────────────
// On desktop (≥ 1024px) the cart panel is always visible — these
// helpers are no-ops. On phone / tablet portrait the panel renders as
// a slide-out drawer; open/close toggles a body class that the CSS
// uses to translate the panel and fade the backdrop in.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Touch layout: detection + the tablet override
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Two media queries, mirrored by the tier-1 CSS block:
//   AUTO    — narrow viewport OR a touch-first device up to tablet size.
//   DESKTOP — width only, i.e. the pre-tablet-detection behaviour.
// See the comment on that CSS block for why width alone is not enough.
const MQ_LAYOUT_AUTO    = '(max-width: 1023px), (pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 1366px)';
const MQ_LAYOUT_DESKTOP = '(max-width: 1023px)';

// 'auto' | 'desktop'. Deliberately only two states, both of which resolve
// identically on a mouse-driven machine — the setting rides in the shared
// per-user state blob, so a tablet must not be able to push a touch layout
// onto the same user's laptop.
let _layoutPref = 'auto';

function layoutMQ() { return _layoutPref === 'desktop' ? MQ_LAYOUT_DESKTOP : MQ_LAYOUT_AUTO; }

function isMobileViewport() {
    try { return window.matchMedia(layoutMQ()).matches; }
    catch (_) { return window.innerWidth < 1024; }
}

// Mirrors the tier-2 CSS query — genuinely phone-sized, where a multi-column
// table cannot fit at any column width.
//
// Distinct from isMobileViewport() on purpose. That one answers "should this
// behave for touch", which is true of a tablet; this one answers "is a table
// impossible here", which is not. Conflating them cost tablets the tile/list
// toggle: a 1180px iPad was coerced to tiles with the toggle hidden, despite
// having more width than plenty of laptops.
//
// Deliberately NOT routed through layoutMQ() — the desktop override must not
// be able to claim a phone is wide enough for a table.
const MQ_PHONE = '(max-width: 639px), (max-width: 932px) and (orientation: landscape)';
function isPhoneViewport() {
    try { return window.matchMedia(MQ_PHONE).matches; }
    catch (_) { return window.innerWidth < 640; }
}

// True on a touch-first device big enough that either layout is defensible —
// i.e. a tablet. Uses screen (not viewport) size so rotating does not make the
// button appear and disappear. Phones are excluded: the widest is ~956px, so
// the touch layout is never in question there and the button would be clutter.
function isTabletDevice() {
    try {
        if (!window.matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches) return false;
        const longEdge = Math.max(window.screen?.width || 0, window.screen?.height || 0);
        return longEdge >= 1024;
    } catch (_) { return false; }
}

// The tier-1 CSS block is ~450 rules deep; a body class cannot un-apply it
// without duplicating all of them. Editing the CSSMediaRule's mediaText
// through the CSSOM re-evaluates the whole block in one step instead.
let _layoutMediaRule = null;
function layoutMediaRule() {
    if (_layoutMediaRule) return _layoutMediaRule;
    try {
        for (const sheet of document.styleSheets) {
            let rules;
            try { rules = sheet.cssRules; } catch (_) { continue; }  // cross-origin sheet
            for (const r of rules) {
                if (r.type === CSSRule.MEDIA_RULE && /pointer:\s*coarse/.test(r.media.mediaText)) {
                    _layoutMediaRule = r;
                    return r;
                }
            }
        }
    } catch (_) {}
    return null;
}

// Re-registered on every pref change: the listener has to watch whichever
// query is currently live, or a rotate/resize under the override is missed.
let _layoutMql = null;
function watchLayoutMQ() {
    try {
        if (_layoutMql && _layoutMql.removeEventListener) {
            _layoutMql.removeEventListener('change', onLayoutMQChange);
        }
        _layoutMql = window.matchMedia(layoutMQ());
        _layoutMql.addEventListener('change', onLayoutMQChange);
    } catch (_) {}
}
function onLayoutMQChange() {
    if (_appView === 'orders') renderOrders();
}

function applyLayoutPref() {
    const rule = layoutMediaRule();
    if (rule) {
        try { rule.media.mediaText = layoutMQ(); } catch (_) {}
    }
    document.body.classList.toggle('layout-forced-desktop', _layoutPref === 'desktop');
    const wrap = document.getElementById('layoutToggleWrap');
    if (wrap) wrap.style.display = isTabletDevice() ? '' : 'none';
    const btn = document.getElementById('layoutToggleBtn');
    if (btn) {
        const toTouch = _layoutPref === 'desktop';
        btn.title = toTouch ? 'Switch to the touch layout' : 'Switch to the full desktop layout';
        btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', toTouch ? 'true' : 'false');
        const lbl = btn.querySelector('.lbl');
        if (lbl) lbl.textContent = toTouch ? 'Touch' : 'Desktop';
    }
    watchLayoutMQ();
}

// Header button. setViewMode() re-runs because the tile coercion is keyed off
// isMobileViewport(); renderOrders() because the table/card choice is too.
function toggleLayoutPref() {
    _layoutPref = _layoutPref === 'desktop' ? 'auto' : 'desktop';
    applyLayoutPref();
    saveState();
    setViewMode(_viewMode);
    if (_appView === 'orders') renderOrders();
    showToast(_layoutPref === 'desktop' ? 'Desktop layout' : 'Touch layout');
}
function openCartDrawer()  { document.body.classList.add('cart-drawer-open'); }
function closeCartDrawer() { document.body.classList.remove('cart-drawer-open'); }

// Update the floating cart pill's count + subtotal. Cheap; called from
// renderCart() so the pill stays in sync with the drawer contents
// without the user having to open the drawer.
function updateCartFab() {
    const fab     = document.getElementById('cartFab');
    const countEl = document.getElementById('cartFabCount');
    const labelEl = document.getElementById('cartFabLabel');
    const totalEl = document.getElementById('cartFabTotal');
    if (!fab || !countEl || !labelEl || !totalEl) return;
    const count = _cart.size;
    const total = cartSubtotal() + cartTax();
    countEl.textContent = String(count);
    if (count === 0) {
        fab.classList.add('empty');
        fab.disabled = true;
        labelEl.textContent = 'Cart is empty';
        totalEl.textContent = '';
    } else {
        fab.classList.remove('empty');
        fab.disabled = false;
        labelEl.textContent = 'View cart';
        totalEl.textContent = fmtMoney(total);
    }
}

// Escape closes the drawer (only relevant on mobile but harmless on
// desktop — body class is set/cleared regardless).
window.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if (e.key === 'Escape' && document.body.classList.contains('cart-drawer-open')) {
        closeCartDrawer();
    }
});

function renderCart() {
    const list = document.getElementById('cartList');
    const totals = document.getElementById('cartTotals');
    const header = document.getElementById('cartHeaderTitle');
    const createBtn = document.getElementById('createSoBtn');
    const clearBtn = document.getElementById('clearCartBtn');

    header.textContent = `Cart (${_cart.size})`;
    clearBtn.disabled = _cart.size === 0;
    updateCartFab();

    if (_cart.size === 0) {
        list.innerHTML = `<div class="cart-empty">Add products to start a quote.${_selectedCustomer ? '' : ' Pick a customer when ready to apply pricing.'}</div>`;
        // Reset totals to zero but keep the row visible — it stays anchored
        // at the bottom so the layout doesn't shift when items are added.
        document.getElementById('cartSubtotal').textContent = fmtMoney(0);
        document.getElementById('cartTotal').textContent = fmtMoney(0);
        document.getElementById('cartTax').textContent = '—';
        createBtn.disabled = true;
        return;
    }

    let html = '';
    for (const [pid, line] of _cart) {
        const p = line.product;
        const lineTotal = (line.resolved?.price || 0) * line.qty;
        html += `
            <div class="cart-line" data-pid="${pid}">
                <div class="drag-handle" data-drag-handle title="Drag to reorder">
                    <svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 12 12" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">
                        <rect y="1" width="12" height="1.5" rx="0.75"/>
                        <rect y="5.25" width="12" height="1.5" rx="0.75"/>
                        <rect y="9.5" width="12" height="1.5" rx="0.75"/>
                    </svg>
                </div>
                <div class="info">
                    <div class="num">${escapeHtml(p.num)} · ${escapeHtml((p.description || '').slice(0, 40))}</div>
                    <div class="sub-row">
                        <div class="qty-stepper">
                            <button data-step="-1">−</button>
                            <input type="number" min="1" value="${line.qty}">
                            <button data-step="1">+</button>
                        </div>
                        <span>@</span>
                        <input type="number" class="price-input${line.priceOverride ? ' overridden' : ''}"
                               data-price-pid="${pid}" min="0" step="0.01"
                               value="${(line.resolved?.price || 0).toFixed(2)}"
                               title="${line.priceOverride ? 'Manual override — click to edit' : 'Click to override the calculated price'}">
                        ${line.priceOverride ? `<button type="button" class="price-reset" data-reset-pid="${pid}" title="Reset to calculated price">
                            <svg fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.2" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true">
                                <path d="M9 14L4 9l5-5"/>
                                <path d="M4 9h11a5 5 0 0 1 5 5v1a5 5 0 0 1-5 5h-4"/>
                            </svg>
                        </button>` : ''}
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="line-total-wrap">
                    <div class="line-total">${fmtMoney(lineTotal)}</div>
                    ${taxCodeForLine(p) ? `<span class="tax-pill" title="Tax code applied to this line">${escapeHtml(taxCodeForLine(p))}</span>` : ''}
                </div>
                <button class="remove-btn" title="Remove">×</button>
            </div>
        `;
    }
    list.innerHTML = html;

    // Wire up qty steppers + remove buttons. Same event matrix as the
    // product card: debounced input (300ms), immediate change/blur,
    // explicit Enter handler. The debounced setCartQty re-resolves the
    // line's price, so a qty crossing a rule boundary updates the cart
    // total even while the user is still typing.
    // Track which line is being dragged for the row-level drop handler.
    let _dragPid = null;
    list.querySelectorAll('.cart-line').forEach(row => {
        const pid = parseInt(row.dataset.pid, 10);
        const input = row.querySelector('input');

        // Swipe-to-delete (no-op on desktop).
        attachSwipeToDelete(row, pid);

        // Drag-to-reorder. The whole row is draggable but only initiates
        // when the user grabs the .drag-handle — otherwise clicks on the
        // qty/price inputs would also begin a drag. We toggle draggable
        // on mousedown/up over the handle.
        const handle = row.querySelector('[data-drag-handle]');
        if (handle) {
            handle.addEventListener('mousedown', () => { row.draggable = true; });
            handle.addEventListener('mouseup',   () => { row.draggable = false; });
        }
        row.addEventListener('dragstart', e => {
            _dragPid = pid;
            row.classList.add('dragging');
            e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
            // Firefox requires some payload to start a drag.
            try { e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', String(pid)); } catch (_) {}
        });
        const clearDropIndicators = () => {
            list.querySelectorAll('.cart-line').forEach(r => {
                r.classList.remove('drag-over-top', 'drag-over-bottom');
            });
        };
        row.addEventListener('dragend', () => {
            _dragPid = null;
            row.draggable = false;
            row.classList.remove('dragging');
            clearDropIndicators();
        });
        row.addEventListener('dragover', e => {
            if (_dragPid == null || _dragPid === pid) return;
            e.preventDefault();
            e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'move';
            // Cursor in upper half → drop ABOVE target; lower half → BELOW.
            const rect = row.getBoundingClientRect();
            const after = (e.clientY - rect.top) > rect.height / 2;
            row._dropAfter = after;
            clearDropIndicators();
            row.classList.add(after ? 'drag-over-bottom' : 'drag-over-top');
        });
        row.addEventListener('dragleave', e => {
            // Only clear when leaving the row entirely (relatedTarget outside row).
            // Without this, moving within the row's children flickers the indicator.
            if (!row.contains(e.relatedTarget)) {
                row.classList.remove('drag-over-top', 'drag-over-bottom');
            }
        });
        row.addEventListener('drop', e => {
            e.preventDefault();
            const after = row._dropAfter;
            clearDropIndicators();
            if (_dragPid != null && _dragPid !== pid) {
                if (after) {
                    // Insert AFTER pid → before the next pid in current order,
                    // or push to end if pid is the last line.
                    const ids = [..._cart.keys()];
                    const i = ids.indexOf(pid);
                    const nextPid = (i >= 0 && i < ids.length - 1) ? ids[i + 1] : null;
                    moveCartLine(_dragPid, nextPid);
                } else {
                    moveCartLine(_dragPid, pid);
                }
            }
            _dragPid = null;
        });
        const commit = () => setCartQty(pid, Math.max(1, parseInt(input.value, 10) || 1));
        const debouncedCommit = debounce(commit, 300);
        row.querySelector('[data-step="-1"]').addEventListener('click', () => setCartQty(pid, Math.max(1, (parseInt(input.value, 10) || 1) - 1)));
        row.querySelector('[data-step="1"]') .addEventListener('click', () => setCartQty(pid, (parseInt(input.value, 10) || 1) + 1));
        input.addEventListener('input',  debouncedCommit);
        input.addEventListener('change', commit);
        input.addEventListener('blur',   commit);
        input.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
            if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); commit(); }
        });
        input.addEventListener('focus', e => e.target.select());
        row.querySelector('.remove-btn').addEventListener('click', () => removeFromCart(pid));

        // Manual price override — commit on change/blur/Enter. Empty
        // value clears the override and snaps back to the calculated price.
        const priceInput = row.querySelector('.price-input[data-price-pid]');
        if (priceInput) {
            const commitPrice = () => {
                const raw = priceInput.value.trim();
                if (raw === '') { setCartPrice(pid, null); return; }
                const n = parseFloat(raw);
                if (isNaN(n) || n < 0) { setCartPrice(pid, null); return; }
                setCartPrice(pid, n);
            };
            priceInput.addEventListener('change', commitPrice);
            priceInput.addEventListener('blur',   commitPrice);
            priceInput.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
                if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); commitPrice(); priceInput.blur(); }
                if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); setCartPrice(pid, null); }
            });
            priceInput.addEventListener('focus', e => e.target.select());
        }

        // Reset-to-calculated-price button. Only present when the line
        // currently carries a manual override.
        const resetBtn = row.querySelector('.price-reset[data-reset-pid]');
        if (resetBtn) {
            resetBtn.addEventListener('click', () => setCartPrice(pid, null));
        }
    });

    // Totals
    const subtotal = cartSubtotal();
    const tax = cartTax();
    document.getElementById('cartSubtotal').textContent = fmtMoney(subtotal);
    document.getElementById('cartTax').textContent = tax > 0 ? fmtMoney(tax) : '—';
    document.getElementById('cartTotal').textContent = fmtMoney(subtotal + tax);

    const hasAddresses = _selectedShipToId != null && _selectedBillToId != null;
    const standaloneLocked = MODE === 'standalone';
    const canSubmit = !!_selectedCustomer && _cart.size > 0 && hasAddresses && !standaloneLocked;
    createBtn.disabled = !canSubmit;
    createBtn.title = standaloneLocked   ? 'SO creation is desktop-only — browse & quote in standalone, submit from the Fishbowl desktop client'
                    : !_selectedCustomer ? 'Select a customer first'
                    : _cart.size === 0   ? 'Add products to the cart first'
                    : !hasAddresses      ? 'Pick a ship-to and bill-to address'
                    : `Create sales order for ${_selectedCustomer.name}`;
}

// ── Sales-order creation via ImportSalesOrder (FALLBACK ROUTE) ───────
// Historically the only route: Fishbowl created SOs via the legacy XML API's
// ImportRequest mechanism, same as the SO module's CSV-import feature.
//
// SUPERSEDED, but still live: POST /api/sales-orders DOES exist on current
// Fishbowl builds (26.6 confirmed). It returns 405 on older ones — which is
// where the "no such endpoint" claim above came from. submitSoCreate() prefers
// REST and falls back to everything below, so this path stays until every
// target server is upgraded. See buildSoRestPayload().
//
// CSV column reference: https://fishbowlhelp.com/files/csv/importSO.html
//   - Each submit is one Flag="SO" header row + N Flag="Item" rows
//   - SONum left blank → Fishbowl auto-numbers
//   - Status: 10=Estimate, 20=Issued, 95=Historical
//   - Addresses (BillTo + ShipTo) are REQUIRED — that's why the cart
//     panel renders the ship-to / bill-to selectors below the lines
//
// Wire pattern (from PPP_Pricing_Validator.htm L2871, the canonical example):
//   runApiRequest('ImportRq', JSON.stringify({ImportRq:{Type, Rows:{Row:[…]}}}))

// CSV field escaper. Always quotes; escapes embedded quotes by doubling
// them. Always emits empty fields as "" (safer for the import parser than
// bare commas). Null/undefined → empty string.
//
// Newlines are stripped by csvSafe BEFORE quoting — see its note. This
// matters here as well as on the customer import: the order Note is a
// textarea, so a multi-line note would otherwise tear the SO row in half
// when submitSoImport joins the rows with '\n'.
function csvField(v) {
    if (v == null) return '""';
    return '"' + csvSafe(v).replace(/"/g, '""') + '"';
}

// Format today (or any date) in the FB-configured short format. Used
// for the SO header's Date and OrderDateScheduled columns.
function todayShort() { return moment().format(MOMENT_FMT); }

// Build the ImportSalesOrder payload — the {ImportRq:{Type,Rows:{Row:[…]}}}
// object passed straight to runApiRequest. Returns null if the cart or
// addresses aren't ready (caller surfaces a toast).
function buildImportPayload(statusOverride) {
    if (!_selectedCustomer || _cart.size === 0) return null;
    const ship = _customerAddresses.find(a => a.id === _selectedShipToId);
    const bill = _customerAddresses.find(a => a.id === _selectedBillToId);
    if (!ship || !bill) return null;

    const cust = _selectedCustomer;
    // statusOverride lets the confirm dialog pick Estimate/Issued per-order
    // without changing the saved default.
    const effectiveStatus = statusOverride != null ? parseInt(statusOverride, 10) : _defaultStatusId;
    const status = effectiveStatus === 20 ? 20 : 10;  // Issued vs Estimate
    const today  = todayShort();
    // TaxRateName: send empty when the customer has no default — an
    // empty field tells Fishbowl to apply its own server-side default.
    const taxRateName = cust.taxRateName || '';
    // CarrierName: order-level override → customer default → company
    // default. The company fallback exists because sending an empty
    // CarrierName triggers "Unknown Carrier on line number 3" on some
    // installs; the company default is what the desktop SO module
    // would have used anyway.
    const carrierName = effectiveCarrierName(cust);
    // Customer PO + scheduled date come from the SO-details drawer.
    const customerPo = _orderCustomerPO || '';
    // Convert the date input's YYYY-MM-DD value to the install's
    // configured DateFormatShort (Fishbowl's ImportSalesOrder CSV
    // expects dates in that format). Empty string when no date was
    // picked, in which case the OrderDateScheduled column falls back
    // to today (the prior behaviour).
    const scheduledDate = _orderDateScheduled
        ? moment(_orderDateScheduled, 'YYYY-MM-DD').format(MOMENT_FMT)
        : today;

    // Column lists — kept as named arrays so the header rows we emit
    // stay in sync with the data rows. Order matches the canonical CSV
    // export (verified against an actual SO export from this install,
    // not just the published doc which omits TotalIncludesTax).
    const SO_COLS = [
        'Flag','SONum','Status','CustomerName','CustomerContact',
        'BillToName','BillToAddress','BillToCity','BillToState','BillToZip','BillToCountry',
        'ShipToName','ShipToAddress','ShipToCity','ShipToState','ShipToZip','ShipToCountry',
        'ShipToResidential','CarrierName','TaxRateName','PriorityId','TotalIncludesTax',
        'PONum','VendorPONum','Date','Salesman','ShippingTerms','PaymentTerms','FOB','Note',
        'QuickBooksClassName','LocationGroupName','OrderDateScheduled','URL','CarrierService',
        'CurrencyName','CurrencyRate','PriceIsHomeCurrency','DateExpired','Phone','Email','Category',
    ];
    const ITEM_COLS = [
        'Flag','SOItemTypeID','ProductNumber','ProductDescription','ProductQuantity',
        'UOM','ProductPrice','Taxable','TaxCode','Note','ItemQuickBooksClassName',
        'ItemDateScheduled','ShowItem','KitItem','RevisionLevel','CustomerPartNumber',
    ];

    const soValues = [
        'SO',                                  // Flag
        '',                                    // SONum (blank = auto)
        status,                                // Status (numeric)
        cust.name,                             // CustomerName
        ship.recipient || cust.name,           // CustomerContact
        bill.recipient || cust.name,           // BillToName
        bill.street, bill.city, bill.state, bill.zip, bill.country,
        ship.recipient || cust.name,           // ShipToName
        ship.street, ship.city, ship.state, ship.zip, ship.country,
        ship.residential ? 'true' : 'false',   // ShipToResidential
        carrierName,                           // CarrierName
        taxRateName,                           // TaxRateName
        cust.priorityId || 30,                 // PriorityId (30 = Normal)
        'false',                               // TotalIncludesTax — tax computed on top of unit price
        customerPo,                            // PONum — from SO-details drawer
        '',                                    // VendorPONum
        today,                                 // Date
        cust.salesmanName || '',               // Salesman
        cust.shipTermsName || '',              // ShippingTerms
        cust.paymentTermsName || '',           // PaymentTerms
        '',                                    // FOB
        _orderNote || '',                      // Note — from SO-details drawer (order-level free text)
        '',                                    // QuickBooksClassName
        _despatchLg ? _despatchLg.name : '',   // LocationGroupName — from Despatch LG selector
        scheduledDate,                         // OrderDateScheduled — from SO-details drawer (falls back to today)
        '',                                    // URL
        '',                                    // CarrierService
        '',                                    // CurrencyName
        '',                                    // CurrencyRate
        'true',                                // PriceIsHomeCurrency
        '',                                    // DateExpired
        '',                                    // Phone
        '',                                    // Email
        '',                                    // Category
    ];

    // Per-line TaxCode. The rule:
    //   customer HAS a tax rate  → that code applies to EVERY line
    //   customer has NONE        → each line carries the product's own code
    //
    // The header TaxRateName is NOT a fallback for the lines. This used to
    // blank the column whenever the customer had a default rate, on the
    // assumption that the header cascaded down — it does not. A blank
    // TaxCode parks the line on taxrate id 1 (None); it inherits nothing.
    // Verified on demodb: SO 437 carries header "GST on Income" @10% over a
    // 4.75 subtotal and posts totalTax 0.00, with every soitem.taxId = 1.
    // Same on 438/441/457. The controlled 458/459/460 triple (same product,
    // minutes apart) isolates it — setting the header rate was the only
    // change, and it was the one that flipped the lines to None.
    //
    // The importer resolves this column against taxrate.CODE — the SO lines
    // that did come through correctly landed on the ids whose code matched
    // what was sent — so send the code, never the name (name is only a
    // last-ditch fallback for a rate with no code set).
    //
    // Caveat that this route cannot fix: taxrate.code is not unique (demodb
    // has NCG on ids 4 and 13, NCF on 5 and 8, the duplicates being inactive
    // legacy rows), so an install with duplicate codes can resolve to the
    // wrong rate.
    //
    // FIXED on the REST route, which is now preferred — buildSoRestPayload()
    // sends no tax code at all and lets the server apply the customer's own
    // rate by id, so there is no string left to resolve ambiguously. This
    // caveat applies only when falling back to the CSV importer.
    const customerTaxCode = cust.taxRateId
        ? (cust.taxRateCode || cust.taxRateName || '')
        : '';
    const itemValueRows = [..._cart.entries()].map(([pid, line]) => {
        const p = line.product;
        const unitPrice = line.resolved?.price ?? p.price ?? 0;
        return [
            'Item',                            // Flag
            10,                                // SOItemTypeID (10 = Sale)
            p.num,                             // ProductNumber
            p.description || '',               // ProductDescription
            line.qty,                          // ProductQuantity
            p.uomCode || 'ea',                 // UOM
            unitPrice,                         // ProductPrice
            p.taxableFlag ? 'true' : 'false',  // Taxable
            customerTaxCode || p.taxCode || '',  // TaxCode — customer's rate wins, else the product's
            '',                                // Note
            '',                                // ItemQuickBooksClassName
            '',                                // ItemDateScheduled
            'true',                            // ShowItem
            '',                                // KitItem
            '',                                // RevisionLevel
            '',                                // CustomerPartNumber
        ];
    });

    const enc = arr => arr.map(csvField).join(',');
    return {
        ImportRq: {
            Type: 'ImportSalesOrder',
            // Fishbowl's SO import expects two header rows (one per row
            // type) before the data rows — matches the format Fishbowl
            // itself exports via File → Export.
            Rows: { Row: [
                enc(SO_COLS),
                enc(ITEM_COLS),
                enc(soValues),
                ...itemValueRows.map(enc),
            ]},
        },
    };
}

// ── Native REST create — POST /api/sales-orders ──────────────────────
//
// Preferred over the CSV import above, which has two defects it cannot fix:
//   * taxrate.code is not unique (this install has NCG on ids 4 and 13, NCF
//     on 5 and 8), so code-based tax resolution can pick the wrong rate;
//   * the response echoes nothing, so the new SO number had to be GUESSED
//     with "SELECT num FROM so ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1" — a race.
// REST identifies everything by id and returns the created order.
//
// NOT universally available: this server build registers only GET on
// /api/sales-orders and answers POST with 405. submitSoCreate() probes once
// per session and falls back to the CSV path, which is why buildImportPayload
// above is still live code rather than history.

// soitemtype ids (verified against the soitemtype lookup table).
const SOITEM_TYPE_SALE      = 10;
const SOITEM_TYPE_DROP_SHIP = 12;
const SOITEM_TYPE_KIT       = 80;

// REST wants the country ABBREVIATION where the CSV wanted the name, so this
// prefers countryAbbrev and only falls back to the full name.
function addrForRest(a, cust) {
    return {
        name:       a.recipient || (cust && cust.name) || '',
        street:     a.street || '',
        city:       a.city || '',
        state:      a.state || '',              // already stateconst.code
        postalCode: a.zip || '',
        country:    a.countryAbbrev || a.country || '',
    };
}

// Cart lines the REST create cannot accept. Kits and drop-ship lines return
// 422, so they are screened BEFORE the confirm dialog and routed through the
// CSV importer (which does support them) rather than failing mid-submit with
// a raw server message.
function unsupportedRestLines() {
    return [..._cart.values()].filter(l => {
        const p = l.product || {};
        return p.kitFlag === true
            || p.defaultSoItemType === SOITEM_TYPE_KIT
            || p.defaultSoItemType === SOITEM_TYPE_DROP_SHIP;
    });
}

// Build the JSON body for POST /api/sales-orders. Returns null when the cart
// or addresses aren't ready (same contract as buildImportPayload).
//
// DELIBERATELY SPARSE. Almost everything the 42-column CSV row spells out is
// a server-side default derived from the customer, and echoing those values
// back is how the CSV path acquired its failure modes. Omitted on purpose:
//
//   number         — blank lets Fishbowl auto-number. Never call
//                    GET /api/sales-orders/next-number to fill it: that
//                    endpoint CONSUMES the number even if no order follows.
//   taxRate        — server applies the customer's default (None for
//                    tax-exempt customers). This is what makes the duplicate
//                    taxrate.code bug unreachable: no code string is sent.
//   soItems[].taxRate — each line inherits the order rate. Sending per-line
//                    rates is also rejected outright on US databases when
//                    they differ from the order rate.
//   type, paymentTerms, shipTerms, fobPointName, currency, class,
//   dateCreated    — all default from the customer / today.
//
// opts.omitSalesperson drops salesperson for the 403 retry — see submitSoCreate().
function buildSoRestPayload(statusOverride, opts) {
    if (!_selectedCustomer || _cart.size === 0) return null;
    const ship = _customerAddresses.find(a => a.id === _selectedShipToId);
    const bill = _customerAddresses.find(a => a.id === _selectedBillToId);
    if (!ship || !bill) return null;

    const cust = _selectedCustomer;
    const effectiveStatus = statusOverride != null ? parseInt(statusOverride, 10) : _defaultStatusId;
    const body = {
        status: effectiveStatus === 20 ? 'Issued' : 'Estimate',
        customer: { id: cust.id },
        customerContact: ship.recipient || cust.name,
        shipToAddress: addrForRest(ship, cust),
        billToAddress: addrForRest(bill, cust),
        soItems: [..._cart.entries()].map(([pid, line], i) => ({
            product:    { id: pid },
            type:       { id: SOITEM_TYPE_SALE },
            lineNumber: i + 1,
            // Strings, matching the documented example — these are decimals
            // and JSON numbers would risk float noise on the wire.
            quantity:   String(line.qty),
            unitPrice:  String(line.resolved?.price ?? line.product?.price ?? 0),
        })),
    };

    // The customer's salesman, preserving the CSV's commission attribution.
    // Requires SO_EDIT_SALESPERSON when it isn't the signed-in user; the
    // caller retries without it on a 403 rather than failing the order.
    if (!(opts && opts.omitSalesperson) && cust.salesmanId) {
        body.salesperson = { id: cust.salesmanId };
    }

    const carrierId = effectiveCarrierId(cust);
    if (carrierId)             body.carrier          = { id: carrierId };
    if (_despatchLg && _despatchLg.id) body.locationGroup = { id: _despatchLg.id };
    if (_orderCustomerPO)      body.customerPoNumber = _orderCustomerPO;
    if (_orderNote)            body.note             = _orderNote;
    // Sent as the raw YYYY-MM-DD from the date input — NOT reformatted through
    // MOMENT_FMT the way the CSV needs, because the API takes ISO dates.
    if (_orderDateScheduled)   body.dateScheduled    = _orderDateScheduled;

    return body;
}

// Submit the ImportSalesOrder CSV body to Fishbowl. Three transports
// depending on MODE:
//   fishbowl   → runRestApiAsync if available, else fall back to the
//                legacy runApiRequest('ImportRq', ...) JSON-XML bridge.
//   portal     → fetch through the Cloudflare Worker (Worker injects
//                FB auth; Content-Type stays text/plain).
//   standalone → fetch direct to FB REST API (browser must allow CORS).
//
// Returns { ok: true } on success or throws an Error on failure.
async function submitSoImport(csvBody, payload) {
    // Prefer REST in fishbowl mode if runRestApiAsync is exposed — it's
    // the modern path and matches what the Fishbowl_Advanced_API_Tool
    // uses. Falls through to runApiRequest only when REST isn't bridged.
    if (MODE === 'fishbowl' && typeof runRestApiAsync === 'function') {
        const resp = await runRestApiAsync({
            method: 'POST',
            path:   '/api/import/Sales-Order',
            body:   csvBody,
            contentType: CSV_CONTENT_TYPE,
        });
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('runRestApiAsync /api/import/Sales-Order response: ' + JSON.stringify(resp));
        return { ok: true, resp };
    }
    if (MODE === 'fishbowl' && typeof runApiRequest === 'function') {
        // Legacy bridge — uses the ImportRq JSON envelope, not the REST
        // CSV body. Falls back to the format buildImportPayload built.
        const raw = runApiRequest('ImportRq', JSON.stringify(payload));
        const resp = typeof raw === 'string' ? safeParse(raw) : raw;
        const flat = JSON.stringify(resp || {}).toLowerCase();
        const ok = /statuscode"\s*:\s*"?1000/.test(flat) || /"success"\s*:\s*true/.test(flat);
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('runApiRequest ImportRq response: ' + JSON.stringify(resp));
        if (!ok) throw new Error(extractImportError(resp) || 'Import did not return success status');
        return { ok: true, resp };
    }
    // portal / standalone — POST the raw CSV to /api/import/Sales-Order
    // via fetch.
    //   - portal mode: same-origin POST; Access cookie + Pages Function
    //     handle identity. No Bearer token from JS.
    //   - standalone mode: cross-origin POST with the FB Bearer token.
    if (MODE === 'standalone' && !_conn.token) {
        throw new Error('Not connected — log in via the header Connect button.');
    }
    const url = _conn.baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, '') + '/api/import/Sales-Order';
    const headers = {
        'Content-Type':  CSV_CONTENT_TYPE,
        'Accept':        'application/json, text/plain',
    };
    if (_conn.token) headers.Authorization = 'Bearer ' + _conn.token;
    let res;
    try {
        res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: csvBody });
    } catch (e) {
        // Outright network failure — Pages Function unreachable.
        if (MODE === 'portal') noteServerError();
        throw new Error('Network error submitting SO: ' + (e && e.message || e));
    }
    const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
    if (DEBUG) qoDebug('REST /api/import/Sales-Order ' + res.status + ': ' + text.slice(0, 400));
    if (!res.ok) {
        // 5xx from the proxy = upstream FB is sick. Mark the server
        // unreachable so the user sees the recovery pill and can
        // retry once it clears.
        if (MODE === 'portal' && res.status >= 500) noteServerError();
        // Try to surface the FB error message if the body parses as JSON.
        let detail = text;
        try {
            const j = JSON.parse(text);
            detail = j.detail || j.message || j.error || text;
        } catch (_) {}
        throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status + (detail ? ' — ' + String(detail).slice(0, 400) : ''));
    }
    // Success — clear any prior unreachable banner.
    if (MODE === 'portal') noteServerOk();
    let resp = text;
    try { resp = JSON.parse(text); } catch (_) { /* response may be CSV / empty */ }
    return { ok: true, resp };
}

// POST the JSON body to /api/sales-orders. Same three-transport shape as
// submitSoImport, with two differences:
//
//   * No runApiRequest branch. The legacy bridge speaks only ImportRq CSV
//     envelopes — there is no legacy equivalent of this call, so a host with
//     runApiRequest but no runRestApiAsync is pinned to the CSV route.
//   * The gate is `typeof runRestApiAsync === 'function'` alone. submitSoImport
//     also tests MODE === 'fishbowl', which is redundant: MODE is *defined* as
//     'fishbowl' when that global exists.
//
// Throws on failure with err.status set, which is what submitSoCreate() reads
// to tell "route missing" (404/405) from a real rejection.
async function submitSoRest(body) {
    const json = JSON.stringify(body);
    if (DEBUG) qoDebug('POST /api/sales-orders body: ' + json);

    if (typeof runRestApiAsync === 'function') {
        const resp = await runRestApiAsync({
            method: 'POST',
            path:   '/api/sales-orders',
            body:   json,
            contentType: 'application/json',
        });
        if (DEBUG) qoDebug('runRestApiAsync /api/sales-orders response: ' + JSON.stringify(resp));
        return resp;
    }

    if (MODE === 'standalone' && !_conn.token) {
        throw new Error('Not connected — log in via the header Connect button.');
    }
    const url = _conn.baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, '') + '/api/sales-orders';
    const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Accept': 'application/json' };
    if (_conn.token) headers.Authorization = 'Bearer ' + _conn.token;
    let res;
    try {
        res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: json });
    } catch (e) {
        if (MODE === 'portal') noteServerError();
        throw new Error('Network error creating SO: ' + (e && e.message || e));
    }
    const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
    if (DEBUG) qoDebug('REST /api/sales-orders ' + res.status + ': ' + text.slice(0, 400));
    if (!res.ok) {
        if (MODE === 'portal' && res.status >= 500) noteServerError();
        let detail = text;
        try {
            const j = JSON.parse(text);
            detail = j.detail || j.message || j.error || text;
        } catch (_) {}
        const err = new Error('HTTP ' + res.status + (detail ? ' — ' + String(detail).slice(0, 400) : ''));
        err.status = res.status;
        throw err;
    }
    if (MODE === 'portal') noteServerOk();
    try { return JSON.parse(text); } catch (_) { return text; }
}

// HTTP status out of either rejection shape: runRestApiAsync rejects with
// {message, status}; the fetch branch throws an Error carrying .status. When
// neither is present, fall back to reading the status out of the message —
// the bridge's rejection shape is documentation, not something observed here.
function restErrStatus(err) {
    if (!err) return 0;
    const n = parseInt(err.status, 10);
    if (!isNaN(n)) return n;
    const m = String(err.message || err);
    if (/\b405\b|method not allowed/i.test(m)) return 405;
    if (/\b404\b|not found/i.test(m))          return 404;
    if (/\b403\b|forbidden/i.test(m))          return 403;
    if (/\b422\b/.test(m))                     return 422;
    return 0;
}

// Pull id + number out of the create response. Defensive because the exact
// shape is unverified — it may be the order itself or an envelope, and the
// number field could be number/num/soNumber. Anything not found stays null and
// the caller falls back to the SQL lookup.
function extractCreatedSo(resp) {
    const o = (typeof resp === 'string' ? safeParse(resp) : resp) || {};
    const so = o.salesOrder || o.data || o;
